subject: Physics
question: A proposed relation is v = u + at². Why is it dimensionally invalid?

options.B: at² has dimensions of length, not velocity
options.C: Acceleration cannot be multiplied by time
options.D: Velocity and acceleration have identical dimensions

correct_answer: at² has dimensions of length, not velocity
explanation: In a sum, every term must have the same dimensions. Here at² has dimensions [L], whereas u and v have dimensions [L T⁻¹].
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 1: Physics and Measurement

subject: Physics
question: If the time period T of a simple pendulum depends on length l and gravitational acceleration g, dimensional analysis gives T proportional to:
explanation: Let T ∝ lᵃgᵇ. Equating dimensions gives a = 1/2 and b = -1/2, hence T ∝ √(l/g).
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 1: Physics and Measurement

subject: Physics
question: The dimensions of the universal gravitational constant G are:
explanation: Using F = Gm₁m₂/r² gives [G] = [F r²/M²] = [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²].

subject: Physics
question: For a stretched string, wave speed v depends on tension F and linear density μ. Which relation is dimensionally consistent?

subject: Physics
question: Which relation is dimensionally consistent for the speed v of a wave on a stretched string with tension T and linear mass density μ?

question: Which result cannot be obtained from dimensional analysis alone?

question: For any motion of a particle between two given instants, the correct relation between the path length s and the magnitude of the displacement d is:

options.A: d is less than or equal to s, with equality only for motion along a straight line in one direction
options.B: d is always exactly equal to s for every kind of motion
options.C: d is greater than s when the particle reverses its direction of motion
options.D: d is always greater than s whenever the path is curved

correct_answer: d is less than or equal to s, with equality only for motion along a straight line in one direction
explanation: The displacement is the straight line vector joining the initial and final positions, and the straight line is the shortest route between them. Hence the magnitude of the displacement can never exceed the length of the actual path, and the two are equal only when the particle moves along a straight line without reversing.

question: A particle moves along a curved path in a plane. At any instant the direction of its instantaneous velocity is:

options.A: along the chord joining the initial and final positions
options.B: along the position vector drawn from the origin
options.C: along the normal to the path at that point
options.D: along the tangent to the path at that point

explanation: Instantaneous velocity is the limit of the ratio of a small displacement to a small time interval. As the interval shrinks the chord joining the two positions turns into the tangent, so the instantaneous velocity always points along the tangent to the path.

question: Which statement correctly expresses the independence of perpendicular components in plane motion:

options.A: The motion along x fixes the motion along y through the direction of the resultant acceleration
options.B: Each perpendicular component obeys its own one dimensional equation of motion, with the same value of t appearing in both
options.C: The two components must always be solved together because each has its own value of the time
options.D: Only the resultant equation of motion is valid, so the components have no separate equations of motion

correct_answer: Each perpendicular component obeys its own one dimensional equation of motion, with the same value of t appearing in both
explanation: Because the vector equations of motion hold component wise, the x motion is governed only by the x components of u and a, and the y motion only by their y components. Neither influences the other. The single link is the time t, which is the same for both.

question: The standard treatment of projectile motion in a plane rests on the assumptions that:

options.A: air resistance is neglected and the acceleration due to gravity is constant in magnitude and direction
options.B: both the horizontal and the vertical accelerations are constant and non zero
options.C: the acceleration due to gravity falls off with height while air resistance is neglected
options.D: air resistance is included and the acceleration due to gravity is neglected

correct_answer: air resistance is neglected and the acceleration due to gravity is constant in magnitude and direction
explanation: Elementary projectile theory assumes that the projectile moves close to the earth so that g is constant in magnitude and direction, that air resistance is negligible, and that the range is small enough for the earth to be treated as flat and non rotating. question: A projectile is launched from level ground and lands back on the same level. Comparing the velocity at landing with the velocity at launch,:

options.B: the speeds are equal, and the angle below the horizontal at landing equals the launch angle above it

explanation: Here v_x = 20 cos 30 = 10 √3 m s⁻¹ and v_y = 10 - 10 t. For the velocity to point 30° below the horizontal, v_y must equal -10 √3 tan 30 = -10 m s⁻¹. Solving 10 - 10 t = -10 gives t = 2 s, which is exactly the time of flight, as the symmetry of the parabola requires.

question: For a projectile in flight, the way in which the components of velocity depend on time is best described by saying that:

options.A: the horizontal component stays constant while the vertical component changes linearly with time
options.B: the horizontal component stays constant while the vertical component changes as the square of the time

question: From the top of the same tower one ball is simply dropped and another is thrown horizontally at the same instant. Neglecting air resistance,:

question: Rain is falling vertically downwards. A man runs horizontally along a level road. To keep himself dry he must hold his umbrella tilted:

question: To a man running due east at 3 m s⁻¹, rain appears to fall vertically downwards at 4 m s⁻¹. The actual velocity of the rain is:

options.A: 5 m s⁻¹, at 53° to the vertical, slanting towards the east
options.B: 7 m s⁻¹, at 37° to the vertical, slanting towards the east
options.C: 5 m s⁻¹, at 37° to the vertical, slanting towards the east

correct_answer: 5 m s⁻¹, at 37° to the vertical, slanting towards the east
explanation: The apparent velocity is v_rain - v_man = -4 j m s⁻¹ with east as i. Hence v_rain = -4 j + 3 i m s⁻¹, of magnitude √(9 + 16) = 5 m s⁻¹. The angle with the vertical satisfies tan θ = 3 / 4, so θ is about 37°, the rain slanting towards the east.

subject: Physics
chapter: Motion in a Straight Line and Motion in a Plane
question: For a boat crossing a river whose current is slower than the boat, which comparison of the shortest path crossing with the shortest time crossing is correct:

options.A: The shortest time crossing is impossible whenever the current is slower than the boat
options.B: The two crossings take the same time, since the width of the river is the same
options.C: The shortest path crossing takes more time than the shortest time crossing
options.D: The shortest path crossing takes less time, since the boat travels a shorter distance

correct_answer: The shortest path crossing takes more time than the shortest time crossing
explanation: Heading straight across gives a crossing speed v and time d / v. Landing directly opposite requires part of the boat velocity to cancel the current, leaving only √(v² - u²) across the river, and a time d / √(v² - u²). Since √(v² - u²) is smaller than v, the shortest path route always takes longer.

question: The velocity of a body P relative to a body Q and the velocity of Q relative to P are:

explanation: For a (i + j + k): a² (1 + 1 + 1) = 1, so 3 a² = 1 and a = 1 / √(3). For b (i - j): b² (1 + 1) = 1, so 2 b² = 1 and b = 1 / √(2). Hence a / b = √(2) / √(3) = √(2 / 3), which is about 0.816.

question: Which statement about the null vector is correct?

options.A: Its magnitude is zero and its direction is indeterminate
options.B: Its magnitude is zero and it can never be written as the sum of two non zero vectors
options.C: Its magnitude is one and its direction is indeterminate
options.D: Its magnitude is zero and its direction is always along the x axis

correct_answer: Its magnitude is zero and its direction is indeterminate
explanation: A null vector is an arrow of zero length, so no direction can be assigned to it. It arises whenever a vector is added to its own negative, or when a closed polygon of vectors is traversed once completely.

question: Two vectors are said to be equal if:

options.A: they have the same magnitude and the same direction
options.B: they act at the same point of the body
options.C: they have the same direction, whatever their magnitudes may be
options.D: they have the same magnitude, whatever their directions may be

correct_answer: they have the same magnitude and the same direction
explanation: Two vectors are equal only when their magnitudes are equal and their directions are identical. Their positions in space are irrelevant, so two equal arrows drawn at different places still represent the same vector.

question: Two non zero vectors are collinear. Which statement about them is necessarily true?

options.A: The angle between them is 90° and nothing else
options.B: The angle between them is 0° and nothing else
options.C: The angle between them is either 0° or 180°
options.D: The angle is 0° and their magnitudes are equal

correct_answer: The angle between them is either 0° or 180°
explanation: Collinear vectors lie along one line. They may point the same way, giving an angle of 0°, or opposite ways, giving 180°. In either case the sine of the angle is zero, which is why their vector product vanishes.

question: The minimum number of coplanar vectors of unequal magnitudes whose vector sum can be a null vector is:
explanation: Two unequal vectors can never cancel, since their resultant lies between the difference and the sum of their magnitudes and both bounds are non zero. Three unequal vectors can be arranged as the sides of a triangle taken in order, and a closed triangle gives a null resultant.

question: For two vectors P and Q, the relation between P - Q and Q - P is that:

options.B: they have different magnitudes and opposite directions
options.C: they are equal in both magnitude and direction
options.D: they have equal magnitudes and opposite directions

explanation: Q - P = -(P - Q), so the two differences are negatives of each other. They therefore have the same magnitude but point in exactly opposite directions, which shows that subtraction of vectors is not commutative.

question: Two particles are fixed on a rotating disc, one at distance r and the other at distance 2 r from the axis. Comparing them,:

options.A: their angular speeds are in the ratio 2 : 1 and their centripetal accelerations are equal
options.B: their linear speeds are equal and their centripetal accelerations are in the ratio 1 : 2
options.C: their angular speeds are equal and their centripetal accelerations are in the ratio 1 : 2
options.D: their angular speeds are equal and their centripetal accelerations are in the ratio 1 : 4

correct_answer: their angular speeds are equal and their centripetal accelerations are in the ratio 1 : 2
explanation: All points of a rigid rotating disc turn through the same angle in the same time, so ω is the same for both. Their linear speeds v = r ω are therefore in the ratio 1 : 2, and their centripetal accelerations a = r omega² are also in the ratio 1 : 2.

subject: Physics
question: In an Atwood machine, masses of 5 kg and 3 kg hang from the ends of a light string over a light frictionless pulley, and the pulley itself hangs from a spring balance. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the reading of the spring balance is:
explanation: The acceleration is (5 - 3) × 10/8 = 2.5 m s⁻² and the tension is 2 × 5 × 3 × 10/8 = 37.5 N. The pulley is light, so the balance must simply support the two string portions, giving a reading of 2 × 37.5 = 75 N. This is less than the combined weight of 80 N, the shortfall of 5 N being exactly the net downward rate of change of momentum of the two masses, since (5 - 3) × 2.5 = 5 N.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A block of mass 10 kg on a smooth horizontal table is joined by a light string over a frictionless pulley at the edge to a hanging block of mass 10 kg. In a second experiment the hanging block is removed and the free end of the string is pulled straight down with a steady force of 100 N. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the acceleration of the block on the table is:

options.B: 5 m s⁻² in the first case and 10 m s⁻² in the second
options.C: 10 m s⁻² in the first case and 5 m s⁻² in the second

correct_answer: 5 m s⁻² in the first case and 10 m s⁻² in the second
explanation: In the first case the driving force is 100 N but the moving mass is 20 kg, so a = 100/20 = 5 m s⁻² and the tension is 50 N, not 100 N. In the second case the 100 N acts directly on the string and only the 10 kg block has to be accelerated, so a = 100/10 = 10 m s⁻². A hanging weight is therefore not the same as an equal steady pull, because the hanging body must itself be accelerated.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: For a light inextensible string passing over a frictionless pulley, the tension:

options.A: has the same magnitude at every point along the string
options.B: is zero at the point where the string touches the pulley
options.C: is greater on the side carrying the heavier mass
options.D: increases steadily with the length of string paid out

correct_answer: has the same magnitude at every point along the string
explanation: Any short element of a massless string has zero mass, so the net force on it must vanish however it accelerates. The tensions pulling on its two ends must therefore be equal, and this holds all along the string. A frictionless pulley merely changes the direction of the string without changing its tension.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A block of mass 2 kg lies on a smooth plane inclined at 30°, and is joined by a light string over a frictionless pulley at the top of the incline to a block of mass 4 kg hanging vertically. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the acceleration of the system is:
explanation: The hanging block pulls with 4 × 10 = 40 N, while the block on the incline is held back by the component of its weight along the plane, 2 × 10 x sin 30 = 10 N. The net driving force is 30 N and the total mass is 6 kg, so a = 30/6 = 5 m s⁻².
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: In an Atwood machine the two masses are 6 kg and 4 kg. Starting from rest and taking g = 10 m s⁻², the distance moved by each mass in 2 s is:
explanation: The acceleration is (6 - 4) × 10/(6 + 4) = 20/10 = 2 m s⁻². Starting from rest, s = (1/2) × 2 × 2² = 4 m. One mass descends 4 m while the other rises 4 m.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: In an Atwood machine with two unequal masses released from rest, the tension in the string is:

options.A: equal to the difference of the two weights
options.B: equal to the total weight of the two masses
options.C: less than the weight of the heavier mass and greater than the weight of the lighter mass
options.D: equal to the weight of the heavier mass

correct_answer: less than the weight of the heavier mass and greater than the weight of the lighter mass
explanation: The heavier mass accelerates downward, so the upward tension on it must be less than its weight. The lighter mass accelerates upward, so the tension on it must exceed its weight. The tension therefore lies strictly between the two weights, and it equals both of them only when the masses are equal.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: Two blocks joined by a taut light inextensible string are set in motion. At every instant:

options.A: their velocities are equal in both magnitude and direction whatever the arrangement
options.B: the heavier block has the larger acceleration
options.C: their accelerations are in the inverse ratio of their masses
options.D: the magnitudes of their accelerations along the string are equal

correct_answer: the magnitudes of their accelerations along the string are equal
explanation: Since the string cannot stretch, the speed at which one end moves along the string must equal the speed at which the other end moves along it. Differentiating, the magnitudes of the accelerations along the string are equal, even though the directions may differ, as they do on either side of a pulley.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: Two blocks of masses 2 kg and 3 kg are placed in contact on a smooth horizontal surface and a horizontal force of 10 N is applied to the outer face of the 2 kg block. The acceleration of the blocks is:
explanation: The two blocks stay in contact and so share a common acceleration. Treating them as a single body of mass 5 kg, a = 10/5 = 2 m s⁻².

subject: Physics
question: Two masses of 3 kg and 2 kg hang from the two ends of a light string passing over a frictionless pulley. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the acceleration of the system is:
explanation: The net driving force is the difference of the weights, (3 - 2) × 10 = 10 N, while the mass being accelerated is the total, 3 + 2 = 5 kg. Hence a = 10/5 = 2 m s⁻², with the heavier mass descending.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
question: A boy of mass 40 kg stands at rest on a boat of mass 160 kg floating on still water. He then walks along the boat with a speed of 1 m s⁻¹ relative to the water. Neglecting the resistance of the water, the speed of the boat relative to the water is:
explanation: Before the boy walks, the system is at rest, and the water offers no horizontal force, so the total momentum stays zero. The boy carries 40 × 1 = 40 kg m s⁻¹ forward, so the boat carries 40 kg m s⁻¹ backward and its speed is 40/160 = 0.25 m s⁻¹.

subject: Physics
question: Two trolleys X and Y of masses 2 kg and 6 kg are held together on a smooth horizontal track with a compressed spring between them. When they are released, the ratio of the speed of X to that of Y is:
explanation: The spring exerts internal forces only, so the total momentum stays zero. Hence 2 v_X = 6 v_Y, giving v_X/v_Y = 6/2 = 3. The light trolley moves off three times as fast.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
question: In any collision between two bodies of an isolated system,:

options.A: the total linear momentum is conserved whether or not the kinetic energy is conserved
options.B: neither quantity is conserved unless the two bodies have equal masses
options.C: both the total linear momentum and the total kinetic energy are always conserved
options.D: the total kinetic energy is conserved but the total linear momentum need not be

correct_answer: the total linear momentum is conserved whether or not the kinetic energy is conserved
explanation: The impulsive forces during a collision are internal to the two body system and cancel in pairs, so the total momentum before equals the total momentum after. Kinetic energy, in contrast, can be converted into heat, sound and permanent deformation, and is conserved only in an elastic collision.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A shell at rest explodes into three fragments. Two of them, each of mass 1 kg, fly off at right angles to each other, each with a speed of 10 m s⁻¹. The third fragment has mass 2 kg. Its speed is:
explanation: Each 1 kg fragment carries momentum 1 × 10 = 10 kg m s⁻¹, and the two are perpendicular, so their resultant has magnitude 10 √(2) kg m s⁻¹. The third fragment must carry an equal momentum in the opposite direction, so 2 v = 10 √(2) and v = 5 √(2), about 7.1 m s⁻¹.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A body at rest explodes into two pieces of masses 2 kg and 3 kg. If the 2 kg piece moves off with a speed of 6 m s⁻¹, the speed of the 3 kg piece is:
explanation: The 2 kg piece carries momentum 2 × 6 = 12 kg m s⁻¹. The 3 kg piece must carry 12 kg m s⁻¹ in the opposite direction, so its speed is 12/3 = 4 m s⁻¹.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A stationary bomb explodes into several fragments. Which statement about the fragments is correct?

options.A: Their total momentum is greater than zero because the explosion supplies momentum
options.B: Both their total momentum and their total kinetic energy are zero
options.C: Their total kinetic energy is unchanged because momentum is conserved
options.D: Their total momentum is zero while their total kinetic energy is greater than before the explosion

correct_answer: Their total momentum is zero while their total kinetic energy is greater than before the explosion
explanation: The explosive forces are internal, so the total momentum stays at its initial value of zero, with the fragment momenta cancelling as vectors. The chemical energy stored in the charge is released and appears largely as kinetic energy of the fragments, so the total kinetic energy rises from zero to a positive value.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A bullet of mass 10 g moving horizontally at 400 m s⁻¹ embeds itself in a wooden block of mass 1.99 kg hanging from a long light string. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the height through which the block rises is:
explanation: The impact is perfectly inelastic, so 0.01 × 400 = 4 kg m s⁻¹ is shared by a total mass of 2 kg, giving a common speed of 2 m s⁻¹. The block and bullet then rise until this kinetic energy becomes potential energy, so h = v²/(2 g) = 4/20 = 0.2 m.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: The total linear momentum of a system of particles stays constant in time provided:

options.A: the total kinetic energy of the system is constant
options.B: all the particles of the system have equal masses
options.C: the net external force on the system is zero
options.D: the net internal force on the system is zero

correct_answer: the net external force on the system is zero
explanation: Summing the second law over all the particles, the internal forces cancel in pairs by the third law, leaving dP/dt equal to the net external force. If that force is zero the total momentum P does not change, whatever violent interactions take place inside the system.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A gun of mass 4 kg fires a bullet of mass 20 g with a muzzle speed of 400 m s⁻¹. The recoil speed of the gun is:
explanation: The bullet carries momentum 0.02 × 400 = 8 kg m s⁻¹. The gun must carry 8 kg m s⁻¹ backward, so its recoil speed is 8/4 = 2 m s⁻¹.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
question: When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun recoils backward. This happens because:

options.A: the gun has a larger mass than the bullet
options.B: the total kinetic energy of the gun and bullet must stay zero
options.C: the gun is pushed back by the air displaced by the bullet
options.D: the total momentum of the gun and bullet must stay zero, so the two momenta are equal and opposite

correct_answer: the total momentum of the gun and bullet must stay zero, so the two momenta are equal and opposite
explanation: Before firing, the system is at rest and has zero total momentum. The explosion involves only internal forces, so the total momentum stays zero. The forward momentum of the bullet must therefore be matched by an equal backward momentum of the gun.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A rocket accelerates forward in outer space because:

options.A: the gases ejected backward carry momentum, so the rocket gains an equal momentum forward
options.B: the pressure of the burning gases is the same in all directions inside the rocket
options.C: the burning of fuel reduces the weight of the rocket
options.D: the ejected gases push against the surrounding air

correct_answer: the gases ejected backward carry momentum, so the rocket gains an equal momentum forward
explanation: The rocket and its fuel form a system with no external force in free space, so the total momentum stays constant. The exhaust gases stream backward with large momentum, and the remaining rocket must acquire an equal forward momentum. Equivalently, by the third law the rocket pushes the gases back and the gases push the rocket forward.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A gun of mass 10 kg fires a bullet of mass 20 g with a muzzle speed of 500 m s⁻¹. The ratio of the kinetic energy of the bullet to that of the recoiling gun is:
explanation: Momentum conservation gives the gun a recoil speed of 0.02 × 500/10 = 1 m s⁻¹. The bullet has kinetic energy (1/2) × 0.02 × 500² = 2500 J while the gun has (1/2) × 10 × 1² = 5 J, a ratio of 500 to 1. This is just the inverse mass ratio, 10/0.02.

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A man of mass 50 kg standing at rest on a frictionless horizontal ice surface throws a stone of mass 5 kg horizontally at 4 m s⁻¹. His recoil speed is:
explanation: The stone carries momentum 5 × 4 = 20 kg m s⁻¹. The man must carry the same momentum in the opposite direction, so his speed is 20/50 = 0.4 m s⁻¹.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A man of mass 60 kg stands on a trolley of mass 40 kg, both at rest on a smooth horizontal track. The man jumps off horizontally with a speed of 4 m s⁻¹ with respect to the ground. The speed of the trolley just afterwards is:
explanation: The track is smooth, so there is no external horizontal force and the total momentum stays zero. The man carries 60 × 4 = 240 kg m s⁻¹ forward, so the trolley must carry 240 kg m s⁻¹ backward. Its speed is 240/40 = 6 m s⁻¹, and it is directed opposite to the jump.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
question: A bullet of mass 10 g moving at 500 m s⁻¹ embeds itself in a block of mass 990 g resting on a smooth horizontal surface. The common speed just after impact is:
explanation: The bullet brings momentum 0.01 × 500 = 5 kg m s⁻¹. The combined mass is 0.01 + 0.99 = 1 kg, so the common speed is 5/1 = 5 m s⁻¹.

subject: Physics
question: A force of 20 N acts in a direction making 60° with the horizontal. Its horizontal and vertical components are:
explanation: With the angle measured from the horizontal, the horizontal component is 20 cos 60 = 20 × 0.5 = 10 N and the vertical component is 20 sin 60 = 20 × (√(3)/2) = 10 √(3) N, about 17.3 N.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
question: If three non parallel forces keep a rigid body in equilibrium, then they must:

options.A: be such that each is perpendicular to the other two
options.C: all lie along the same straight line
options.D: be coplanar and pass through a single point

correct_answer: be coplanar and pass through a single point
explanation: Zero net force makes the three forces form a closed triangle, which requires them to be coplanar. Taking torques about the point where two of the lines of action meet, those two contribute nothing, so the third must also pass through that point or its torque would be unbalanced. Hence all three lines of action meet at a single point.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: Three concurrent coplanar forces keep a body in equilibrium. Two of them have magnitudes 3 N and 4 N and act at right angles to each other. The magnitude of the third force is:
explanation: The resultant of the perpendicular forces 3 N and 4 N has magnitude equal to the square root of (9 + 16), which is 5 N. For equilibrium, the third force must be 5 N directed exactly opposite to this resultant.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A weight of 60 N hangs from the outer end of a light horizontal rod that is hinged to a wall. A wire runs from that same outer end to a point on the wall above the hinge, making 30° with the rod. The tension in the wire is:
explanation: Consider the outer end of the rod. The forces there are the load of 60 N downward, the tension T along the wire towards the wall, and the push of the light rod along its own length, which is horizontal. Only the wire has a vertical component, so T sin 30 = 60. With sin 30 = 0.5, T = 120 N.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A set of concurrent forces keeps a body in equilibrium. This requires that:

options.A: the vector sum of all the forces is zero
options.B: the largest force is equal to the sum of the remaining forces
options.C: all the forces have equal magnitudes
options.D: the sum of the magnitudes of all the forces is zero

correct_answer: the vector sum of all the forces is zero
explanation: Equilibrium under concurrent forces means no net force, and force is a vector, so the requirement is that the vector sum vanishes. In practice this is applied by resolving all the forces along two perpendicular directions and setting each set of components to sum to zero.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A lamp of weight 40 N hangs from the ceiling by a light string. A horizontal string pulls it aside until the first string makes 60° with the vertical. The tension in the string attached to the ceiling is:
explanation: The vertical component of the tension must carry the whole weight, so T cos 60 = 40. Since cos 60 = 0.5, T = 40/0.5 = 80 N. The horizontal string then carries T sin 60 = 80 × (√(3)/2) = 40 √(3), about 69.3 N.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: The normal reaction exerted by a surface on a body resting on it:

options.A: acts along the direction in which the body tends to slide
options.B: always has magnitude equal to the weight of the body
options.C: acts along the perpendicular to the surface of contact
options.D: acts vertically upward whatever the orientation of the surface

correct_answer: acts along the perpendicular to the surface of contact
explanation: The contact force between two surfaces is resolved into a component perpendicular to the plane of contact, called the normal reaction, and a component along that plane, called friction. On an incline of angle θ the normal reaction is m g cos θ, which is less than the weight.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A block of mass 10 kg rests on a smooth plane inclined at 45° to the horizontal and is held in place by a horizontal force. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the horizontal force and the normal reaction are:
explanation: Resolving along the plane, the component of the weight down the plane is m g sin 45 and the component of the horizontal force up the plane is F cos 45. Equating gives F = m g tan 45 = 100 × 1 = 100 N. Resolving perpendicular to the plane, N = m g cos 45 + F sin 45 = 100 × 0.707 + 100 × 0.707, which is 100 √(2), about 141.4 N. The normal reaction is thus larger than the weight because the horizontal force presses the block into the plane.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A body of weight 100 N hangs from the point where two light strings meet. One string makes 30° with the horizontal and the other makes 60° with the horizontal, on opposite sides. The tensions are:

options.A: 50 N in the string at 30° and 50 √(3) N in the string at 60°
options.B: 50 √(3) N in the string at 30° and 50 N in the string at 60°
options.C: 100 N in the string at 30° and 100 N in the string at 60°
options.D: 50 N in the string at 30° and 50 N in the string at 60°

correct_answer: 50 N in the string at 30° and 50 √(3) N in the string at 60°
explanation: Let T1 be the tension in the string at 30° and T2 that in the string at 60°. Horizontal balance gives T1 cos 30 = T2 cos 60, so T2 = T1 √(3). Vertical balance gives T1 sin 30 + T2 sin 60 = 100, that is 0.5 T1 + (√(3) T1)(√(3)/2) = 100, which simplifies to 2 T1 = 100. Hence T1 = 50 N and T2 = 50 √(3), about 86.6 N. The strings are perpendicular to each other, so a check is that 50² + (50 √(3))² = 100².
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A body of mass 5 kg hangs from a light string fixed to the ceiling. A horizontal force holds the string steadily at 45° to the vertical. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the magnitude of the horizontal force is:
explanation: The vertical component of the tension balances the weight, so T cos 45 = 50 N, and the horizontal component balances the applied force, so T sin 45 = F. Dividing gives F = m g tan 45 = 50 × 1 = 50 N. The tension itself is 50/cos 45 = 50 √(2), about 70.7 N.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A body of weight 100 N rests on a smooth plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal and is held in place by a light string parallel to the plane. The tension in the string and the normal reaction are:
explanation: Resolving the weight along and perpendicular to the plane gives components W sin 30 = 100 × 0.5 = 50 N down the plane and W cos 30 = 100 × (√(3)/2) = 50 √(3) N into the plane. The string balances the first and the normal reaction balances the second, giving T = 50 N and N = 50 √(3), about 86.6 N.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: Lami's theorem can be applied to:

options.A: three parallel forces acting on a rigid body
options.B: any number of forces acting at a point
options.C: three coplanar concurrent forces that keep a body in equilibrium
options.D: two forces acting on a body in equilibrium

correct_answer: three coplanar concurrent forces that keep a body in equilibrium
explanation: Lami's theorem follows from representing three equilibrium forces by the sides of a triangle taken in order and applying the sine rule. It therefore needs exactly three forces, all in one plane and all passing through one point.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A body moves along a straight line with constant speed while several forces act on it. It follows that:

options.A: the body must appear to be at rest in every frame of reference
options.B: the vector sum of the forces is zero, although the individual forces need not be zero
options.C: exactly two forces must be acting on the body
options.D: each of the forces acting on the body must separately be zero

correct_answer: the vector sum of the forces is zero, although the individual forces need not be zero
explanation: Constant speed along a straight line means zero acceleration, so by the second law the net force must vanish. This is called dynamic equilibrium. A block sliding at steady speed on a rough floor under an applied force is a standard example: the applied force and friction are individually large but they cancel.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: For a given pair of surfaces, the force of kinetic friction is:

options.A: exactly equal to the limiting force of static friction
options.B: somewhat greater than the limiting force of static friction
options.C: zero once the body has started sliding
options.D: somewhat less than the limiting force of static friction

correct_answer: somewhat less than the limiting force of static friction
explanation: It takes a larger force to start a body sliding than to keep it sliding, because the microscopic junctions between the surfaces have less time to form once relative motion has begun. Hence mu_k is smaller than mu_s, and the friction drops slightly at the instant sliding starts.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A car moving at 20 m s⁻¹ on a level road brakes so hard that its wheels lock and it skids to rest. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.5 and g = 10 m s⁻². The distance the car skids is:
explanation: The retardation is 0.5 × 10 = 5 m s⁻². Then s = u²/(2 a) = 400/10 = 40 m. Doubling the speed would quadruple this distance, which is why speed limits matter so much.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A block of mass 5 kg rests on a horizontal floor for which the coefficient of static friction is 0.4. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the limiting force of friction is:
explanation: The normal reaction is N = 5 × 10 = 50 N. Hence the limiting friction is 0.4 × 50 = 20 N. Any applied horizontal force smaller than 20 N will be exactly balanced by friction and the block will stay at rest.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A body takes twice as long to slide from rest down a rough plane inclined at 45° as it takes to slide down a smooth plane of the same inclination and the same length. The coefficient of friction is:
explanation: For the same length travelled from rest, doubling the time means the acceleration is one quarter as large. On the smooth plane a = g sin θ, and on the rough plane a = g(sin θ - mu cos θ). Setting the second equal to one quarter of the first gives sin θ - mu cos θ = (1/4) sin θ, so mu cos θ = (3/4) sin θ and mu = (3/4) tan θ. With θ = 45°, tan θ = 1 and mu = 0.75.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A rectangular brick can be made to rest on a table on its broad face or on its narrow face. The limiting friction between the brick and the table:

options.A: is greater when the brick rests on its narrow face, in inverse proportion to the area
options.B: is zero when the brick rests on its narrow face, since the contact is too small
options.C: is greater when the brick rests on its broad face, in proportion to the larger area
options.D: is the same in both positions, since it does not depend on the apparent area of contact

correct_answer: is the same in both positions, since it does not depend on the apparent area of contact
explanation: The normal reaction equals the weight of the brick in both positions, and the coefficient of friction depends only on the pair of materials. Hence the limiting friction is unchanged. The real area of microscopic contact adjusts itself so that the friction depends only on the load.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A block of mass 2 kg rests on top of a larger block, and the coefficient of static friction between the two blocks is 0.4. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the greatest horizontal acceleration that can be given to the lower block without the upper block slipping is:
explanation: The upper block is accelerated solely by the friction from the block beneath it. That friction cannot exceed mu_s m g = 0.4 × 2 × 10 = 8 N, so the largest acceleration it can give the 2 kg block is 8/2 = 4 m s⁻². The mass of the upper block cancels, giving the general result a_max = mu_s g.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: For the same pair of surfaces and the same normal reaction, rolling friction is:

options.A: independent of the normal reaction, unlike sliding friction
options.B: much larger than sliding friction, which is why brakes work by rolling
options.C: much smaller than sliding friction, which is why wheels and ball bearings are used
options.D: exactly equal to sliding friction, since the same two surfaces are involved

correct_answer: much smaller than sliding friction, which is why wheels and ball bearings are used
explanation: In rolling, the surfaces are in contact only momentarily at each point and there is no sliding at the contact, so far less resistance arises. This is why loads are moved on wheels and why ball bearings are placed between a shaft and its housing to convert sliding into rolling.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: If the coefficient of friction between two surfaces is 1, the angle of friction is:
explanation: The angle of friction is the angle between the total contact force and the normal to the surface when friction is limiting, and it satisfies tan of that angle equal to mu. With mu = 1, the angle is 45°, and it equals the angle of repose for the same pair of surfaces.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A block lies at rest on a rough horizontal floor and no horizontal force is applied to it. The force of friction acting on the block is:

options.A: equal to the normal reaction, since the two surfaces are in contact
options.B: zero, since friction appears only in response to an applied force or a tendency to slide
options.C: equal to mu times the weight, since that is the value of the frictional force
options.D: equal to the weight of the block, since the block does not move

correct_answer: zero, since friction appears only in response to an applied force or a tendency to slide
explanation: With no horizontal force applied there is no tendency to slide, so the horizontal equilibrium equation reads simply that friction equals zero. The quantity mu_s N is the greatest friction the surfaces can supply, not the value they always supply. The vertical equilibrium is looked after by the normal reaction balancing the weight.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A block placed on a plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal slides down it with constant velocity. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the plane is:
explanation: Sliding with constant velocity means the net force along the plane is zero, so the friction exactly balances the component of the weight down the plane. Hence mu_k m g cos 30 = m g sin 30, and mu_k = tan 30 = 1/√(3), about 0.58.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A block of mass 2 kg is pressed against a vertical wall by a horizontal force. The coefficient of static friction between the block and the wall is 0.5 and g = 10 m s⁻². The least horizontal force that will prevent the block from sliding down is:
explanation: Here the applied force is horizontal and presses the block into the wall, so the normal reaction is N = F. The friction acts vertically upward and must support the weight, so mu F = m g. Hence F = m g/mu = 20/0.5 = 40 N. Note that the friction here is vertical, unlike the usual case of a block on the floor.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: The coefficient of static friction between a body and an inclined surface is 1/√(3). The angle of repose is:
explanation: Setting tan θ = 1/√(3) gives θ = 30°, since tan 30 = 1/√(3), about 0.577. A body placed on this surface will stay at rest for inclinations up to 30° and will begin to slide beyond that.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A block of mass 10 kg rests on a horizontal floor with coefficient of static friction 0.75. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the least force that can just set the block moving, when applied at the most favourable angle above the horizontal, is:
explanation: A pull inclined upward reduces the normal reaction and hence the friction, so it can be more economical than a horizontal pull. Balancing forces at the point of sliding gives F cos θ = mu(m g - F sin θ), so F = mu m g/(cos θ + mu sin θ). The denominator is largest when tan θ = mu, and then F = mu m g/√(1 + mu²). With mu = 0.75 and m g = 100 N this is 75/√(1 + 0.5625) = 75/1.25 = 60 N, against 75 N for a horizontal pull.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A block sliding on a rough horizontal floor with an initial speed of 10 m s⁻¹ comes to rest. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.2 and g = 10 m s⁻². The distance travelled before it stops is:
explanation: The only horizontal force is friction, so the retardation is a = mu_k g = 0.2 × 10 = 2 m s⁻². Using v² = u² - 2 a s with v = 0 gives s = 100/(2 × 2) = 25 m. Note that the mass cancels, so the distance does not depend on how heavy the block is.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A block of mass 2 kg rests on a plane inclined at 45°, with coefficient of friction 0.5 between the block and the plane. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the force applied parallel to the plane and directed up the plane that will just move the block upward is:
explanation: The component of the weight along the plane is 2 × 10 x sin 45 = 20/√(2) = 10 √(2) N, about 14.1 N. The normal reaction is 2 × 10 x cos 45 = 10 √(2) N, so the friction, which now acts down the plane, is 0.5 × 10 √(2) = 5 √(2) N. The required force is the sum, 15 √(2) N, about 21.2 N.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: The angle of repose for a body resting on an inclined surface is:

options.A: the angle whose sine is the coefficient of static friction
options.B: equal to the angle of friction, and its tangent is the coefficient of static friction
options.C: equal to twice the angle of friction
options.D: independent of the coefficient of friction between the surfaces

correct_answer: equal to the angle of friction, and its tangent is the coefficient of static friction
explanation: A body on an incline is on the point of sliding when the component of the weight along the plane equals the limiting friction, that is m g sin θ = mu_s m g cos θ. Cancelling m g gives tan θ = mu_s. Since the angle of friction is defined by tan of that angle equal to mu_s as well, the two angles are equal.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: The limiting force of static friction between two surfaces in contact is:

options.A: directly proportional to the apparent area of contact
options.B: independent of the nature of the two surfaces in contact
options.C: directly proportional to the normal reaction between the surfaces
options.D: directly proportional to the relative speed of the two surfaces

correct_answer: directly proportional to the normal reaction between the surfaces
explanation: The first law of friction states that the limiting friction is proportional to the normal reaction, with the coefficient of static friction as the constant of proportionality. The coefficient depends on the nature and finish of the surfaces but not on their apparent area.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A block of mass 2 kg rests on a block of mass 3 kg which lies on a smooth horizontal floor. The coefficient of static friction between the two blocks is 0.5 and g = 10 m s⁻². The largest horizontal force that can be applied to the lower block so that the two still move together is:
explanation: The upper block can only be accelerated by friction from below, and that friction is at most 0.5 × 2 × 10 = 10 N. This gives the upper block a largest possible acceleration of 10/2 = 5 m s⁻², which is just mu_s g. While the two move together the whole 5 kg accelerates at this rate, so the largest applied force is 5 × 5 = 25 N. A larger force would make the lower block slide out from under the upper one.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A car of mass 1000 kg accelerates from rest along a level road. The forward force that accelerates the car is:

options.A: the kinetic friction between the tyres and the road, acting forward
options.B: the force exerted by the engine directly on the body of the car
options.C: the normal reaction of the road on the tyres
options.D: the static friction exerted by the road on the driving wheels

correct_answer: the static friction exerted by the road on the driving wheels
explanation: The engine turns the wheels so that the contact patch tends to slip backward on the road. Friction opposes this tendency and therefore acts forward on the car. Since the tyre does not actually slide when the car grips well, this is static friction. On an icy road the available friction is small and the car cannot accelerate briskly, which shows that friction really is the driving force.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A ball of mass 1 kg moving due east with a speed of 10 m s⁻¹ is struck so that it afterwards moves due north with the same speed. The magnitude of the impulse given to the ball is:
explanation: The initial momentum is 10 kg m s⁻¹ due east and the final momentum is 10 kg m s⁻¹ due north. The change is the final minus the initial, that is 10 north together with 10 west. These are perpendicular and equal, so the magnitude is the square root of (10² + 10²), which is 10 √(2), about 14.1 N s, directed north west.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: The dimensional formula of impulse is:
explanation: Multiplying the dimensions of force, [M¹ L¹ T⁻²], by the dimension of time, [T¹], gives [M¹ L¹ T⁻¹]. This matches the dimensions of momentum, [M][L T⁻¹], as it must.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A constant force of 5 N acts on a body for 4 s. The magnitude of the impulse imparted is:
explanation: Impulse is the product of the constant force and the time for which it acts, so J = 5 × 4 = 20 N s. The body therefore gains 20 kg m s⁻¹ of momentum along the direction of the force.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: The SI unit of impulse, the newton second, is identical to the SI unit of:
explanation: One newton second equals one kg m s⁻² multiplied by one second, that is one kg m s⁻¹, which is the unit of linear momentum. This equality of units reflects the impulse momentum theorem, which states that impulse equals the change in momentum.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A body of mass 2 kg moves with a speed of 5 m s⁻¹. Its linear momentum is:
explanation: Linear momentum is the product of mass and velocity, so p = 2 × 5 = 10 kg m s⁻¹, directed along the velocity.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A force F = 6 t newton, with t in second, acts on a body of mass 3 kg initially at rest. The speed of the body at t = 2 s is:
explanation: The force grows from zero at t = 0 to 12 N at t = 2 s, so the graph is a triangle of base 2 s and height 12 N. Its area is (1/2) × 2 × 12 = 12 N s, which is the impulse. Then m v = 12 gives v = 12/3 = 4 m s⁻¹.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: The impulse of a force acting on a body during a time interval is equal to:

options.A: the rate of change of momentum of the body
options.B: the linear momentum of the body at the end of the interval
options.C: the change in the kinetic energy of the body
options.D: the change in the linear momentum of the body

correct_answer: the change in the linear momentum of the body
explanation: Integrating the second law F = dp/dt over the interval of action gives the impulse on the left and the change of momentum on the right. Hence impulse equals final momentum minus initial momentum, a vector relation.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

question: A cricket ball of mass 0.15 kg moving at 20 m s⁻¹ is brought to rest by a fielder in 0.1 s. The average force exerted on the ball is:
explanation: The momentum change has magnitude 0.15 × 20 = 3 kg m s⁻¹. Dividing by the contact time gives F = 3/0.1 = 30 N.

subject: Physics

question: A machine gun fires 10 bullets per second, each of mass 20 g, with a muzzle speed of 500 m s⁻¹. The average force needed to hold the gun steady is:
explanation: Each bullet leaves with momentum 0.02 × 500 = 10 kg m s⁻¹. Ten such bullets leave every second, so the gun must supply momentum at the rate of 10 × 10 = 100 kg m s⁻¹ per second, which is an average force of 100 N. By the third law the gun pushes back on the holder with the same average force.

subject: Physics
question: A body of mass 5 kg has its velocity changed from 2 m s⁻¹ to 8 m s⁻¹ along the same straight line by a constant force acting for 3 s. The impulse received by the body is:
explanation: The change of velocity is 8 - 2 = 6 m s⁻¹, so the impulse is 5 × 6 = 30 N s. Dividing by 3 s would give the constant force, 10 N, but the question asks for the impulse itself.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
subtopic: Force from rate of change of momentum
question: Water strikes a wall normally at the rate of 2 kg per second with a speed of 10 m s⁻¹ and then runs down the wall without rebounding. The force on the wall is:
explanation: Every second, 2 kg of water arrives with momentum 2 × 10 = 20 kg m s⁻¹ and leaves with no momentum along the original direction. The wall therefore destroys 20 kg m s⁻¹ of momentum per second, which is a force of 20 N. Had the water rebounded with the same speed, the force would have been 40 N.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Force from rate of change of momentum
question: A fielder draws his hands backward while catching a fast moving ball. This action:

options.A: increases the time of impact so that the average force on the hands is reduced, the impulse being the same
options.B: reduces the impulse received by the hands so that the force becomes smaller
options.C: increases the impulse but spreads it over a larger area of the palm
options.D: reduces the momentum of the ball before it reaches the hands

correct_answer: increases the time of impact so that the average force on the hands is reduced, the impulse being the same
explanation: The ball must lose all its momentum, so the impulse delivered is fixed at m v whatever the fielder does. Since the impulse equals the average force times the contact time, lengthening the contact time by moving the hands back reduces the average force proportionately, and the catch hurts less.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
question: A ball of mass 0.2 kg strikes a smooth vertical wall with a speed of 20 m s⁻¹ along a direction making 60° with the normal to the wall, and rebounds with the same speed at the same angle. The magnitude of the impulse received by the ball is:
explanation: Resolve the velocity into a component along the normal, 20 cos 60 = 10 m s⁻¹, and a component along the wall, 20 sin 60 m s⁻¹. The smooth wall leaves the parallel component untouched and reverses the normal component. The change of momentum is therefore 2 × 0.2 × 10 = 4 N s, directed along the outward normal.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A body of mass 6 kg initially at rest on a smooth horizontal surface receives an impulse of 30 N s. Its final speed is:
explanation: Starting from rest, the whole impulse appears as final momentum, so m v = 30 and v = 30/6 = 5 m s⁻¹.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A ball of mass 0.2 kg strikes a rigid wall normally with a speed of 10 m s⁻¹ and rebounds with the same speed. The magnitude of the impulse received by the ball is:
explanation: Take the direction towards the wall as positive. The initial momentum is 0.2 × 10 = 2 kg m s⁻¹ and the final momentum is -2 kg m s⁻¹. The change is -2 - 2 = -4 kg m s⁻¹, so the impulse has magnitude 4 N s directed away from the wall.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A horse pulls a cart forward and the cart pulls the horse backward with an equal and opposite force. The cart nevertheless accelerates forward because:

options.A: the two forces of the pair act on different bodies, and the net force on the cart alone is forward
options.B: the weight of the cart cancels the backward pull exerted by the cart
options.C: the force exerted by the cart on the horse acts only after a short time delay
options.D: the force exerted by the horse on the cart is slightly greater than the force exerted by the cart on the horse

correct_answer: the two forces of the pair act on different bodies, and the net force on the cart alone is forward
explanation: To find the motion of the cart, only the forces on the cart are collected. These are the forward pull of the horse and the backward friction on the wheels. The backward pull of the cart on the horse appears in the equation of motion of the horse, not of the cart. When the forward pull exceeds the friction on the cart, the cart accelerates.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A man of mass 50 kg stands on a weighing machine inside a lift that is accelerating upward at 2 m s⁻². Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the reading of the machine is:
explanation: The machine reads the normal reaction N. For the man, N - m g = m a with the acceleration upward, so N = m(g + a) = 50 × (10 + 2) = 50 × 12 = 600 N.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: The linear momentum of a body is plotted against time and the graph is a straight line through the origin whose slope is 6 kg m s⁻². The magnitude of the net force acting on the body is:
explanation: The second law in its general form states that force equals the rate of change of momentum, which is the slope of the graph. A slope of 6 kg m s⁻² therefore corresponds to a constant force of 6 N.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A body of mass 2 kg moving with a velocity of 10 m s⁻¹ is brought to rest uniformly in 4 s. The magnitude of the retarding force is:
explanation: The retardation is (10 - 0)/4 = 2.5 m s⁻². Hence the force is F = 2 × 2.5 = 5 N, directed opposite to the motion. The same result follows from impulse, since the momentum change is 2 × 10 = 20 kg m s⁻¹ over 4 s, giving 20/4 = 5 N.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: The position of a particle of mass 2 kg moving along a straight line is given by x = 3 t² + 4 t, where x is in metre and t in second. The magnitude of the net force acting on the particle is:
explanation: Differentiating once gives the velocity 6 t + 4, and differentiating again gives a constant acceleration of 6 m s⁻². Hence F = m a = 2 × 6 = 12 N, and the force is constant in time.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A book lies at rest on a horizontal table. The reaction to the gravitational force exerted by the earth on the book is:

options.A: the gravitational force exerted by the book on the earth
options.B: the normal force exerted by the table on the book
options.C: the normal force exerted by the book on the table
options.D: the weight of the table pressing on the floor

correct_answer: the gravitational force exerted by the book on the earth
explanation: The pull of the earth on the book is gravitational. Its third law partner must be gravitational, of the same magnitude, opposite in direction, and must act on the earth. That force is the gravitational pull of the book on the earth.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A block rests on a horizontal floor. Which of the following is a correct action and reaction pair under the third law?

options.A: The weight of the block and the push of the block on the floor
options.B: The push of the floor on the block and the push of the block on the floor
options.C: The weight of the block and the normal force of the floor on the block
options.D: The weight of the block and the weight of the floor

correct_answer: The push of the floor on the block and the push of the block on the floor
explanation: The contact interaction between block and floor gives one force on the block from the floor and one force on the floor from the block. These form the pair. The weight of the block is gravitational and its partner is the pull of the block on the earth. Weight and normal reaction act on the same body and so can never be a third law pair, even though they are numerically equal when the block is in equilibrium on a horizontal floor.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: The cable of a lift snaps and the lift falls freely. A person of mass 60 kg inside stands on a weighing machine. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the machine reads:
explanation: In free fall the lift and the person both accelerate downward at g. The equation for the person is m g - N = m g, which gives N = 0. The person and the machine fall together and press on each other with no force, a state described as weightlessness.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A net force of 20 N acts on a body of mass 5 kg lying on a smooth horizontal surface. The acceleration produced is:
explanation: Using a = F/m with F = 20 N and m = 5 kg gives a = 20/5 = 4 m s⁻², directed along the applied force.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A student checks an equation by dimensions and needs the dimensions of force. These are:
explanation: Force is mass times acceleration. Acceleration has dimensions [L T⁻²], so force has dimensions [M¹ L¹ T⁻²]. The corresponding SI unit is the newton, equal to kg m s⁻².
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A constant force of 10 N acts for 5 s on a body of mass 2 kg initially at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. The distance covered in this time is:
explanation: The acceleration is a = 10/2 = 5 m s⁻². Starting from rest, s = (1/2) × 5 × 5² = (1/2) × 5 × 25 = 62.5 m.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: Two perpendicular forces of magnitudes 3 N and 4 N act simultaneously on a body of mass 5 kg lying on a smooth horizontal surface. The magnitude of the acceleration produced is:
explanation: The resultant of the two forces is the square root of (3² + 4²), which is 5 N. Dividing by the mass gives a = 5/5 = 1 m s⁻².
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A man of mass 50 kg stands on a spring balance inside a lift and the balance reads 400 N. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the lift must be:
explanation: The true weight is 50 × 10 = 500 N, and the balance reads less than this, so the acceleration must be directed downward. Writing N = m(g - a) gives 400 = 50(10 - a), so 10 - a = 8 and a = 2 m s⁻² downward. Note that the lift could be moving upward while slowing down, since only the acceleration matters.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A monkey of mass 20 kg climbs a rope that can withstand a maximum tension of 300 N. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the greatest upward acceleration with which the monkey can climb without breaking the rope is:
explanation: The rope tension must satisfy T = m(g + a) and cannot exceed 300 N. Hence 20(10 + a) is at most 300, so 10 + a is at most 15 and a is at most 5 m s⁻². If the monkey merely hangs on, the tension is 200 N, and if it climbs with acceleration 5 m s⁻² the tension reaches exactly 300 N.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: According to Newton's second law, the net external force acting on a body is equal to:

options.A: the product of its mass and its velocity
options.B: the rate of change of its linear momentum
options.C: the rate of change of its kinetic energy
options.D: the rate of change of its displacement

correct_answer: the rate of change of its linear momentum
explanation: The general statement of the second law is that the net external force equals the time rate of change of linear momentum. For a body of constant mass, dp/dt = m dv/dt = m a, giving the familiar form F = m a.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: The same constant force acts separately on two bodies X and Y of masses 2 kg and 8 kg, both initially at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. The ratio of the acceleration of X to that of Y is:
explanation: With F fixed, a = F/m, so a_X/a_Y = m_Y/m_X = 8/2 = 4. The lighter body accelerates four times as fast.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: Newton's first law of motion is essentially a statement about which property of matter?

options.A: The tendency of a body to resist any change in its state of rest or of uniform motion
options.B: The tendency of a body to move towards a region of lower potential energy
options.C: The tendency of a body to resist any change in its total mass
options.D: The tendency of a body to return to its original position after being displaced

correct_answer: The tendency of a body to resist any change in its state of rest or of uniform motion
explanation: The first law says a body cannot change its own state of rest or of uniform straight line motion. This built in resistance to a change of state is called inertia, which is why the first law is also called the law of inertia. Mass is the quantitative measure of inertia.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: The coefficient of restitution for a collision between two bodies is defined as:

options.A: the ratio of the total kinetic energy after the collision to that before it
options.B: the ratio of the relative speed of separation to the relative speed of approach
options.C: the ratio of the total momentum after the collision to that before it
options.D: the ratio of the relative speed of approach to the relative speed of separation

correct_answer: the ratio of the relative speed of separation to the relative speed of approach
explanation: The coefficient of restitution measures how much of the relative motion survives the collision. It is 1 for a perfectly elastic collision, in which the bodies separate as fast as they approached, and 0 for a perfectly inelastic collision, in which they move off together with no relative velocity at all. Real collisions lie between these two limits.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A body of mass 2 kg moving at 8 m s⁻¹ makes a head on elastic collision with a stationary body of mass 6 kg. The velocity of the 2 kg body just after the collision is:

options.A: 8 m s⁻¹ in the reverse direction
options.B: 2 m s⁻¹ in the reverse direction
options.C: 4 m s⁻¹ in the reverse direction
options.D: 4 m s⁻¹ in the original direction

correct_answer: 4 m s⁻¹ in the reverse direction
explanation: Substituting m1 = 2 kg, m2 = 6 kg and u = 8 m s⁻¹ gives v1 = (2 - 6) × 8/8 = -4 m s⁻¹, so the 2 kg body rebounds at 4 m s⁻¹. The 6 kg body moves forward at v2 = 2 × 2 × 8/8 = 4 m s⁻¹. A check: momentum before is 16 kg m s⁻¹ and after is -8 + 24 = 16 kg m s⁻¹, while the kinetic energy is 64 J before and 16 + 48 = 64 J after.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A ball dropped from a height of 10 m onto a floor rebounds to a height of 2.5 m. The coefficient of restitution between the ball and the floor is:
explanation: The speed at any height is proportional to the square root of that height, since v is the square root of 2 g h. Hence e equals the square root of (2.5/10), which is the square root of 0.25, that is 0.5. Equivalently, the height ratio is the square of the coefficient.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: A body moving with speed u collides head on and elastically with an identical body at rest. After the collision:

options.A: the first body stops and the second moves off with speed u
options.B: the first rebounds with speed u and the second stays at rest
options.C: both move off with speed u in opposite directions
options.D: both move forward together with speed u/2

correct_answer: the first body stops and the second moves off with speed u
explanation: Momentum conservation gives v1 + v2 = u and kinetic energy conservation gives v1² + v2² = u². Solving these together gives either the initial state or the exchanged state v1 = 0 and v2 = u. Since the bodies must separate, the exchange is the physical solution. This is what is seen when one carrom coin strikes another squarely.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

subject: Physics
question: The work energy theorem states that the net work done on a body by all the forces acting on it equals:

options.A: the change in its kinetic energy
options.B: its total mechanical energy at the end of the motion
options.C: the change in its linear momentum
options.D: the impulse delivered to it by those forces

correct_answer: the change in its kinetic energy
explanation: Starting from F = m a and using v² = u² + 2 a s, multiplying by m/2 gives F s equal to the difference of the two kinetic energy terms. Hence the net work done equals the change in kinetic energy, whatever forces are involved.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 3: Laws of Motion

question: For a body to just complete a vertical circle of radius r, its minimum speed at the lowest point must be:
