question: In a hydraulic lift the two pistons have areas in the ratio 1 : 50. A force of 100 N is applied on the smaller piston. The maximum load that can be raised on the larger piston is:
explanation: The same pressure acts on both pistons, so F2 = F1 × (A2 / A1) = 100 × 50 = 5000 N. The lift multiplies force by the area ratio, while the smaller piston must be pushed through a correspondingly larger distance.

question: For a point inside a liquid that is open to the atmosphere, the gauge pressure is:

options.A: the atmospheric pressure minus the absolute pressure at the point
options.B: the absolute pressure at the point plus the atmospheric pressure
options.C: the absolute pressure at the point divided by the atmospheric pressure
options.D: the absolute pressure at the point minus the atmospheric pressure

correct_answer: the absolute pressure at the point minus the atmospheric pressure
explanation: A pressure gauge open to the atmosphere on one side reads the excess of the true pressure over atmospheric pressure. Hence P_gauge = P_absolute - P_atmospheric, and for a liquid column P_gauge = h ρ g.

question: Equal masses of water, of specific heat capacity 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, and of an oil, of specific heat capacity 2100 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, are given the same quantity of heat, with no change of state in either. Then:

options.A: the oil ends up hotter, its temperature rise being twice that of the water
options.B: the water ends up hotter, its temperature rise being twice that of the oil
options.C: the oil ends up hotter, its temperature rise being four times that of the water
options.D: both reach the same temperature rise, since they were given the same quantity of heat

correct_answer: the oil ends up hotter, its temperature rise being twice that of the water
explanation: The oil has half the specific heat capacity of the water, so for the same mass and the same heat its temperature rise is twice as large. Starting from the same temperature, the oil therefore ends up hotter.

question: Water is used as the coolant in a car radiator chiefly because:

options.A: it has a small specific heat capacity, so it heats up quickly and so carries the heat away quickly
options.B: it has a large latent heat of fusion, so it stays cold for a long time
options.C: it is a better conductor of heat than the metal of the radiator itself
options.D: it has a large specific heat capacity, so it can carry away much heat for a small rise in its own temperature

correct_answer: it has a large specific heat capacity, so it can carry away much heat for a small rise in its own temperature
explanation: With c = 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, water has one of the largest specific heat capacities of any common substance. Each kilogram absorbs 4200 J for every kelvin it warms, so a modest flow of water can carry a large amount of heat away from the engine without itself becoming very hot.

question: The principle of calorimetry, used when hot and cold bodies are mixed in a well insulated container, states that:

options.A: the final temperature is always the arithmetic mean of the initial temperatures
options.B: the heat lost by the hotter bodies equals the heat lost by the colder bodies
options.C: the heat lost by the hotter bodies equals the heat gained by the colder bodies
options.D: the temperature lost by the hotter bodies equals the temperature gained by the colder bodies

correct_answer: the heat lost by the hotter bodies equals the heat gained by the colder bodies
explanation: In an insulated container no heat escapes to the surroundings, so all the heat given out by the hotter bodies is taken up by the colder ones. Writing this balance as m1 c1 (T1 - T) = m2 c2 (T - T2) gives the equation from which the final temperature is found.

question: Two blocks of the same metal have masses 1 kg and 3 kg. Comparing the two blocks,:

options.A: their heat capacities are equal, while the specific heat capacity of the heavier block is three times that of the lighter one
options.B: both the specific heat capacity and the heat capacity are the same for the two blocks
options.C: their specific heat capacities are equal, while the heat capacity of the heavier block is three times that of the lighter one
options.D: both the specific heat capacity and the heat capacity of the heavier block are three times those of the lighter one

correct_answer: their specific heat capacities are equal, while the heat capacity of the heavier block is three times that of the lighter one
explanation: Both blocks are of the same metal, so both have the same c. The heat capacity is m c, so for the 3 kg block it is three times that for the 1 kg block. The heavier block therefore needs three times as much heat for the same temperature rise.

question: A metal sphere of volume 2 × 10⁻⁴ m³ and density 8000 kg m⁻³ falls with its terminal velocity through a liquid of density 1000 kg m⁻³. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the viscous drag acting on the sphere at that stage is:
explanation: Weight = V ρ g = 2 × 10⁻⁴ x 8000 × 10 = 16 N. Upthrust = V sigma g = 2 × 10⁻⁴ x 1000 × 10 = 2 N. Since the sphere moves with constant velocity the net force is zero, so the drag makes up the difference: 16 minus 2 = 14 N. Notice that no value of the coefficient of viscosity is needed for this balance.

question: The tiny water droplets of a fog appear to remain suspended in the air for a very long time. The main reason is that:

options.A: their terminal velocity is extremely small because it varies as the square of the radius
options.B: the coefficient of viscosity of air increases sharply when fog forms
options.C: the upthrust of the air on them exactly balances their weight
options.D: the surface tension of water holds the droplets up against gravity

correct_answer: their terminal velocity is extremely small because it varies as the square of the radius
explanation: Fog droplets have radii of the order of a few micrometres. Because the terminal velocity varies as the square of the radius, reducing the radius by a factor of a thousand compared with a raindrop reduces the terminal velocity by a factor of a million. The droplets therefore settle so slowly that the slightest air current keeps them aloft.

unit: Unit 7: Properties of Solids and Liquids

question: A small sphere whose density is less than that of the surrounding liquid is released at the bottom of a deep tank of that liquid. After a short time the sphere:

options.A: stays exactly where it was released, since the upthrust and the weight are equal
options.B: moves upward with a constant terminal speed
options.C: moves upward with a steadily increasing speed all the way to the surface
options.D: moves downward with a constant terminal speed

correct_answer: moves upward with a constant terminal speed
explanation: When ρ is less than sigma the quantity ρ minus sigma is negative, so the terminal velocity comes out negative, meaning that the steady motion is upward. Physically the upthrust exceeds the weight, the sphere accelerates upward, and the drag now acts downward and grows until the three forces balance. An air bubble rising steadily through water is the familiar example.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

question: For small spheres of the same material falling through the same liquid, the terminal velocity is:

options.A: directly proportional to the radius of the sphere
options.B: inversely proportional to the radius of the sphere
options.C: independent of the radius of the sphere
options.D: directly proportional to the square of the radius of the sphere

correct_answer: directly proportional to the square of the radius of the sphere
explanation: The effective weight of the sphere grows as r³ while the Stokes drag grows only as r, so the balance is struck at a speed that grows as r². Hence doubling the radius makes the terminal velocity four times as large.

question: A small sphere released in a deep column of a viscous liquid finally attains a terminal velocity. At that stage:

options.A: the weight of the sphere is balanced by the upthrust alone, the viscous drag having fallen to zero
options.B: the weight, the upthrust and the viscous drag all act downwards and add up to zero
options.C: the weight of the sphere is balanced by the sum of the upthrust and the viscous drag
options.D: the viscous drag alone balances the weight, the upthrust being negligible for a solid sphere

correct_answer: the weight of the sphere is balanced by the sum of the upthrust and the viscous drag
explanation: As the sphere speeds up the viscous drag 6 π eta r v grows, while the weight and the upthrust stay fixed. When the drag has grown enough that the upward forces balance the weight, the acceleration becomes zero and the sphere continues at a constant terminal velocity.

question: A main pipe of cross sectional area 12 cm² carries water at 2 m s⁻¹. It branches into four identical smaller pipes, each of cross sectional area 2 cm². The speed of the water in each smaller pipe is:
explanation: The volume flow rate in the main pipe is 12 × 2 = 24 in units of cm² m s⁻¹. The four branches together offer a cross sectional area of 4 × 2 = 8 cm². Hence the speed in each branch is 24 divided by 8 = 3 m s⁻¹. Note that the total branch area is smaller than the main pipe area, so the water speeds up.

question: Water leaves a tap of radius 4 mm with a speed of 1 m s⁻¹ and falls freely as a smooth stream. Taking g = 10 m s⁻² and neglecting any effect of surface tension, the radius of the stream at a point 0.75 m below the tap is:
explanation: The speed after falling 0.75 m is given by v2² = 1 + 2 × 10 × 0.75 = 16, so v2 = 4 m s⁻¹. Applying the equation of continuity to the circular stream, r1² v1 = r2² v2, so r2² = 16 × 1 divided by 4 = 4, giving r2 = 2 mm. The stream narrows because it speeds up as it falls.

topic: Streamline Flow and Equation of Continuity
question: In the steady streamline flow of a liquid, two streamlines can never cross each other because:

options.A: the pressure would become infinitely large at the point where they crossed
options.B: a crossing point would give the fluid particle there two different velocities at the same instant
options.C: the liquid is incompressible and its density cannot change at a crossing point
options.D: the viscosity of the liquid prevents adjacent layers from ever meeting

correct_answer: a crossing point would give the fluid particle there two different velocities at the same instant
explanation: The velocity of the fluid at any point of a streamline is directed along the tangent to that streamline. If two streamlines crossed, the particle at the crossing point would have to move along two different tangents at the same instant, which is impossible. Hence streamlines never intersect in steady flow.

question: For a liquid flowing through a pipe, the flow is expected to be:

options.A: streamline at every value of the Reynolds number provided the pipe is smooth
options.B: turbulent at every value of the Reynolds number provided the liquid has some viscosity
options.C: streamline when the Reynolds number is below about 1000 and turbulent when it is above about 2000
options.D: turbulent when the Reynolds number is below about 1000 and streamline when it is above about 2000

correct_answer: streamline when the Reynolds number is below about 1000 and turbulent when it is above about 2000
explanation: A small Reynolds number means viscous forces dominate and the layers slide smoothly over one another, giving streamline flow. A large Reynolds number means inertial effects dominate and the flow becomes turbulent. For flow in a pipe the flow is streamline up to about 1000 and turbulent beyond about 2000, with an unstable region in between.

question: Water flows steadily through a pipe whose cross sectional area falls from 10 cm² to 5 cm². Where the area is 10 cm² the speed of the water is 2 m s⁻¹. Where the area is 5 cm² the speed is:
explanation: A1 v1 = 10 × 2 = 20 in units of cm² m s⁻¹. Hence v2 = 20 divided by 5 = 4 m s⁻¹. Converting both areas to square metres would give the same ratio, so the conversion is not needed here.

question: The Reynolds number of a flowing fluid is:

options.A: measured in metre per second, like the critical velocity
options.B: a dimensionless quantity with no unit
options.C: measured in kg m⁻³, like the density of the fluid
options.D: measured in N s m⁻², like the coefficient of viscosity

correct_answer: a dimensionless quantity with no unit
explanation: Substituting dimensions, [M L⁻³][L T⁻¹][L] divided by [M L⁻¹ T⁻¹] gives [M⁰ L⁰ T⁰]. The Reynolds number is therefore a pure number, which is why the same critical values apply to pipes of every size.

question: Eight identical spherical drops of a liquid, each of radius 1 mm, coalesce isothermally into a single large drop. The surface tension of the liquid is 0.05 N m⁻¹. The energy released is:
explanation: Volume conservation gives R = 8¹⁄³ x r = 2 × 1 mm = 2 mm. Initial total area = 8 × 4 π r² = 32 π x 10⁻⁶ m². Final area = 4 π R² = 4 π x 4 × 10⁻⁶ = 16 π x 10⁻⁶ m². The area decreases by 16 π x 10⁻⁶ m², so the energy released is T x 16 π x 10⁻⁶ = 0.05 × 16 π x 10⁻⁶ = 0.8 π x 10⁻⁶ J.

question: A soap film is formed on a frame carrying a movable wire of length 20 cm. The surface tension of the solution is 0.04 N m⁻¹. The force that must be applied to the wire to keep the film from contracting is:
explanation: F = 2 T l = 2 × 0.04 × 0.20 = 0.016 N. The factor of two arises because the film has an upper and a lower surface, each pulling on the wire with force T l.

question: A single spherical drop of radius R is broken into 64 identical smaller drops. The radius of each smaller drop is:
explanation: The total volume is unchanged, so 64 × (4/3) π r³ = (4/3) π R³, giving r³ = R³ divided by 64 and hence r = R divided by 4. The total surface area rises by the factor 64¹⁄³ = 4, which is why energy must be supplied.

question: Two soap bubbles of unequal radii are blown at the two ends of a tube and the connecting tap between them is opened. Then:

options.A: the smaller bubble shrinks and the larger bubble grows
options.B: the larger bubble shrinks and the smaller bubble grows
options.C: both bubbles stay exactly as they were because the surface tension is the same
options.D: both bubbles adjust until they reach the same radius

correct_answer: the smaller bubble shrinks and the larger bubble grows
explanation: The excess pressure inside a bubble is 4 T / R, which is greater for the bubble of smaller radius. When the tap is opened air flows from the region of higher pressure to that of lower pressure, that is from the smaller bubble into the larger one. The smaller bubble therefore collapses further while the larger one expands.

question: Two soap bubbles of radii 3 cm and 4 cm coalesce isothermally under vacuum to form a single bubble. The radius of the resulting bubble is:
explanation: For a soap bubble the pressure inside is 4 T / R above the outside pressure, which is zero here. Applying Boyle's law to the enclosed air, (4 T / R1)(4/3 π R1³) + (4 T / R2)(4/3 π R2³) = (4 T / R)(4/3 π R³), which simplifies to R1² + R2² = R². Hence R = square root of (9 + 16) = 5 cm.

question: A liquid drop and a soap bubble of the same liquid have the same radius. The ratio of the excess pressure inside the drop to that inside the bubble is:
explanation: The drop has one liquid to air surface and gives 2 T / R. The soap bubble has an inner and an outer surface and gives 4 T / R. The ratio is therefore 2 T / R to 4 T / R, that is 1 : 2.

question: A mercury drop is broken into 27 identical smaller drops at constant temperature. The ratio of the total surface energy of the parent drop to that of all the smaller drops taken together is:
explanation: Each small drop has radius r = R divided by 27¹⁄³ = R divided by 3. The total area of the small drops is 27 × 4 π (R/3)² = 27 × 4 π R² divided by 9 = 3 × 4 π R². Since surface energy is T times area, the ratio of the parent energy to the total final energy is 4 π R² T to 12 π R² T, that is 1 : 3. The extra energy comes from the work done in splitting.

question: A drop of a liquid of surface tension 0.05 N m⁻¹ and radius 1 mm is sprayed into 1000 identical droplets. The work done in the process is:
explanation: Here n¹⁄³ = 1000¹⁄³ = 10, so the factor n¹⁄³ minus 1 equals 9. With R = 1 × 10⁻³ m, R² = 1 × 10⁻⁶ m². Hence W = 4 π x 0.05 × 1 × 10⁻⁶ x 9 = 1.8 π x 10⁻⁶ J, which is about 5.7 × 10⁻⁶ J. Each droplet has radius 1 mm divided by 10, that is 0.1 mm.

question: The work done in increasing the free surface area of a liquid by one square metre at constant temperature is numerically equal to:

options.A: twice the surface tension of the liquid
options.B: the surface tension of the liquid
options.C: half the surface tension of the liquid
options.D: the surface tension divided by the density of the liquid

correct_answer: the surface tension of the liquid
explanation: Isothermal work done in creating extra surface is W = T dA. For dA = 1 m² the work equals T numerically, which is why surface tension can be quoted in J m⁻² as well as in N m⁻¹.

question: A spherical drop of radius R and surface tension T is broken up isothermally into n identical smaller drops. The work that must be done is:
explanation: Conserving volume, n x (4/3) π r³ = (4/3) π R³, so r = R divided by n¹⁄³. The total final area is n x 4 π r² = 4 π R² x n¹⁄³. The initial area is 4 π R². The increase is 4 π R² (n¹⁄³ - 1), and the work done is T times this, that is 4 π T R² (n¹⁄³ - 1).

unit: Unit 7: Properties of Solids and Liquids
chapter: Mechanical Properties of Solids, Mechanical Properties of Fluids and Thermal Properties of Matter
question: According to the molecular theory of surface tension, a molecule lying exactly on the free surface of a liquid experiences:

options.A: a net force directed along the surface towards the walls of the vessel
options.B: a net outward force directed away from the bulk of the liquid
options.C: no net force at all because its sphere of influence is complete
options.D: a net inward force directed into the bulk of the liquid

correct_answer: a net inward force directed into the bulk of the liquid
explanation: A molecule deep inside the liquid is pulled equally in all directions and the resultant is zero. For a molecule on the surface the upper half of its sphere of influence is nearly empty, so the cohesive pull from below is unbalanced and the resultant force is directed inwards. This is why a surface molecule has extra potential energy and why the liquid tends to minimise its surface area.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

unit: Unit 7: Properties of Solids and Liquids

question: As the temperature of a liquid is raised towards its critical temperature, the surface tension of the liquid:

options.A: first decreases and then increases sharply near the critical temperature
options.B: decreases and becomes zero at the critical temperature
options.C: increases and becomes maximum at the critical temperature
options.D: remains constant because surface tension is a property of the liquid alone

correct_answer: decreases and becomes zero at the critical temperature
explanation: Rising temperature increases the average separation and the thermal motion of the molecules, which weakens the cohesive forces responsible for surface tension. At the critical temperature the distinction between liquid and vapour disappears and the surface tension falls to zero. This is why hot water cleans better than cold water.

question: The triple point of water is:

options.A: the temperature at which water has its greatest density, namely 277.15 K
options.B: the temperature at which water boils under a pressure of one atmosphere, namely 373.15 K
options.C: the single temperature and pressure at which ice, water and water vapour coexist in equilibrium, the temperature being 273.16 K
options.D: the temperature at which ice melts under a pressure of one atmosphere, namely 273.15 K

correct_answer: the single temperature and pressure at which ice, water and water vapour coexist in equilibrium, the temperature being 273.16 K
explanation: At the triple point the solid, liquid and vapour phases of water are all in equilibrium together, and this happens at only one temperature and one pressure. That temperature is 273.16 K, which is 0.01° Celsius, and it is used as a fixed point in defining the kelvin.

question: A rise in temperature of 1 kelvin is the same as a rise of:

unit: Unit 7: Properties of Solids and Liquids
chapter: Mechanical Properties of Solids, Mechanical Properties of Fluids and Thermal Properties of Matter
question: Two bodies at different temperatures are placed in thermal contact and the pair is isolated from the surroundings. The two bodies are said to have reached thermal equilibrium when:

options.A: the hotter body has given up the whole of its internal energy to the colder body
options.B: their temperatures have become equal and there is no further net transfer of heat between them
options.C: the colder body stops absorbing heat while the hotter body goes on losing heat
options.D: the two bodies contain equal amounts of internal energy

correct_answer: their temperatures have become equal and there is no further net transfer of heat between them
explanation: Heat flows from the hotter body to the colder one until the two temperatures become equal. At that stage each body still exchanges energy with the other, but the two exchanges are equal and opposite, so the net transfer is zero. Equality of temperature, not of internal energy, is the condition for thermal equilibrium.

question: A glass vessel of volume 1000 cm³ is partly filled with mercury. The volume of the empty space above the mercury is to stay the same at every temperature. Mercury has gamma = 1.8 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹ and the glass has alpha = 9 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹. The volume of mercury required is:
explanation: gamma_glass = 3 × 9 × 10⁻⁶ = 2.7 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹. The empty space is V_vessel - V_mercury, and for it to be unchanged the two expansions must be equal, so V_mercury x 1.8 × 10⁻⁴ = 1000 × 2.7 × 10⁻⁵. Hence V_mercury = 1000 × 2.7 × 10⁻⁵ / 1.8 × 10⁻⁴ = 150 cm³.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 7: Properties of Solids and Liquids

question: A solid metal block is heated so that its temperature rises, with no melting and no loss of material. Of the following, the quantity that stays the same is:
explanation: Heating does not add or remove any material, so the mass is unchanged. Every length grows by (1 + alpha delta T), so areas grow by (1 + 2 alpha delta T) and the volume by (1 + 3 alpha delta T). Since density is mass divided by volume, the density must fall.

question: A bimetallic strip is made by riveting together a strip of brass and a strip of iron, brass having the larger coefficient of linear expansion. When the strip is heated it bends so that:

options.A: both strips curve equally, so the strip stays straight and merely becomes longer
options.B: the iron lies along the outer side of the curve and the brass along the inner side
options.C: the brass lies along the outer side of the curve and the iron along the inner side
options.D: the strip twists about its own long axis instead of bending

correct_answer: the brass lies along the outer side of the curve and the iron along the inner side
explanation: For the same temperature rise the brass tries to become longer than the iron. Being riveted together, the pair can only accommodate this by curving, with the longer brass on the outside of the arc and the shorter iron on the inside. This bending is used to open and close contacts in thermostats.

question: A steel measuring scale is correct at 20° Celsius. On a hot day at 40° Celsius the scale is used to measure a rod and reads 100.000 cm. Steel has alpha = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹. The true length of the rod is:
explanation: At 40° Celsius each division of the scale is longer than its marked value by the factor (1 + 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ x 20) = 1 + 2.4 × 10⁻⁴. Since each division now covers more length than it claims, the reading is an underestimate. True length = 100.000 × (1 + 2.4 × 10⁻⁴) = 100.024 cm.

question: A liquid is heated in a glass vessel. The coefficient of apparent expansion of the liquid, as judged from the change in its level in the vessel, is:

options.A: the real coefficient of cubical expansion of the liquid plus the coefficient of cubical expansion of the glass
options.B: the real coefficient of cubical expansion of the liquid minus the coefficient of cubical expansion of the glass
options.C: the real coefficient of cubical expansion of the liquid minus the coefficient of linear expansion of the glass
options.D: the coefficient of cubical expansion of the glass minus the real coefficient of cubical expansion of the liquid

correct_answer: the real coefficient of cubical expansion of the liquid minus the coefficient of cubical expansion of the glass
explanation: The container expands at the same time as the liquid, so part of the extra liquid volume is taken up by the extra vessel volume. Only the difference shows as a rise in level, giving gamma_apparent = gamma_real - gamma_vessel.

question: In a cold country the water in a pond freezes at the surface first, while fish survive in the water below. The chief reason is that:

options.A: ice is denser than water and so forms at the surface, where the cooling is fastest
options.B: water conducts heat so well that the whole pond cools uniformly and then freezes downward
options.C: the pressure at the bottom of the pond raises the freezing point of the water there
options.D: water is densest at 4° Celsius, so water colder than this is lighter and stays on top to freeze, while water at 4° Celsius collects at the bottom

correct_answer: water is densest at 4° Celsius, so water colder than this is lighter and stays on top to freeze, while water at 4° Celsius collects at the bottom
explanation: As the pond cools, water sinks until it reaches 4° Celsius, the temperature of maximum density. Cooled below that, the water becomes lighter and remains at the surface, where it freezes. Ice, being less dense still, floats and forms an insulating lid, leaving water at about 4° Celsius below in which fish can live.

question: A circular hole is cut in a uniform metal plate. When the whole plate is heated uniformly, the diameter of the hole:

options.A: increases, in exactly the same proportion as any length marked on the plate
options.B: decreases at first and then increases once the whole plate is hot
options.C: stays unchanged, because empty space cannot expand
options.D: decreases, because the surrounding metal expands inward into the hole

correct_answer: increases, in exactly the same proportion as any length marked on the plate
explanation: Imagine the disc of metal that was removed to make the hole. On heating, that disc would expand and still fit the hole exactly, so the hole must expand by the same amount. All distances in the plate, filled or empty, are multiplied by the same factor (1 + alpha delta T).

question: A viscous liquid flows steadily along a horizontal pipe of circular cross section. The magnitude of the velocity gradient is:

options.A: greatest on the axis of the pipe and zero at the wall
options.B: greatest at the wall of the pipe and zero on the axis
options.C: the same at every point of the cross section of the pipe
options.D: zero everywhere, because the flow is steady

correct_answer: greatest at the wall of the pipe and zero on the axis
explanation: The layer touching the wall is held at rest by adhesion, while the layer along the axis moves fastest. The speed therefore changes most steeply just beside the wall, so the velocity gradient and the viscous drag are largest there. On the axis the speed passes through its maximum, so the gradient falls to zero.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

question: According to Newton's law of viscosity, the viscous force between two adjacent layers of a flowing liquid is directly proportional to:

options.A: the square of the velocity gradient and the area of contact of the layers
options.B: the volume of the liquid between the layers and the velocity gradient
options.C: the area of contact of the layers and the relative velocity of the layers alone
options.D: the area of contact of the layers and the velocity gradient perpendicular to them

correct_answer: the area of contact of the layers and the velocity gradient perpendicular to them
explanation: Newton's law of viscous flow states that the tangential force between adjacent layers is F = eta A dv/dx, where A is the area of contact and dv/dx is the velocity gradient normal to the layers. The constant eta is the coefficient of viscosity of the liquid.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

question: From Stokes' law F = 6 π eta r v, the dimensional formula of the coefficient of viscosity eta is:
explanation: Force has dimensions [M L T⁻²], area has [L²] and the velocity gradient has [T⁻¹]. Hence eta has dimensions [M L T⁻²] divided by ([L²][T⁻¹]), which gives [M¹ L⁻¹ T⁻¹].

question: When the temperature of a gas is raised at constant pressure, its coefficient of viscosity:

options.A: decreases, because the cohesive forces between the molecules become weaker
options.B: decreases, because the gas expands and its density falls
options.C: increases, because faster molecules transfer momentum between layers more rapidly
options.D: remains unchanged, because the molecules of a gas are already far apart

correct_answer: increases, because faster molecules transfer momentum between layers more rapidly
explanation: In a gas the layers are coupled not by cohesion but by molecules wandering from one layer to another and carrying momentum with them. Raising the temperature raises the mean molecular speed, so momentum is transported faster and the viscosity increases. This is the exact opposite of the behaviour of a liquid.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Comparing heat needed in two processes
question: The same mass of an ideal gas is given the same rise in temperature, once at constant volume and once at constant pressure. Compared with the constant volume case, the heat needed in the constant pressure case is:

options.A: the same, since the change in internal energy is the same in the two cases
options.B: greater, since the internal energy change is larger at constant pressure
options.C: smaller, since the expanding gas returns some energy to the surroundings
options.D: greater, since the gas also does work while expanding

correct_answer: greater, since the gas also does work while expanding
explanation: In both cases the internal energy rises by n Cv dT. At constant pressure the gas additionally does work n R dT, and this extra energy must come from the heat supplied. Hence more heat is needed at constant pressure, and Cp exceeds Cv by R.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: Process with given P against V relation
question: One mole of a monatomic ideal gas expands so that its pressure falls linearly with volume from 3 × 10⁵ Pa at 1 × 10⁻³ m³ to 1 × 10⁵ Pa at 3 × 10⁻³ m³. Taking R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, the heat absorbed by the gas is:
explanation: The mean pressure is (3 × 10⁵ plus 1 × 10⁵)/2 = 2 × 10⁵ Pa and the volume increases by 2 × 10⁻³ m³, so W = 400 J. The products of pressure and volume are 300 J at both ends, so the temperature is unchanged and dU = 0. Hence dQ = 0 plus 400 = 400 J.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: The first law of thermodynamics is expressed as:

options.A: dQ = dU minus dW, where dQ is the heat supplied, dU the change in internal energy and dW the work done by the system
options.B: dU = dQ + dW, where dQ is the heat supplied, dU the change in internal energy and dW the work done by the system
options.C: dQ = dU + dW, where dQ is the heat supplied, dU the change in internal energy and dW the work done by the system
options.D: dW = dU + dQ, where dQ is the heat supplied, dU the change in internal energy and dW the work done by the system

correct_answer: dQ = dU + dW, where dQ is the heat supplied, dU the change in internal energy and dW the work done by the system
explanation: Energy supplied as heat has only two destinations. Part of it raises the internal energy of the system and the rest leaves as work done by the system, giving dQ = dU + dW.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A gas is compressed so that 400 J of work is done on it, and during the process it rejects 250 J of heat. The internal energy of the gas:
explanation: Heat rejected gives dQ = minus 250 J. Work done on the gas gives dW = minus 400 J. Then dU = minus 250 minus (minus 400) = plus 150 J, so the internal energy rises by 150 J and the gas gets hotter.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: Physical content of the first law
question: The first law of thermodynamics is essentially a statement of:

options.A: the impossibility of converting all the absorbed heat into work in a cycle
options.B: the transitive property of thermal equilibrium between systems
options.C: the fact that entropy of an isolated system never decreases
options.D: the conservation of energy applied to systems that exchange heat and work

correct_answer: the conservation of energy applied to systems that exchange heat and work
explanation: By recognising heat as a form of energy transfer, the first law simply says that energy is conserved in any thermodynamic process. It puts no restriction on the direction of a process.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics
tags: Physical content of the first law

subject: Physics
question: An ideal gas is compressed isothermally and 150 J of work is done on it by the piston. During this process the gas:

options.A: neither absorbs nor rejects heat, since the temperature is constant
options.B: absorbs 150 J of heat from the surroundings
options.C: rejects 75 J of heat to the surroundings
options.D: rejects 150 J of heat to the surroundings

correct_answer: rejects 150 J of heat to the surroundings
explanation: For an isothermal change of an ideal gas dU = 0, hence dQ = dW. Work done on the gas means dW = minus 150 J, so dQ = minus 150 J and the gas rejects 150 J of heat.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A diatomic ideal gas with gamma = 1.4 is heated at constant pressure. The fraction of the heat supplied that leaves the gas as work is:
explanation: The work done is n R dT and the heat supplied is n Cp dT. Since Cp = gamma R divided by (gamma minus 1), the ratio is (gamma minus 1) divided by gamma = 0.4 divided by 1.4 = 2/7.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: Direct use of the first law
question: A gas absorbs 200 J of heat and does 120 J of work on its surroundings. The change in the internal energy of the gas is:
explanation: Here dQ = plus 200 J and dW = plus 120 J, so dU = 200 minus 120 = plus 80 J. The internal energy of the gas increases by 80 J.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: First law for an adiabatic process
question: For a gas expanding adiabatically, the first law gives:

options.A: no change in internal energy, since no heat is exchanged
options.B: a fall in internal energy equal in magnitude to the work done by the gas
options.C: a fall in internal energy equal in magnitude to the heat absorbed
options.D: a rise in internal energy equal in magnitude to the work done by the gas

correct_answer: a fall in internal energy equal in magnitude to the work done by the gas
explanation: With dQ = 0 the first law becomes 0 = dU + dW, that is dU = minus dW. In an expansion dW is positive, so dU is negative and the gas cools; the work done comes entirely from the store of internal energy.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics
tags: First law for an adiabatic process

subject: Physics
question: A gas at 2 × 10⁵ Pa occupying 3 × 10⁻³ m³ is first expanded at constant pressure to 5 × 10⁻³ m³. Its pressure is then lowered at constant volume until the internal energy returns to its original value. For the two stages taken together, the heat absorbed by the gas is:
explanation: Work in the first stage is 2 × 10⁵ x (5 minus 3) × 10⁻³ = 400 J. No work is done in the second stage since the volume is fixed. The internal energy ends where it began, so dU total is zero and dQ total = 0 plus 400 = 400 J.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A block of ice is melted at constant pressure. During melting the substance contracts in volume. For the ice water system during this change,:

options.A: the internal energy falls, since work is done on the system by the atmosphere
options.B: the internal energy does not change, since the temperature stays constant
options.C: the increase in internal energy is slightly less than the heat absorbed
options.D: the increase in internal energy is slightly greater than the heat absorbed

correct_answer: the increase in internal energy is slightly greater than the heat absorbed
explanation: Melting ice contracts, so dV is negative and dW = P dV is negative: the atmosphere does work on the system. Then dU = dQ minus dW = dQ plus a small positive amount, so the internal energy rises by slightly more than the heat absorbed.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: Two moles of a monatomic ideal gas in a rigid vessel are supplied 1245 J of heat. Taking R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, the rise in temperature of the gas is:
explanation: Since the vessel is rigid, all the heat raises the internal energy. So 1245 = (3/2) × 2 × 8.3 x dT = 24.9 dT, giving dT = 1245 divided by 24.9 = 50 K.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: First law for an isochoric process
question: When heat is supplied to a gas held in a rigid closed vessel, the first law reduces to:
explanation: A rigid vessel keeps the volume fixed, so dV is zero and no work is done. The first law dQ = dU + dW then becomes dQ = dU, and all the heat supplied raises the internal energy.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics
tags: First law for an isochoric process

subject: Physics
question: The barrel of a bicycle pump becomes noticeably warm when air inside it is pumped rapidly. The best explanation is that:

options.A: the air is compressed isothermally, so the heat produced is passed to the barrel
options.B: the air is compressed almost adiabatically, so the work done on it raises its internal energy
options.C: the air expands adiabatically, so its internal energy is converted into heat
options.D: friction at the piston is the only source of the heating, the gas playing no part

correct_answer: the air is compressed almost adiabatically, so the work done on it raises its internal energy
explanation: Pumping quickly gives the gas no time to exchange heat with the surroundings, so the process is nearly adiabatic. Work is done on the gas, making dW negative, so dU = minus dW is positive and the temperature of the trapped air rises.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: State and path quantities in the first law
question: In the relation dQ = dU + dW applied to a process between two fixed states,:

options.A: all three of dQ, dU and dW have the same value for every path
options.B: dU has the same value for every path, while dQ and dW depend on the path
options.C: dW has the same value for every path, while dQ and dU depend on the path
options.D: dQ has the same value for every path, while dU and dW depend on the path

correct_answer: dU has the same value for every path, while dQ and dW depend on the path
explanation: Whatever route is taken between two given states, the change in internal energy is the same. The heat absorbed and the work done individually vary with the route, though their difference dQ minus dW always equals the same dU.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics
tags: State and path quantities in the first law

subject: Physics
question: Which of the following cannot be decided using the first law of thermodynamics alone?

options.A: The change in internal energy of a gas between two given states
options.B: Whether a given process will actually take place in a particular direction
options.C: The work done by a gas when the heat absorbed and the internal energy change are known
options.D: The heat that must be supplied to produce a given change of state and work output

correct_answer: Whether a given process will actually take place in a particular direction
explanation: Energy conservation is satisfied both by heat flowing from hot to cold and by the reverse. The first law therefore cannot rule out the reverse process, and a separate principle, the second law, is needed to fix the direction.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: Match the process with the term that vanishes in dQ = dU + dW. In an isochoric process, an isothermal process of an ideal gas and an adiabatic process, the vanishing terms are respectively:
explanation: A rigid container makes the volume constant, so no work is done and dW = 0. A constant temperature process of an ideal gas leaves the internal energy unchanged, so dU = 0. An adiabatic process is defined by the absence of heat exchange, so dQ = 0.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A gas is taken round a closed cycle. During the cycle it absorbs 900 J of heat from a hot source and rejects 600 J to a cold sink. Over one complete cycle,:

options.A: the internal energy increases by 300 J and the net work done by the gas is zero
options.B: the internal energy is unchanged and the net work done by the gas is 1500 J
options.C: the internal energy is unchanged and the net work done by the gas is 300 J
options.D: the internal energy decreases by 600 J and the net work done by the gas is 900 J

correct_answer: the internal energy is unchanged and the net work done by the gas is 300 J
explanation: Since the gas returns to its initial state, the change in internal energy over the cycle is zero. The first law then gives net work = net heat = 900 minus 600 = 300 J done by the gas.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: Isobaric heating of a monatomic gas
question: One mole of a monatomic ideal gas is heated at constant pressure from 300 K to 400 K. Taking R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, the heat supplied and the work done by the gas are respectively:
explanation: With n = 1 and dT = 100 K, n R dT = 8.3 × 100 = 830 J. Hence the work done is 830 J, the rise in internal energy is (3/2) × 830 = 1245 J and the heat supplied is 830 + 1245 = 2075 J.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: First law for an isothermal process
question: For an ideal gas taken through an isothermal process, the first law reduces to:
explanation: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature. In an isothermal process the temperature is fixed, so dU = 0 and the first law gives dQ = dW: all the heat absorbed leaves as work.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A gas absorbs 500 J of heat while doing 200 J of work, then rejects 150 J of heat while 250 J of work is done on it, and is finally brought back to its original state by a third stage carried out at constant volume. The heat exchanged during the third stage is:
explanation: Stage one gives dU1 = 500 minus 200 = 300 J. Stage two gives dU2 = minus 150 minus (minus 250) = plus 100 J. So the internal energy has risen by 400 J. For the cycle to close, the third stage must give dU3 = minus 400 J, and since the volume is fixed no work is done, so dQ3 = minus 400 J, that is 400 J of heat is rejected.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: During a process the internal energy of a gas rises by 500 J while the gas does 300 J of work on its surroundings. The heat supplied to the gas is:
explanation: The heat supplied must cover both destinations of energy, so dQ = 500 + 300 = 800 J.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A system absorbs 500 J of heat and does 200 J of work on its surroundings. The change in internal energy is:
explanation: Using ΔQ = ΔU + W for work done by the system, ΔU = 500 - (200) = 300 J.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A system absorbs 250 J of heat and does -50 J of work on its surroundings. The change in internal energy is:
explanation: Using ΔQ = ΔU + W for work done by the system, ΔU = 250 - (-50) = 300 J.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A system absorbs 300 J of heat and does 100 J of work on its surroundings. The change in internal energy is:
explanation: Using ΔQ = ΔU + W for work done by the system, ΔU = 300 - (100) = 200 J.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: Internal energy of a monatomic gas
question: Two moles of a monatomic ideal gas are heated from 300 K to 400 K. Taking R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, the increase in the internal energy of the gas is:
explanation: Here n = 2 and dT = 100 K, so dU = (3/2) × 2 × 8.3 × 100 = 3 × 830 = 2490 J. The result is the same whatever process is used, since internal energy depends only on temperature.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
subtopic: Internal energy as a state function
question: The internal energy of a thermodynamic system is called a state function because:

options.A: it is always equal to the heat supplied to the system in every process
options.B: it can be measured directly with a thermometer for any system
options.C: it always keeps the same value while the system passes through any process
options.D: its value is fixed by the present state of the system and not by the way that state was reached

correct_answer: its value is fixed by the present state of the system and not by the way that state was reached
explanation: For a system taken from one state to another by different routes, the change in internal energy is the same for every route. That is precisely what is meant by calling internal energy a state function.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: Work in a two step process
question: A gas at a constant pressure of 2 × 10⁵ Pa expands from 2 × 10⁻³ m³ to 5 × 10⁻³ m³. It is then compressed at a constant pressure of 1 × 10⁵ Pa back to 2 × 10⁻³ m³. The net work done by the gas is:
explanation: First stage: W1 = 2 × 10⁵ x (5 minus 2) × 10⁻³ = 600 J. Second stage: W2 = 1 × 10⁵ x (2 minus 5) × 10⁻³ = minus 300 J. Net work = 600 minus 300 = 300 J done by the gas.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics
tags: Work in a two step process

subject: Physics
question: A system gives out 300 J of heat while 500 J of work is done on it by the surroundings. The internal energy of the system:
explanation: Heat rejected gives dQ = minus 300 J. Work done on the system gives dW = minus 500 J. Then dU = dQ minus dW = minus 300 minus (minus 500) = plus 200 J, so the internal energy rises by 200 J.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: In the convention used with the first law of thermodynamics, the work associated with a gas that expands against an external pressure is:

options.A: zero, because the pressure of the gas does not change during the expansion
options.B: negative, because the gas loses energy while it expands
options.C: positive, because the gas does work on the surroundings
options.D: positive only if heat is supplied to the gas at the same time

correct_answer: positive, because the gas does work on the surroundings
explanation: Work done by a gas is the integral of P dV. When the volume increases, dV is positive, so dW is positive and the work is counted as done by the gas on the surroundings.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A gas kept at a constant pressure of 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa expands from a volume of 0.02 m³ to a volume of 0.05 m³. The work done by the gas is:
explanation: The change in volume is 0.05 minus 0.02, that is 0.03 m³. Then W = 1.5 × 10⁵ x 0.03 = 4.5 × 10³ J, so the gas does 4500 J of work.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: An insulated rigid container is divided by a partition. One half holds an ideal gas and the other half is evacuated. The partition is suddenly removed and the gas fills the whole container. For this process,:

options.A: the work done by the gas is zero and its temperature falls
options.B: the work done by the gas is zero and its temperature stays the same
options.C: the work done by the gas is P dV and its temperature rises
options.D: the work done by the gas is n R T ln 2 and its temperature falls

correct_answer: the work done by the gas is zero and its temperature stays the same
explanation: The gas expands into vacuum, so there is no opposing pressure and no work is done. The walls are insulating, so no heat enters. From the first law dU = dQ minus dW = 0, and since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, the temperature is unchanged.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: Internal energy of an ideal gas
question: For a fixed mass of an ideal gas, the internal energy depends on:
explanation: There is no intermolecular potential energy in an ideal gas, so the whole internal energy is molecular kinetic energy, which is fixed by temperature. Hence U depends only on T for a given amount of gas.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: Heat on a straight line path
question: One mole of a monatomic ideal gas is taken along a straight line on a pressure volume diagram from the state with pressure 1 × 10⁵ Pa and volume 1 × 10⁻³ m³ to the state with pressure 2 × 10⁵ Pa and volume 2 × 10⁻³ m³. The heat absorbed by the gas is:
explanation: The area under the straight line is the mean pressure times the change in volume, that is (1 × 10⁵ plus 2 × 10⁵)/2 × 1 × 10⁻³ = 150 J. The products of pressure and volume are 100 J initially and 400 J finally, so dU = (3/2)(400 minus 100) = 450 J. Hence dQ = 450 plus 150 = 600 J.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics
tags: Heat on a straight line path

subject: Physics
question: One mole of a monatomic ideal gas is heated at constant pressure. The fraction of the supplied heat that appears as work done by the gas is:
explanation: For a temperature rise dT of one mole, the work done is R dT and the heat supplied is (5/2) R dT. The ratio is R dT divided by (5/2) R dT, which is 2/5. This equals (gamma minus 1) divided by gamma with gamma = 5/3.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A gas at pressure P expands slowly by a small volume dV. The small amount of work done by the gas is:
explanation: If the piston of area A moves out through a small distance dx, the gas exerts force P A on it, so the work is P A dx. Since A dx is the small volume change dV, the work done is P dV.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A gas is compressed while at the same time it gives out heat to its surroundings. In the convention used with dQ = dU + dW, the signs are:
explanation: Heat leaving the system makes dQ negative. Compression means dV is negative, so dW, which equals P dV, is also negative. Then dU = dQ minus dW can still be positive if the magnitude of the work done on the gas exceeds the heat lost.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: Two paths between the same states
question: A gas is carried from state X to state Y along two different paths. Along the first path it absorbs 600 J of heat and does 200 J of work. Along the second path it does 500 J of work. The heat absorbed along the second path is:
explanation: Along the first path, dU = 600 minus 200 = 400 J. The same 400 J change occurs along the second path, since the end states are identical. Hence the heat absorbed along the second path is 400 plus 500 = 900 J.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A gas is taken from one given state to another given state. Which of the following depends on the particular route followed?

options.A: The change in the pressure of the gas
options.B: The change in the internal energy of the gas
options.C: The change in the temperature of the gas
options.D: The work done by the gas

correct_answer: The work done by the gas
explanation: Work equals the area under the path drawn on a pressure volume diagram, and different routes between the same end points enclose different areas. All of pressure, volume, temperature and internal energy are fixed once the state is fixed, so only the work is route dependent.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: Internal energy change by two routes
question: Two moles of an ideal gas are taken from 300 K to 500 K, once at constant volume and once at constant pressure. The change in internal energy:

options.A: is larger in the constant pressure case, since more heat has to be supplied there
options.B: is the same in the two cases, since internal energy depends only on temperature
options.C: is larger in the constant volume case, since no work is done there
options.D: is zero in the constant pressure case, since the gas expands as it is heated

correct_answer: is the same in the two cases, since internal energy depends only on temperature
explanation: In both cases the temperature rises by 200 K for the same two moles of gas, so dU = n Cv dT is the same. The processes differ in the heat supplied, since at constant pressure part of the heat leaves as work, but the change in internal energy is identical.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics
tags: Internal energy change by two routes

subject: Physics
question: In thermodynamics, heat is best described as:

options.A: the energy that must be supplied to raise the temperature of unit mass by one kelvin
options.B: the total energy stored in the random motion of the molecules of a system
options.C: the energy a system possesses because of its pressure and volume
options.D: energy in transit between a system and its surroundings because of a temperature difference

correct_answer: energy in transit between a system and its surroundings because of a temperature difference
explanation: Heat exists only while it is crossing a boundary. Once it has entered the system it becomes part of the internal energy, so a body cannot be said to contain a certain amount of heat.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: For a gas taken from one state to another, the area under the path drawn on a pressure volume diagram represents:

options.A: the heat absorbed by the gas
options.B: the change in internal energy of the gas
options.C: the change in temperature of the gas
options.D: the work done by the gas

correct_answer: the work done by the gas
explanation: Since the work done in a small step is P dV, adding the strips of width dV and height P gives the whole area under the path, which is therefore the work done by the gas.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: Two routes between the same states
question: A gas is taken from the state with pressure 3 × 10⁵ Pa and volume 1 × 10⁻³ m³ to the state with pressure 1 × 10⁵ Pa and volume 3 × 10⁻³ m³ by two routes. Route X is an expansion at the constant pressure 3 × 10⁵ Pa followed by a fall of pressure at constant volume. Route Y is a fall of pressure at constant volume followed by an expansion at the constant pressure 1 × 10⁵ Pa. The heat absorbed along route X exceeds that along route Y by:
explanation: Along route X the work is 3 × 10⁵ x 2 × 10⁻³ = 600 J, the constant volume stage contributing nothing. Along route Y the work is 1 × 10⁵ x 2 × 10⁻³ = 200 J. Since the end states are the same, dU is common, so the heat difference equals 600 minus 200 = 400 J.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: On a pressure volume diagram with pressure on the vertical axis, a stage of a cycle appears as a vertical straight line segment. During this stage,:

options.A: the work done is the largest of all the stages, since the pressure changes most
options.B: no work is done, since the volume does not change
options.C: no work is done, since the pressure does not change
options.D: the work done equals the product of the volume and the change in pressure

correct_answer: no work is done, since the volume does not change
explanation: A vertical segment has a fixed volume, so dV = 0 at every point and the area under it is zero. Hence the work done during that stage is zero, however large the pressure change may be.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: Heat in a constant volume stage
question: During one stage of a cycle, a monatomic ideal gas kept at a fixed volume of 1 × 10⁻³ m³ has its pressure raised from 1 × 10⁵ Pa to 3 × 10⁵ Pa. The heat supplied to the gas during this stage is:
explanation: The change in the product of pressure and volume is (3 × 10⁵ minus 1 × 10⁵) × 1 × 10⁻³ = 200 J, and this equals n R dT. For a monatomic gas dU = (3/2) n R dT = 300 J, and since no work is done the heat supplied is 300 J.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A cycle traced in the clockwise sense on a pressure volume diagram corresponds to:

options.A: net work done by the gas on the surroundings
options.B: no net work, since the gas returns to its starting state
options.C: net work done on the gas by the surroundings
options.D: net heat rejected exactly equal to the net heat absorbed

correct_answer: net work done by the gas on the surroundings
explanation: In a clockwise loop the upper branch is the expansion and the lower branch is the compression. The gas therefore does more work while expanding than is done on it while being compressed, so the net work is positive and equal to the enclosed area.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: For a gas taken round a closed loop on a pressure volume diagram, the area enclosed by the loop is equal in magnitude to:

options.A: the sum of the heat absorbed and the heat rejected during the cycle
options.B: the heat absorbed from the hot reservoir during the cycle
options.C: the net work done during the cycle
options.D: the net change in internal energy during the cycle

correct_answer: the net work done during the cycle
explanation: The work along the outward branch is the area under it and the work along the return branch is the area under that branch taken with the opposite sign. The difference is the area enclosed by the loop, which is the net work.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A gas is expanded between the same two volumes along two different paths on a pressure volume diagram. Path X lies entirely above path Y. The work done by the gas is:

options.A: greater along path X, since the area under it is larger
options.B: greater along path X only if the gas absorbs heat along it
options.C: greater along path Y, since the pressure is lower and the gas expands more easily
options.D: the same along both paths, since the volume limits are the same

correct_answer: greater along path X, since the area under it is larger
explanation: Between the same volume limits, the area under the higher path is larger at every value of the volume. Hence the gas does more work along path X than along path Y, even though both start and end at the same volumes.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: A gas is taken clockwise round a rectangular cycle on a pressure volume diagram in which the pressure varies between 1 × 10⁵ Pa and 3 × 10⁵ Pa and the volume varies between 2 × 10⁻³ m³ and 5 × 10⁻³ m³. The net work done by the gas per cycle is:
explanation: The pressure range is 2 × 10⁵ Pa and the volume range is 3 × 10⁻³ m³. The enclosed area is 2 × 10⁵ x 3 × 10⁻³ = 600 J, and since the traversal is clockwise this work is done by the gas.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
subtopic: Total heat absorbed in a cycle
question: One sample of a monatomic ideal gas is taken clockwise round a rectangular cycle whose corners are at pressures 1 × 10⁵ Pa and 3 × 10⁵ Pa and volumes 1 × 10⁻³ m³ and 3 × 10⁻³ m³. The total heat absorbed by the gas during those stages in which it takes in heat is:
explanation: The four corner values of the product of pressure and volume are 100 J, 300 J, 900 J and 300 J. Heating at the fixed smaller volume gives dQ = (3/2)(300 minus 100) = 300 J. Expansion at 3 × 10⁵ Pa gives dU = (3/2)(900 minus 300) = 900 J and W = 600 J, so dQ = 1500 J. The other two stages both reject heat. Hence the total heat taken in is 300 plus 1500 = 1800 J.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: When a gas is taken round a complete cycle and returns to its starting state, the change in its internal energy over the cycle is:

options.A: zero, because internal energy is a state function
options.B: equal to the net work done by the gas
options.C: equal to the area enclosed by the cycle
options.D: equal to the heat absorbed from the source

correct_answer: zero, because internal energy is a state function
explanation: The gas ends in exactly the state it began in, with the same pressure, volume and temperature. Since internal energy depends only on the state, its change over the cycle is zero.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
question: A gas expands along a straight line on a pressure volume diagram from a pressure of 2 × 10⁵ Pa at a volume of 1 × 10⁻³ m³ to a pressure of 1 × 10⁵ Pa at a volume of 3 × 10⁻³ m³. The work done by the gas is:
explanation: The mean pressure is (2 × 10⁵ plus 1 × 10⁵) divided by 2 = 1.5 × 10⁵ Pa and the volume increases by 2 × 10⁻³ m³. Hence W = 1.5 × 10⁵ x 2 × 10⁻³ = 300 J.

subject: Physics
question: In one complete cycle a gas absorbs 1000 J of heat and does 400 J of net work on its surroundings. The heat rejected by the gas during the cycle is:
explanation: Since the internal energy returns to its starting value, 1000 minus Q rejected = 400. Hence the heat rejected is 600 J.

subject: Physics
subtopic: What must vanish over a cycle
question: For a gas taken round any complete cycle, which quantity is necessarily zero?

options.A: The net heat exchanged with the surroundings
options.C: The heat rejected to the cold reservoir
options.D: The net work done by the gas

explanation: Internal energy is a state function, so after a complete cycle it returns to its original value and its change is zero. Heat and work are path functions, and for a loop of finite area both the net heat and the net work are non zero and equal to each other.

subject: Physics
question: A cyclic heat engine cannot convert all the heat absorbed from a single reservoir into work because this would violate:
explanation: The Kelvin–Planck statement forbids a cyclic engine whose sole result is complete conversion of heat from one reservoir into work.

subject: Physics
question: System X is found to be in thermal equilibrium with system Z, and system Y is separately found to be in thermal equilibrium with the same system Z. Without bringing X and Y into contact, it can be stated that:

options.A: X and Y hold equal internal energies and therefore cannot exchange energy
options.B: X and Y are at the same temperature and no heat would flow if they were joined
options.C: heat would flow from X to Y if they were joined, since X reached equilibrium with Z first
options.D: X and Y are at the same temperature only if they are made of the same material

correct_answer: X and Y are at the same temperature and no heat would flow if they were joined
explanation: By the zeroth law, thermal equilibrium is transitive. X in equilibrium with Z and Y in equilibrium with Z together force X and Y to be in equilibrium, that is, to be at the same temperature, so joining them would produce no net heat flow.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: Which statement is the zeroth law of thermodynamics?

options.A: If two systems are each separately in thermal equilibrium with a third system, heat flows from the hotter of the two to the colder one.
options.B: If two systems are each separately in thermal equilibrium with a third system, then they are in thermal equilibrium with each other.
options.C: The heat supplied to a system equals the rise in its internal energy plus the work done by the system.
options.D: Heat cannot flow on its own from a colder body to a hotter body.

correct_answer: If two systems are each separately in thermal equilibrium with a third system, then they are in thermal equilibrium with each other.
explanation: The zeroth law states that if system X is in thermal equilibrium with system Z, and system Y is also in thermal equilibrium with Z, then X and Y are in thermal equilibrium with each other. This transitivity is what allows a single number, the temperature, to be attached to every system.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: Bodies X and Y are placed in thermal contact and heat is observed to flow from X to Y. This observation shows that:

options.A: the specific heat capacity of X is greater than that of Y
options.B: the temperature of X is higher than the temperature of Y
options.C: the mass of X is greater than the mass of Y
options.D: the internal energy of X is greater than the internal energy of Y

correct_answer: the temperature of X is higher than the temperature of Y
explanation: Spontaneous heat flow is governed only by the temperature difference. Since heat flows from X to Y, X must be at the higher temperature. Nothing can be concluded about masses or internal energies from this single observation.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: Block X of mass 2 kg and block Y of mass 1 kg are made of the same metal. X is at 300 K and Y is at 320 K. They are brought into thermal contact and isolated from the surroundings. Which statement is correct?

options.A: No heat flows, because the products of mass and temperature are nearly equal for the two blocks.
options.B: Heat flows from Y to X until the two blocks hold equal internal energies.
options.C: Heat flows from Y to X, even though X may hold the larger internal energy.
options.D: Heat flows from X to Y, because X holds the larger internal energy.

correct_answer: Heat flows from Y to X, even though X may hold the larger internal energy.
explanation: Y is at the higher temperature of 320 K, so heat flows from Y to X. For the same metal, internal energy is proportional to mass times temperature, so X with 2 kg at 300 K holds more energy than Y with 1 kg at 320 K, yet it still receives heat. Flow stops when both reach a common temperature between 300 K and 320 K.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: Two gas samples occupy two chambers separated by a fixed wall that lets the samples settle to a common temperature but does not let any gas cross. Such a wall is described as:
explanation: Since the two samples reach a common temperature, energy must be able to cross the wall, so the wall is diathermic. Since no matter crosses and the chambers keep fixed volumes, the wall is also rigid and non porous.

subject: Physics
question: Two moles of a monatomic ideal gas labelled X and one mole of a diatomic ideal gas labelled Y occupy two chambers separated by a rigid diathermic wall. Both samples are at 300 K. Take R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Which statement is correct?

options.A: There is no net heat flow, although the internal energy of X, about 7470 J, exceeds that of Y, about 6225 J.
options.B: Heat flows from Y to X, because each molecule of Y carries more energy than each molecule of X.
options.C: Heat flows from X to Y, because the internal energy of X is larger than that of Y.
options.D: There is no net heat flow, because the two samples hold equal internal energies at 300 K.

correct_answer: There is no net heat flow, although the internal energy of X, about 7470 J, exceeds that of Y, about 6225 J.
explanation: For X, U = (3/2) × 2 × 8.3 × 300 = 7470 J. For Y, U = (5/2) × 1 × 8.3 × 300 = 6225 J. The internal energies differ, yet both samples sit at 300 K, so the temperature difference is zero and no net heat crosses the diathermic wall.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: Two bodies in thermal contact are found to be in thermal equilibrium. Which quantity is necessarily the same for the two bodies?

options.C: The total heat stored in them

explanation: Thermal equilibrium is signalled by the absence of any net heat exchange between the bodies. The single property whose equality guarantees this is temperature, so the temperatures of the two bodies must be equal.

subject: Physics
question: A clinical thermometer is kept in contact with a patient and read only after the mercury column stops moving. The reading is taken as the temperature of the patient. This procedure is justified by:
explanation: Waiting until the column stops means the thermometer has reached thermal equilibrium with the patient. By the zeroth law, since the thermometer is also in equilibrium with its own calibrated scale, the scale reading equals the patient temperature.

subject: Physics
question: The zeroth law of thermodynamics makes it logically possible to define:

options.A: temperature, as a property whose equality decides thermal equilibrium
options.B: heat, as the energy transferred because of a temperature difference
options.C: efficiency, as the fraction of absorbed heat converted into work
options.D: internal energy, as a function of the state of a system alone

correct_answer: temperature, as a property whose equality decides thermal equilibrium
explanation: Because thermal equilibrium is transitive, all systems in equilibrium with one another can be given one common label. That label is temperature. Hence the zeroth law is the basis of the very concept of temperature.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
question: A sample of 1 kg of water at 50° celsius is brought into contact with a sample of 100 g of water at 50° celsius. Which statement describes what happens?

options.A: Heat flows from the 100 g sample to the 1 kg sample until the energy per unit mass becomes equal.
options.B: There is no net exchange of heat, because both samples are at the same temperature.
options.C: Heat flows from the 1 kg sample to the 100 g sample, because it holds more heat energy.
options.D: Heat flows from the 1 kg sample until the two samples hold equal internal energies.

correct_answer: There is no net exchange of heat, because both samples are at the same temperature.
explanation: Both samples are at 50° celsius, so the temperature difference driving heat flow is zero. Even though the 1 kg sample contains ten times the internal energy of the 100 g sample, there is no net transfer of energy between them.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Adiabatic compression of a diatomic gas
question: A diatomic ideal gas with gamma = 1.4 is compressed adiabatically until its volume becomes one thirty second of the original value. The pressure of the gas becomes:
explanation: The volume ratio is 32, so P2 divided by P1 = 32¹.4. Writing 32 as 2⁵ gives 2^(5 × 1.4) = 2⁷ = 128. Hence the pressure becomes 128 times the original value.

subject: Physics
question: A gas expands at a constant pressure P from volume V1 to volume V2. The work done by the gas is:

options.B: P V2 minus P V2 divided by 2
options.C: 2.303 P V1 log (V2 divided by V1)

explanation: Since P is constant it comes out of the integral, giving W = P times the change in volume, that is P (V2 minus V1). On a pressure volume diagram this is the rectangular area under the horizontal path.

subtopic: Adiabatic relation between P and V
question: For a quasi static adiabatic change of an ideal gas, the pressure and the volume are related by:
explanation: Combining dU = minus dW for an adiabatic change with the ideal gas equation gives P V^gamma = constant, where gamma is the ratio of the two principal molar heat capacities.
