subtopic: Adiabatic compression of a monatomic gas
question: A monatomic ideal gas at 300 K is compressed adiabatically until its volume becomes one eighth of the original value. Taking gamma = 5/3, the final temperature is:
explanation: Here V1 divided by V2 is 8 and gamma minus 1 is 2/3, so the temperature ratio is 8²⁄³ = 4. Hence T2 = 300 × 4 = 1200 K.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Isothermal relation between P and V
question: For a fixed mass of an ideal gas held at constant temperature, the pressure volume curve is:

options.A: a vertical straight line, since the volume does not change
options.B: a horizontal straight line, since the pressure does not change
options.C: a rectangular hyperbola, since P V is constant
options.D: a straight line through the origin, since P is proportional to V

correct_answer: a rectangular hyperbola, since P V is constant
explanation: At constant temperature the ideal gas equation gives P V = constant, so P varies as the reciprocal of V. A graph of P against V is therefore a rectangular hyperbola.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Adiabatic work with a general gamma
question: A gas for which gamma = 1.5 expands adiabatically from a pressure of 8 × 10⁵ Pa and a volume of 1 × 10⁻³ m³ to a volume of 4 × 10⁻³ m³. The work done by the gas is:
explanation: The volume ratio is 4, so the pressure falls by a factor 4¹.5 = 8, giving P2 = 1 × 10⁵ Pa. Then P1 V1 = 800 J and P2 V2 = 1 × 10⁵ x 4 × 10⁻³ = 400 J. The work is (800 minus 400) divided by 0.5 = 800 J.

subject: Physics
question: For a gas to undergo a nearly isothermal change, it should be:

options.A: kept in a thin walled conducting vessel and made to change very slowly
options.B: kept in a thick walled insulating vessel and made to change very slowly
options.C: kept in a thin walled conducting vessel and made to change very rapidly
options.D: kept in a thick walled insulating vessel and made to change very rapidly

correct_answer: kept in a thin walled conducting vessel and made to change very slowly
explanation: To hold the temperature fixed, heat must flow freely between the gas and its surroundings. This calls for thin conducting walls, and the change must be slow enough for that exchange to keep pace.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
subtopic: Adiabatic relation between P and T
question: For an adiabatic change of an ideal gas, the correct relation between pressure and temperature is:
explanation: From the gas equation V is proportional to T divided by P. Substituting into P V^gamma = constant gives P (T divided by P)^gamma = constant, that is P^(1 minus gamma) T^gamma = constant.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Heat capacity in an isothermal change
question: For an isothermal change of an ideal gas, the molar heat capacity is:

options.A: equal to R, since the whole of the heat appears as work
options.B: zero, since the internal energy of the gas does not change
options.C: equal to Cp minus Cv, since pressure and volume both change
options.D: infinite, since heat is exchanged with no change in temperature

correct_answer: infinite, since heat is exchanged with no change in temperature
explanation: In an isothermal change of an ideal gas the whole of the heat absorbed leaves as work, so dQ is not zero, while dT is zero. The ratio dQ divided by n dT therefore has no finite value and the molar heat capacity is said to be infinite.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subtopic: Adiabatic relation between T and V
question: For an adiabatic change of an ideal gas, the temperature and the volume are related by:
explanation: Write P = n R T divided by V and put it into P V^gamma = constant. The volume powers combine to give T V^(gamma minus 1) = constant for a fixed amount of gas.

subject: Physics
question: One mole of a monatomic ideal gas expands adiabatically and its temperature falls from 400 K to 300 K. Taking R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and gamma = 5/3, the work done by the gas is:
explanation: Here gamma minus 1 = 2/3, so the work is 1 × 8.3 × 100 divided by (2/3) = 830 × 1.5 = 1245 J. This equals the fall in internal energy, as it must when no heat is exchanged.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
question: A gas in a cylinder is compressed so quickly that there is no time for heat exchange with the surroundings. This compression is best described as:

options.A: adiabatic, with the temperature of the gas staying constant
options.B: adiabatic, with the temperature of the gas rising
options.C: isothermal, with the temperature of the gas staying constant
options.D: isobaric, with the pressure of the gas staying constant

correct_answer: adiabatic, with the temperature of the gas rising
explanation: With no time for heat exchange, dQ = 0 and the process is adiabatic. Work is done on the gas, so dW is negative and dU = minus dW is positive, meaning the internal energy and hence the temperature rise.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: An isothermal curve and an adiabatic curve for the same gas are drawn through a common point on a pressure volume diagram. Near that point,:

options.A: the isothermal curve is steeper than the adiabatic curve
options.B: the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve
options.C: the isothermal curve is steeper only for a monatomic gas
options.D: the two curves have the same slope, since both pass through the same state

correct_answer: the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve
explanation: Differentiating P V = constant gives a slope of minus P divided by V. Differentiating P V^gamma = constant gives a slope of minus gamma P divided by V. Since gamma exceeds one, the adiabatic curve falls more steeply at the common point.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: At the point where an isothermal curve and an adiabatic curve for the same ideal gas intersect on a pressure volume diagram, the ratio of the magnitude of the slope of the adiabatic curve to that of the isothermal curve is:
explanation: Differentiating P V = constant gives P dV + V dP = 0, so the isothermal slope is minus P divided by V. Differentiating P V^gamma = constant gives gamma P dV + V dP = 0, so the adiabatic slope is minus gamma P divided by V. At the common point P and V are shared, so the ratio of the magnitudes is gamma.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

subject: Physics
question: Starting from the same state, a fixed mass of ideal gas is expanded to the same final volume, once isothermally and once adiabatically. The work done by the gas is:

options.A: greater in the adiabatic expansion, since no heat has to be supplied to the gas
options.B: the same in the two cases, since the volume limits are the same
options.C: greater in the isothermal expansion, since the pressure stays higher throughout
options.D: greater in the adiabatic expansion, since the temperature of the gas falls

correct_answer: greater in the isothermal expansion, since the pressure stays higher throughout
explanation: From the common starting point, the adiabatic curve falls more steeply because its slope is gamma times as large in magnitude. Hence at every larger volume the adiabatic pressure is lower, the area under the adiabatic curve is smaller, and the isothermal expansion delivers more work.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 8: Thermodynamics

question: An adiabatic process is one in which:

options.A: no heat is exchanged between the system and its surroundings
options.B: the pressure of the system stays constant throughout
options.C: the internal energy of the system stays constant throughout
options.D: the temperature of the system stays constant throughout

subject: Physics
question: Two moles of an ideal gas are heated at constant pressure so that the temperature rises by 100 K. Taking R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, the work done by the gas is:
explanation: Using P V = n R T at constant pressure gives P dV = n R dT. Hence W = 2 × 8.3 × 100 = 1660 J. Note that the answer does not depend on whether the gas is monatomic or diatomic.

subject: Physics
question: One mole of a monatomic ideal gas at 300 K is compressed adiabatically until its volume is one eighth of the original. It is then cooled at constant volume back to 300 K. Taking R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ and gamma = 5/3, the heat rejected during the cooling stage is:
explanation: The adiabatic compression raises the temperature to 300 × 8²⁄³ = 300 × 4 = 1200 K. Cooling at constant volume from 1200 K to 300 K gives a drop of 900 K, so the heat rejected is (3/2) × 1 × 8.3 × 900 = 12.45 × 900 = 11205 J.

question: The work done by a gas during an isochoric change is:

options.A: equal to the change in the product of pressure and volume
options.B: equal to the heat supplied divided by the number of moles
options.C: zero, whatever the change in pressure
options.D: equal to V times the change in pressure

correct_answer: zero, whatever the change in pressure
explanation: With the volume held fixed, dV is zero at every stage, so the integral of P dV vanishes. The gas does no work however much its pressure and temperature change.

subject: Physics
question: When a tyre bursts, the air rushing out is found to be noticeably cooler than the air inside the tyre was. This happens because the escaping air:

options.A: expands isothermally and gives out heat to the surrounding air
options.B: is compressed adiabatically by the atmosphere outside the tyre
options.C: loses molecules of high speed first, so the average speed of those left falls
options.D: expands adiabatically and does work at the cost of its own internal energy

correct_answer: expands adiabatically and does work at the cost of its own internal energy
explanation: The escape is too fast for heat exchange, so dQ = 0. The air pushes back the atmosphere, making dW positive, so dU = minus dW is negative. The internal energy and hence the temperature of the escaping air fall.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Pressure change in an adiabatic expansion
question: A monatomic ideal gas with gamma = 5/3 expands adiabatically and its temperature falls from 400 K to 100 K. The final pressure of the gas is:

options.A: one thirty second of the initial pressure
options.B: one quarter of the initial pressure
options.C: one eighth of the initial pressure
options.D: one hundred and twenty eighth of the initial pressure

correct_answer: one thirty second of the initial pressure
explanation: From T V^(gamma minus 1) = constant with gamma minus 1 = 2/3, the volume ratio is (T1 divided by T2) raised to the power 3/2, that is 4³⁄² = 8. Then from P V = n R T, the pressure ratio is (T2 divided by T1) times (V1 divided by V2) = (1/4) × (1/8) = 1/32.

subject: Physics

subject: Physics
question: According to the kinetic theory of gases, the collisions of gas molecules with one another and with the walls of the container are:

options.A: perfectly inelastic, so that the molecules move together after collision
options.B: perfectly elastic, so that the total kinetic energy of the colliding molecules is conserved
options.C: elastic with the walls but inelastic among the molecules themselves
options.D: partially elastic, a small fraction of the kinetic energy being lost as heat in every collision

correct_answer: perfectly elastic, so that the total kinetic energy of the colliding molecules is conserved
explanation: Kinetic theory assumes that a gas molecule suffers no loss of kinetic energy in a collision. Momentum and kinetic energy are both conserved. This is why a gas kept at constant temperature in an insulated vessel maintains a steady pressure indefinitely; if any energy were lost per collision the pressure would keep decreasing.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
question: Kinetic theory assumes that the time taken for one collision is negligible compared with the time between two successive collisions. The direct consequence of this assumption is that:

options.A: the pressure on the wall is produced only during the free flight
options.B: the molecules must all move with the same speed
options.C: the number of collisions per second becomes extremely small
options.D: a molecule spends almost all of its time in free straight line motion

correct_answer: a molecule spends almost all of its time in free straight line motion
explanation: If each collision lasts for a vanishingly small time, then almost the entire lifetime of a molecule is spent travelling freely in a straight line. This is what makes it meaningful to define a free path and a mean free path, and it also justifies calculating pressure as a sequence of instantaneous momentum transfers. The frequency of collisions can still be very large; a short duration does not mean a small number.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
question: For a large number of molecules of a gas in a closed container at rest, the average of the velocity vectors of all the molecules and the average of the squares of their speeds are respectively:

options.B: zero and a non zero positive quantity
options.C: a non zero positive quantity and zero
options.D: non zero and non zero, both directed along the container axis

correct_answer: zero and a non zero positive quantity
explanation: Molecular motion is completely random, so for every molecule moving with a certain velocity there is on average another moving with the opposite velocity. The vector sum, and hence the average velocity, is zero for a container at rest. The square of a speed is always positive, so no cancellation is possible and the mean square speed is a definite positive number. That is exactly why pressure is written using the mean square speed and not the average velocity.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
question: In deriving the expression P = (1/3) ρ v_rms² for an ideal gas, the assumptions that are essential are that the collisions with the wall are elastic, that the molecular motion is random and isotropic, and that:

options.A: the collisions between molecules must be neglected altogether or the result changes
options.B: intermolecular forces are absent between collisions so that a molecule crosses the vessel at constant speed
options.C: the molecules all travel with the same speed equal to v_rms
options.D: the gas must be monatomic so that rotation cannot store energy

correct_answer: intermolecular forces are absent between collisions so that a molecule crosses the vessel at constant speed
explanation: The standard derivation follows one molecule bouncing between two opposite faces. Force free flight lets the transit time be written as twice the side length divided by the velocity component. Elastic collision at the wall makes the momentum change equal to twice the momentum component. Isotropy allows the mean square components along the three axes to be set equal, which produces the factor one third. A single common speed is never assumed; averaging over the distribution is what converts the sum of squared speeds into the mean square speed.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
question: A real gas behaves most nearly like an ideal gas at:
explanation: At low pressure the molecules are far apart, so their own volume is a negligible fraction of the vessel and the attractive forces are weak. At high temperature the average kinetic energy is large compared with the potential energy of attraction, so the attractive forces hardly affect the motion. Both requirements of the ideal gas model are therefore best satisfied at low pressure and high temperature.

subject: Physics
question: Between two successive collisions, a molecule of an ideal gas moves:

options.A: along a straight line with constant velocity
options.B: along a straight line but with continuously decreasing speed
options.C: in a random zig zag path even without collisions
options.D: along a curved path because of the mutual attraction of the other molecules

correct_answer: along a straight line with constant velocity
explanation: Kinetic theory neglects intermolecular forces except during the brief collision. With zero net force the acceleration is zero, so the molecule travels in a straight line at constant speed. The straight segment between two collisions is exactly what is called a free path, and its average value is the mean free path.

subject: Physics
question: The two corrections that must be applied to the ideal gas equation to describe a real gas arise because:

options.A: gravity acts on the molecules and makes the density non uniform
options.B: the molecules occupy a finite volume and they attract one another
options.C: the molecules move with different speeds and collide with the walls
options.D: the collisions between molecules are inelastic and the gas loses energy

correct_answer: the molecules occupy a finite volume and they attract one another
explanation: The ideal gas model assumes point molecules with no mutual force. A real molecule has a finite size, so the space available for motion is less than the vessel volume, which requires a volume correction. A real molecule also attracts its neighbours, so a molecule about to strike the wall is pulled back by the gas behind it and the measured pressure is smaller than the ideal value, which requires a pressure correction.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

question: The molar specific heat at constant volume of a gas is 20.75 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. Taking R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, the gas is:

options.A: non linear triatomic with gamma equal to 1.33

explanation: f = 2 × 20.75 / 8.3 = 41.5 / 8.3 = 5, so the molecule has five degrees of freedom and is a rigid diatomic. Then gamma = 1 + 2/5 = 1.40. Note that 20.75 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ is also the value of C_p for a monatomic gas, which is why the identification must be made from the definition and not from the number alone.

explanation: A diatomic molecule is a dumb bell. Its centre of mass can move along three independent directions, giving 3 translational modes. subject: Physics
subtopic: Temperature as a measure of energy
question: On the kinetic theory picture, the absolute zero of temperature is the temperature at which:

options.A: the density of the gas becomes zero
options.B: the pressure of the gas becomes maximum
options.C: the molecules move with the most probable speed
options.D: the average translational kinetic energy of the molecules becomes zero

correct_answer: the average translational kinetic energy of the molecules becomes zero
explanation: Because the average translational kinetic energy per molecule is directly proportional to the absolute temperature, it vanishes only when T = 0. Absolute zero is therefore the temperature at which the translational motion assumed by kinetic theory ceases, and it is why no lower temperature is possible on the Kelvin scale.

subject: Physics
question: The average translational kinetic energy of a molecule of an ideal gas at absolute temperature T is:
explanation: Each of the three translational degrees of freedom carries an average energy (1/2) k T by the law of equipartition. The total translational energy of one molecule is therefore 3 × (1/2) k T = (3/2) k T, and this value is the same for every ideal gas at a given temperature.

subject: Physics
question: A vessel contains 2 moles of helium and 3 moles of oxygen at 300 K. Taking R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, the total translational kinetic energy of the mixture is:
explanation: Translational energy per mole depends only on temperature, so both gases contribute (3/2) R T per mole. The total number of moles is 2 + 3 = 5. Energy = 1.5 × 5 × 8.3 × 300 = 1.5 × 12450 = 18675 J.

subject: Physics
question: The root mean square speed of the molecules of a gas at 250 K is doubled. The average translational kinetic energy per molecule and the final temperature are respectively:

options.A: four times the initial energy and 1000 K
options.B: two times the initial energy and 500 K
options.C: two times the initial energy and 1000 K
options.D: four times the initial energy and 500 K

correct_answer: four times the initial energy and 1000 K
explanation: Since the energy varies as the square of the speed, doubling v_rms makes the energy 2² = 4 times its original value. Because the energy is directly proportional to the absolute temperature, the temperature must also become 4 times, that is 4 × 250 = 1000 K.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

question: The total translational kinetic energy of a sample of gas at 200 K is 4.14 × 10⁻¹⁸ J. Taking k = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹, the number of molecules in the sample is:
explanation: Energy per molecule = 1.5 × 1.38 × 10⁻²³ x 200 = 4.14 × 10⁻²¹ J. Hence N = 4.14 × 10⁻¹⁸ / 4.14 × 10⁻²¹ = 1000 molecules.

question: A gas is at 27° celsius. The temperature to which it must be raised so that the average kinetic energy of its molecules is doubled is:
explanation: The initial absolute temperature is 27 + 273 = 300 K. To double the energy the absolute temperature must become 600 K. Converting back, 600 minus 273 = 327° celsius.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Combined change of n and d
question: The number density of a gas is reduced to one fourth of its initial value and, in a different sample, the effective molecular diameter is also halved. Taken together, these two changes make the mean free path:
explanation: Reducing n to one fourth multiplies λ by 4. Halving d divides d² by 4 and therefore multiplies λ by another 4. The combined factor is 4 × 4 = 16.

subject: Physics
question: Two gases have the same number density but the molecular diameter of the second is twice that of the first. The mean free path in the second gas compared with the first is:
explanation: The collision cross section is proportional to the square of the molecular diameter, and it appears in the denominator of λ = 1 / (√(2) π d² n). Doubling d multiplies d² by 4, so the mean free path falls to one fourth of its earlier value.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
subtopic: Combined change of T and P
question: The absolute temperature of a gas is doubled and at the same time its pressure is made four times the initial value. The mean free path of its molecules becomes:
explanation: The mean free path is proportional to T and inversely proportional to P. The combined factor is (T_new / T_old) × (P_old / P_new) = 2 × (1/4) = 1/2. Hence the mean free path falls to half its initial value.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
question: The mean free path of a molecule of a gas is:

options.A: the shortest distance a molecule can travel before it stops
options.B: the average distance between the walls of the container
options.C: the total distance travelled by a molecule in one second
options.D: the average distance travelled by a molecule between two successive collisions

correct_answer: the average distance travelled by a molecule between two successive collisions
explanation: Between two collisions a molecule travels a straight segment called a free path. These segments have different lengths, and their average value is the mean free path, usually written as λ. For air at room temperature and atmospheric pressure it is of the order of 10⁻⁷ m, far smaller than the size of any container.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
question: The pressure of a gas is doubled while the temperature is held constant. The mean free path of its molecules becomes:

options.B: unchanged, because the temperature has not changed
options.D: one fourth of its initial value

explanation: At constant temperature the number density is proportional to the pressure, so doubling P doubles n. Since λ varies inversely as n, the mean free path falls to half. The same follows directly from λ = k T / (√(2) π d² P) with T fixed.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
question: The mean free path of the molecules of a gas varies with the number of molecules per unit volume n as:

options.A: inversely proportional to the square of n

explanation: The more molecules there are in a given volume, the sooner a moving molecule meets one. In the standard expression λ = 1 / (√(2) π d² n), the number density appears in the denominator to the first power, so the mean free path is inversely proportional to n.

subject: Physics
question: The dimensions of the quantity ρ v_rms², where ρ is density and v_rms is the root mean square speed, are:
explanation: Density has dimensions M¹ L⁻³ and speed squared has dimensions L² T⁻². Their product is M¹ L⁻³ x L² T⁻² = M¹ L⁻¹ T⁻², which is exactly the dimensional formula of pressure. This confirms that P = (1/3) ρ v_rms² is dimensionally consistent, the numerical factor 1/3 being dimensionless.

subject: Physics
question: Two different gases are found to have the same pressure and the same density. Then:

options.A: their molecules have the same mass
options.B: their molecules have the same average kinetic energy
options.C: they are necessarily at the same temperature
options.D: their molecules have the same root mean square speed

correct_answer: their molecules have the same root mean square speed
explanation: Rearranging the pressure expression gives v_rms = √(3P / ρ). If both P and ρ are the same for the two gases, then v_rms must be the same. Nothing follows about the molecular mass, since a gas of heavy molecules can reach the same density with fewer molecules per unit volume, and nothing follows about temperature because v_rms = √(3RT/M) involves the molar mass as well.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
subtopic: Pressure in terms of number of molecules
question: For a gas containing N molecules each of mass m in a vessel of volume V, the kinetic theory expression for pressure is:
explanation: The density of the gas is the total mass N m divided by the volume V. Substituting ρ = N m / V into P = (1/3) ρ v_rms² gives P = (1/3) (N m / V) v_rms². The quantity N m / V has units kg m⁻³ and multiplying by the square of a speed gives Pa.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
subtopic: Link between pressure formula and v_rms
question: Starting from P = (1/3) ρ v_rms² and using the ideal gas equation for one mole, PV = RT, the root mean square speed is obtained as:

options.C: v_rms = √(3 R T / M), where M is the molar mass

correct_answer: v_rms = √(3 R T / M), where M is the molar mass
explanation: For one mole the density is ρ = M / V. Substituting gives P = (1/3)(M / V) v_rms², that is P V = (1/3) M v_rms². Since P V = R T for one mole, R T = (1/3) M v_rms², so v_rms² = 3 R T / M and v_rms = √(3 R T / M). The molar mass must be taken in kilogram per mole for SI units.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
subtopic: Pressure and kinetic energy per unit volume
question: If E is the translational kinetic energy of the molecules of an ideal gas per unit volume, then the pressure of the gas is:
explanation: Kinetic energy per unit volume is E = (1/2) ρ v_rms², so ρ v_rms² = 2E. Substituting in P = (1/3) ρ v_rms² gives P = (1/3) × 2E = (2/3) E. Equivalently the energy density is one and a half times the pressure.

subtopic: Pressure with changed molecule number and speed
question: A rigid vessel contains a gas at pressure P. Half the molecules are allowed to escape and the root mean square speed of the remaining molecules is then made twice its original value. The final pressure is:
explanation: With the volume and molecular mass unchanged, the pressure is proportional to the product of the number of molecules and the square of the root mean square speed. The number falls to one half and the square of the speed rises by a factor of 2² = 4. Hence P_final / P = (1/2) × 4 = 2, so the final pressure is 2P.

question: A gas at a pressure of 2 × 10⁵ Pa occupies a volume of 0.5 m³. The total translational kinetic energy of all its molecules is:
explanation: Energy per unit volume is (3/2)P, so the total translational kinetic energy in a volume V is (3/2) P V = 1.5 × 2 × 10⁵ x 0.5 = 1.5 × 10⁵ J. The same result follows from (3/2) n R T combined with P V = n R T.

subject: Physics
question: A fixed mass of gas is compressed to half its volume while the temperature is held constant. Using P = (1/3) ρ v_rms², the pressure:

options.A: becomes four times, because both the density and v_rms double
options.B: doubles, because v_rms doubles while the density stays the same
options.C: doubles, because the density doubles while v_rms stays the same
options.D: remains unchanged, because the number of molecules does not change

correct_answer: doubles, because the density doubles while v_rms stays the same
explanation: The root mean square speed depends only on temperature through v_rms = √(3RT/M), so an isothermal change leaves it unaltered. Halving the volume for a fixed mass doubles the density. Since P = (1/3) ρ v_rms² with v_rms fixed, the pressure doubles, which is exactly Boyle's law recovered from kinetic theory.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
subtopic: Origin of the factor one third
question: In the kinetic theory expression for pressure, the factor 1/3 arises because:

options.A: only one third of the molecules strike a given wall at any instant
options.B: a cube has three pairs of opposite faces and pressure acts on one pair
options.C: each molecule loses one third of its momentum at the wall
options.D: the mean square speed is shared equally among the three mutually perpendicular directions

correct_answer: the mean square speed is shared equally among the three mutually perpendicular directions
explanation: For any molecule the squared speed is the sum of the squares of its three velocity components. Because the motion is random and isotropic, the averages of the three squared components are equal, so each equals one third of the mean square speed. Only the component perpendicular to a wall contributes to the momentum transfer at that wall, and this introduces the factor 1/3 into the pressure expression.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
question: Hydrogen of molar mass 2 g mol⁻¹ and oxygen of molar mass 32 g mol⁻¹ are at the same temperature. The ratio of the root mean square speed of hydrogen to that of oxygen is:
explanation: The ratio is √(M_oxygen / M_hydrogen) = √(32 / 2) = √(16) = 4. So hydrogen molecules have a root mean square speed four times that of oxygen molecules at the same temperature.

subject: Physics
subtopic: Speed and energy in a mixture
question: Hydrogen of molar mass 2 g mol⁻¹ and oxygen of molar mass 32 g mol⁻¹ are mixed in a vessel and allowed to reach thermal equilibrium. For a hydrogen molecule compared with an oxygen molecule,:

options.A: both the root mean square speed and the average kinetic energy are 4 times larger
options.B: the root mean square speed is 16 times larger while the average kinetic energy is the same
options.C: the root mean square speed is 4 times larger while the average kinetic energy is the same
options.D: the root mean square speed is the same while the average kinetic energy is 16 times larger

correct_answer: the root mean square speed is 4 times larger while the average kinetic energy is the same
explanation: Thermal equilibrium means a common temperature, so every molecule of either gas has the same average translational kinetic energy (3/2)kT. Since (1/2) m v_rms² is the same for both, the speed ratio is √(32 / 2) = 4 in favour of hydrogen.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
question: Hydrogen and oxygen are kept at the same temperature. Compared with an oxygen molecule, a hydrogen molecule has:

options.A: a smaller root mean square speed because a lighter molecule carries less energy
options.B: a larger root mean square speed because hydrogen molecules are diatomic
options.C: a larger root mean square speed because v_rms varies inversely as the square root of molar mass
options.D: the same root mean square speed because the temperature is the same

correct_answer: a larger root mean square speed because v_rms varies inversely as the square root of molar mass
explanation: At the same temperature every molecule has the same average translational kinetic energy (3/2)kT. Since this equals (1/2) m v_rms², a smaller mass must be balanced by a larger speed. Numerically v_rms is proportional to 1 / √(M), and hydrogen with molar mass 2 g mol⁻¹ is far lighter than oxygen with 32 g mol⁻¹.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
question: The molecules of a gas at 200 K have a root mean square speed of 400 m s⁻¹. Take k = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹. At 800 K the root mean square speed of the same molecules is:
explanation: The molecular mass is unchanged, so v_rms is proportional to √(T). The temperature ratio is 800 / 200 = 4, giving a speed ratio of √(4) = 2. The new speed is 2 × 400 = 800 m s⁻¹. The value of the Boltzmann constant is not needed for a ratio question.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
question: At what temperature will the root mean square speed of oxygen molecules of molar mass 32 g mol⁻¹ equal the root mean square speed of hydrogen molecules of molar mass 2 g mol⁻¹ kept at 300 K?
explanation: Setting 3 R T_oxygen / 32 = 3 R x 300 / 2 gives T_oxygen / 32 = 300 / 2 = 150, so T_oxygen = 150 × 32 = 4800 K. The heavier gas must be much hotter to match the speed of the lighter one.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
subtopic: Effect of leakage on speed and energy
question: A vessel of fixed volume contains a gas at 300 K. Gas is allowed to leak out slowly until the pressure falls to half its initial value, the temperature being held at 300 K throughout. As a result,:

options.A: the root mean square speed is unchanged and the total translational kinetic energy of the gas in the vessel is halved
options.B: the root mean square speed is unchanged and the total translational kinetic energy is unchanged
options.C: the root mean square speed falls to 1 / √(2) times its value and the total energy is halved
options.D: both the root mean square speed and the total translational kinetic energy are halved

correct_answer: the root mean square speed is unchanged and the total translational kinetic energy of the gas in the vessel is halved
explanation: The temperature is constant, so v_rms = √(3 R T / M) is unchanged. At constant volume and temperature the pressure is proportional to the number of molecules, so halving the pressure means half the molecules remain. The total translational kinetic energy is (3/2) N k T, which therefore falls to half. The same conclusion follows from (3/2) P V with V fixed and P halved.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

question: The root mean square speed of the molecules of a gas is 1730 m s⁻¹. The mean speed of the molecules at the same temperature is nearly:

subject: Physics
question: Gas A has a molar mass four times that of gas B, and gas A is kept at twice the absolute temperature of gas B. The ratio of the root mean square speed of A to that of B is:
explanation: The ratio is √((T_A / M_A) / (T_B / M_B)) = √((2 T_B / 4 M_B) × (M_B / T_B)) = √(2 / 4) = √(1/2) = 1 / √(2), which is about 0.71. So gas A is the slower of the two despite being hotter.

explanation: Since v_rms = √(3 R T / M), the speed is proportional to the square root of the absolute temperature. Multiplying T by 4 multiplies v_rms by √(4) = 2.

subject: Physics
question: For the molecules of a gas at a given temperature, the correct order of the root mean square speed v_rms, the mean speed v_mean and the most probable speed v_mp is:
explanation: Writing each speed as a coefficient times √(R T / M), the coefficients are √(3) = 1.73 for the root mean square speed, √(8/π) = 1.60 for the mean speed and √(2) = 1.41 for the most probable speed. Hence v_rms is the largest and v_mp is the smallest.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
question: For a gas enclosed in a stationary container, the average of the velocities of all the molecules and the mean speed of the molecules are respectively:

options.A: about 1.60 times √(R T / M) and zero
options.B: both equal to about 1.73 times √(R T / M)
options.D: zero and about 1.60 times √(R T / M)

correct_answer: zero and about 1.60 times √(R T / M)
explanation: Velocity is a vector, and in a stationary container every direction is equally likely, so the components cancel in pairs and the average velocity is zero. Speed is the magnitude of velocity and is always positive, so no cancellation is possible. The mean speed equals √(8 R T / π M), which is 1.60 times √(R T / M).
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
question: For a gas of molar mass M at absolute temperature T, the root mean square speed of the molecules is given by:
explanation: For one mole, P V = R T and P V = (1/3) M v_rms² from kinetic theory. Equating the two gives v_rms² = 3 R T / M, so v_rms = √(3 R T / M) with M in kilogram per mole.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 9: Kinetic Theory of Gases

subject: Physics
subtopic: Nodes and antinodes in a mode
question: In the second overtone of a pipe open at both ends, the air column contains:
explanation: The second overtone of an open pipe is the third harmonic, so the pipe holds three half wavelengths. Counting along the pipe there are antinodes at both ends and at two interior points, giving 4 antinodes, with 3 nodes in between.

subject: Physics
question: An open pipe and a closed pipe sound the same fundamental note in the same air. Comparing their lengths,:

options.A: the open pipe is four times as long as the closed pipe
options.B: the open pipe is twice as long as the closed pipe
options.C: the open pipe is half as long as the closed pipe
options.D: the two pipes have equal lengths

correct_answer: the open pipe is twice as long as the closed pipe
explanation: Setting the two fundamentals equal, v/(2 Lo) = v/(4 Lc), so 4 Lc = 2 Lo and Lo = 2 Lc. The open pipe must be twice as long.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subtopic: Overtone series of an open pipe
question: The frequencies of the fundamental, the first overtone and the second overtone of a pipe open at both ends are in the ratio:
explanation: The allowed frequencies are v/(2L), 2v/(2L), 3v/(2L) and so on. The first three are therefore in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3.

question: For a cylindrical pipe of inner diameter d, the end correction to be added at one open end is taken as:

options.D: 0.3 L, where L is the length of the pipe

explanation: The displacement antinode does not sit exactly at the geometric opening but a little beyond it, at a distance of about 0.3 times the inner diameter. A closed pipe has one open end and so needs one such correction, while an open pipe needs two.

subject: Physics
question: In a resonance tube experiment the first resonance occurs when the air column is 0.24 m long and the second when it is 0.74 m long. Taking the speed of sound in air as 330 m s⁻¹, the frequency of the tuning fork used is:
explanation: The difference of the two resonance lengths is 0.74 - 0.24 = 0.50 m, which equals λ/2, so λ = 1 m. Hence f = v/λ = 330/1 = 330 Hz. This method automatically eliminates the end correction.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI

subject: Physics
subtopic: Consecutive resonances of a closed pipe
question: A pipe closed at one end resonates strongly at 500 Hz and at 700 Hz, with no resonance in between. The fundamental frequency of the pipe is:
explanation: Consecutive odd harmonics differ by twice the fundamental, so 2 n = 700 - 500 = 200 Hz and n = 100 Hz. As a check, 500 = 5 × 100 and 700 = 7 × 100, which are indeed consecutive odd multiples.

subject: Physics
question: A resonance tube is sounded with a tuning fork of frequency 425 Hz. The speed of sound in air is 340 m s⁻¹ and the end correction may be neglected. The length of the air column at the second resonance is:
explanation: The wavelength is λ = v/f = 340/425 = 0.8 m. The first resonance is at λ/4 = 0.2 m and the second at 3 λ/4 = 0.6 m.

subtopic: First overtone of a closed pipe
question: The fundamental frequency of a pipe closed at one end is n. Its first overtone is:

options.A: the second harmonic, of frequency 2 n
options.B: the fifth harmonic, of frequency 5 n
options.C: the third harmonic, of frequency 3 n
options.D: the third harmonic, of frequency n/3

correct_answer: the third harmonic, of frequency 3 n
explanation: The available frequencies are n, 3n, 5n and so on. The first frequency above the fundamental is 3n, so the first overtone is the third harmonic.

subject: Physics
question: A pipe closed at one end can sound:

options.A: only the odd harmonics, in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5
options.B: only the even harmonics, in the ratio 2 : 4 : 6
options.C: all the harmonics, in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3
options.D: only the first two harmonics and nothing beyond them

correct_answer: only the odd harmonics, in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5
explanation: The node at the closed end and the antinode at the open end allow only patterns containing an odd number of quarter wavelengths. The frequencies are therefore v/(4L), 3v/(4L), 5v/(4L) and so on, in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: Two pipes open at both ends have lengths 1.0 m and 1.1 m. They are sounded together in their fundamental modes. Taking the speed of sound in air as 330 m s⁻¹, the number of beats produced per second is:
explanation: The first pipe gives n1 = 330/(2 × 1.0) = 165 Hz and the second gives n2 = 330/(2 × 1.1) = 330/2.2 = 150 Hz. The beat frequency is 165 - 150 = 15 beats per second.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: Two tuning forks A and B produce 4 beats per second. Fork A is loaded with a little wax and the beat rate falls to 2 per second. On adding more wax the beats vanish, and on adding still more wax the beat rate becomes 3 per second. If the frequency of B is 512 Hz, the original frequency of A was:
explanation: Initially A is either 516 Hz or 508 Hz. Wax lowers the frequency of A. Starting from 516 Hz, the frequency falls to about 514 Hz giving 2 beats, then to 512 Hz giving no beats, then to about 509 Hz giving 3 beats, which matches the whole sequence. Starting from 508 Hz the beat rate would only increase, so that possibility is ruled out. Hence A was 516 Hz.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
subtopic: Number of beats in a time interval
question: Two sources of sound of frequencies 300 Hz and 306 Hz are sounded together for 4 s. The total number of beats heard is:
explanation: The beat frequency is 306 - 300 = 6 beats per second. Over 4 s the total number of beats is 6 × 4 = 24.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded together. The number of beats heard per second is:
explanation: The beat frequency is the magnitude of the difference of the two frequencies, that is 260 - 256 = 4 beats per second.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: The range of frequencies to which the normal human ear responds is about:
explanation: Frequencies below about 20 Hz are called infrasonic and are felt rather than heard, while frequencies above about 20000 Hz are ultrasonic and lie beyond the response of the human ear. The upper limit falls steadily with age, so the figure of 20 kHz applies to young ears.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: Which of the following is a source of infrasonic waves?

options.A: the transmitter of a SONAR set on a ship
options.B: the ground vibrations that travel ahead of an earthquake
options.C: the navigation pulses emitted by a bat in flight
options.D: an ultrasonic cleaning bath used for spectacles

correct_answer: the ground vibrations that travel ahead of an earthquake
explanation: Large slow moving masses produce very low frequencies. The ground motion associated with an earthquake contains components well below 20 Hz, which is why some animals appear to sense an earthquake before humans hear anything. Bats, SONAR transmitters and cleaning baths all operate above 20 kHz and are therefore ultrasonic sources.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: Which statement about the energy of a particle performing ideal SHM is correct?

options.A: The total energy is largest at the mean position and smallest at the extremes
options.B: The kinetic and potential energies keep changing but their sum stays constant
options.C: The kinetic and potential energies are equal at every point of the path
options.D: The kinetic and potential energies are both constant throughout the motion

correct_answer: The kinetic and potential energies keep changing but their sum stays constant
explanation: Adding (1/2) m omega² (A² - x²) and (1/2) m omega² x² gives (1/2) m omega² A², in which x does not appear. So energy is continually exchanged between the two forms while the total remains fixed.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: A block of mass 0.5 kg on a spring of force constant 50 N m⁻¹ oscillates with amplitude 0.2 m. Its kinetic energy at a displacement of 0.1 m is:
explanation: E = 0.5 × 50 × 0.2² = 0.5 × 50 × 0.04 = 1 J. PE at x = 0.1 m is 0.5 × 50 × 0.01 = 0.25 J. Hence KE = 1 minus 0.25 = 0.75 J. The mass is not needed because the force constant is given.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: The amplitude of a sound wave of fixed frequency travelling in air is increased to three times its original value. The energy carried by the wave across unit area per second becomes:

options.C: one third of the original value
options.D: one ninth of the original value

explanation: The energy of an oscillating particle is proportional to the square of its amplitude, and the intensity of the wave is the energy crossing unit area per unit time. With the frequency and the medium unchanged, I is proportional to A². Tripling A therefore multiplies the intensity by 3² = 9.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: In a sound wave travelling through air, the distance between the centres of two successive compressions is equal to:

options.A: one quarter of the wavelength of the wave
options.C: one half of the wavelength of the wave
options.D: twice the wavelength of the wave

explanation: Two successive compressions are the nearest pair of points that are in exactly the same state of motion and the same state of pressure. The distance between two such consecutive points in phase is by definition one wavelength. A compression and the rarefaction next to it are in opposite phase and are separated by half a wavelength.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: During a thunderstorm the flash of lightning is seen well before the thunder is heard, even though both are produced at the same instant. This is because:

options.A: the ear responds much more slowly than the eye, and this response time accounts for the gap
options.B: light travels through air about a million times faster than sound, so the sound takes far longer to cover the same distance
options.C: the thunder is produced a few seconds after the flash by the cooling of the air along the channel
options.D: sound is absorbed by the clouds and is released only after some delay

correct_answer: light travels through air about a million times faster than sound, so the sound takes far longer to cover the same distance
explanation: The lightning and the thunder begin at the same moment. Light covers a few kilometres in a small fraction of a millisecond, so the flash is effectively seen at once. Sound covers the same few kilometres at about 340 m s⁻¹ and so takes several seconds. The gap therefore grows in proportion to the distance of the storm, which is why the delay is used to estimate that distance.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: Four statements about sound waves in air are listed. P: they are longitudinal. Q: they transport the air itself from the source to the listener. R: they require a material medium. S: they can be polarised. The statements that are correct are:
explanation: P is correct, since the air particles oscillate along the direction of travel. Q is wrong, because although energy travels forward each particle only oscillates about a fixed mean position and no net mass is carried across. R is correct, since a mechanical wave has nothing to propagate through in vacuum. S is wrong, because polarisation requires vibration across the line of travel and a longitudinal wave has none. Hence only P and R are correct.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: Sound travelling through air is correctly described as:

options.A: an electromagnetic wave produced by the vibrating charges in the source
options.B: a longitudinal mechanical wave in which the particles of air oscillate along the direction of propagation
options.C: a longitudinal electromagnetic wave whose speed is fixed by the electrical properties of air
options.D: a transverse mechanical wave in which the particles of air oscillate at right angles to the direction of propagation

correct_answer: a longitudinal mechanical wave in which the particles of air oscillate along the direction of propagation
explanation: In a sound wave the layers of air are alternately pushed together and pulled apart along the line of travel. Each particle oscillates about its mean position parallel to the direction in which the disturbance advances, which is the defining feature of a longitudinal wave. Because the restoring force comes from the elasticity of the air, the wave is mechanical, not electromagnetic.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: A loudspeaker sounds a steady note in a still room. Regarding the air between the speaker and the listener,:

options.A: air travels from the speaker to the listener but the energy stays localised near the speaker
options.B: neither energy nor air moves through the room, since each particle simply vibrates in place
options.C: both energy and air travel steadily from the speaker to the listener, producing a slow breeze in the room
options.D: energy travels from the speaker to the listener while each air particle merely oscillates about a fixed mean position

correct_answer: energy travels from the speaker to the listener while each air particle merely oscillates about a fixed mean position
explanation: Each particle of air executes a small oscillation about its own mean position and hands its energy on to the next particle. Over one full cycle the net displacement of any particle is zero, so no air is carried across the room, yet the energy given out by the cone of the speaker travels outward continuously and reaches the ear.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: An electric bell is suspended inside a glass jar and kept ringing while the air is slowly pumped out of the jar. As the pumping continues, the sound heard outside:

options.A: first becomes louder and then dies away once the pressure falls below atmospheric pressure
options.B: stays equally loud because the sound travels out through the glass wall of the jar
options.C: becomes louder because the removal of air reduces the resistance offered to the wave
options.D: becomes fainter and fainter and finally cannot be heard at all, although the hammer is still seen striking the gong

correct_answer: becomes fainter and fainter and finally cannot be heard at all, although the hammer is still seen striking the gong
explanation: Sound is carried by the successive pushing of one layer of the medium on the next. As the air is removed there are fewer and fewer particles to pass the disturbance on, so the sound grows steadily fainter. In a good vacuum there is no medium at all and no sound reaches the jar wall, even though light still travels and the hammer is seen to move.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: Two astronauts working outside their spacecraft cannot hear each other even when their helmets are only a metre apart. They communicate by radio because:

options.A: space contains no material medium, so the mechanical vibrations of sound have nothing to travel through, while radio waves need no medium
options.B: radio waves travel much faster than sound and therefore drown the sound out
options.C: the very low temperature of space reduces the speed of sound almost to zero
options.D: their helmets are made of a material that completely absorbs all sound falling on it

correct_answer: space contains no material medium, so the mechanical vibrations of sound have nothing to travel through, while radio waves need no medium
explanation: Sound propagates by the successive compression of layers of a material medium. Outer space is very nearly empty, so there are no layers of matter to be compressed and no sound can cross the gap. Radio waves are electromagnetic and propagate through vacuum without any medium, which is why they are used for communication in space.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: In a sound wave travelling through air, a compression is a region in which:

options.A: the particles are momentarily at rest, so that the density stays normal while the pressure rises
options.B: the particles are spread apart, so that the density and the pressure are both above their normal values
options.C: the particles are crowded together, so that the density is above normal while the pressure falls below normal
options.D: the particles are crowded together, so that the density and the pressure are above their normal values

correct_answer: the particles are crowded together, so that the density and the pressure are above their normal values
explanation: As the source vibrates it pushes the neighbouring layer of air forward, squeezing the particles into a smaller volume. In this region the number of particles per unit volume rises, so the density rises, and since the gas is compressed its pressure also rises above the undisturbed value. The opposite region, where the particles are pulled apart, is a rarefaction of reduced density and reduced pressure.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: A tuning fork of frequency 480 Hz is sounded in air. The number of compressions that pass a fixed point in the air in one second is:
explanation: In every complete vibration the prong of the fork moves forward once, producing one compression, and backward once, producing one rarefaction. The fork completes 480 vibrations each second, so 480 compressions and 480 rarefactions leave it each second and 480 compressions cross any fixed point in the path in one second.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
subtopic: Waves in different states of matter
question: Consider mechanical waves in bulk matter. Which of the following statements describes the situation correctly?

options.A: transverse waves can travel through solids, liquids and gases, while longitudinal waves can travel through the bulk of solids only
options.B: both longitudinal and transverse mechanical waves can travel through the bulk of any of the three states of matter
options.C: longitudinal waves travel only through gases and transverse waves only through liquids
options.D: longitudinal waves can travel through solids, liquids and gases, while transverse mechanical waves can travel through the bulk of solids only

correct_answer: longitudinal waves can travel through solids, liquids and gases, while transverse mechanical waves can travel through the bulk of solids only
explanation: A longitudinal wave alternately compresses and expands the medium, and every state of matter resists a change of volume, so all three can carry it. A transverse wave requires the medium to resist a shearing displacement of one layer past another. Only solids possess a modulus of rigidity, so only solids can carry transverse mechanical waves through their bulk. Ripples on the surface of water are a surface effect governed by gravity and surface tension, not a bulk transverse wave.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves
tags: Waves in different states of matter

subject: Physics
question: A sound wave of frequency 500 Hz travels in air with speed 340 m s⁻¹. The amplitude of oscillation of an air particle is 1 mm. Taking π = 3.14, the maximum speed of an air particle is about:
explanation: The angular frequency is ω = 2 π f = 2 × 3.14 × 500 = 3140 rad s⁻¹. The amplitude is A = 1 mm = 1 × 10⁻³ m. Hence the maximum particle speed is A ω = 1 × 10⁻³ x 3140 = 3.14 m s⁻¹. This is roughly a hundred times smaller than the wave speed of 340 m s⁻¹, which confirms that the particles only jiggle while the disturbance races ahead.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: The SI unit of frequency of an oscillation is the hertz, which is equivalent to:
explanation: Frequency counts oscillations per unit time. Since the oscillation count is a pure number, the unit is simply the reciprocal second, s⁻¹, given the special name hertz.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: For an ideal linear oscillator, which statement about the period is correct?

options.A: The period decreases as the amplitude increases
options.B: The period is independent of the amplitude of oscillation
options.C: The period increases in direct proportion to the amplitude
options.D: The period is proportional to the square root of the amplitude

correct_answer: The period is independent of the amplitude of oscillation
explanation: The period expression involves only the inertia and the stiffness of the system. Increasing the amplitude increases both the distance to be covered and the restoring force in the same proportion, so the time taken per oscillation does not change. This property is called isochronism.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: A tuning fork prong performs SHM at a frequency of 50 Hz. Its angular frequency is:
explanation: ω = 2 π f = 2 π x 50 = 100 π rad s⁻¹, which is about 314 rad s⁻¹.

subject: Physics
question: A particle completes 40 oscillations in 20 s. Its angular frequency is:

options.C: 4 π rad s⁻¹, about 12.6 rad s⁻¹

correct_answer: 4 π rad s⁻¹, about 12.6 rad s⁻¹
explanation: f = 40/20 = 2 Hz, so the period is 0.5 s. Then ω = 2 π f = 2 π x 2 = 4 π rad s⁻¹, about 12.6 rad s⁻¹.

subject: Physics
question: A block on a spring oscillates with period T. Keeping the same spring, the mass must be changed to:

options.A: one half of its original value to make the period T/2
options.B: one quarter of its original value to make the period T/2
options.C: twice its original value to make the period T/2
options.D: four times its original value to make the period T/2

correct_answer: one quarter of its original value to make the period T/2
explanation: Since T is proportional to √(m), halving T requires √(m) to be halved, that is m must become one quarter of its original value. Checking, √(m/4) = (1/2) √(m).
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: A particle performs SHM with acceleration a = -100 x m s⁻². The number of oscillations it completes in one minute is:
explanation: From a = -100 x, omega² = 100 so ω = 10 rad s⁻¹. Then f = 10/(2 π) = 5/π Hz. In 60 s the number of oscillations is 60 × 5/π = 300/π, which is about 95.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: The same mass is attached to a spring whose force constant is four times that of the original spring. The new period is:

options.B: the same as the original period
options.C: one quarter of the original period

explanation: Multiplying k by four divides T by √(4) = 2. The new period is therefore half the original period.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: When two or more waves arrive simultaneously at a point of a medium, the principle of superposition states that:

options.A: only the wave with the larger amplitude decides the displacement
options.B: the resultant displacement is the arithmetic mean of the individual displacements
options.C: the resultant displacement is the product of the individual displacements
options.D: the resultant displacement at that point is the vector sum of the displacements produced by the individual waves

correct_answer: the resultant displacement at that point is the vector sum of the displacements produced by the individual waves
explanation: Because the wave equation is linear, if y1 and y2 are separately solutions then their sum is also a solution. Hence the net displacement of a particle is obtained by adding the individual displacements with their proper signs.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: Which statement about the principle of superposition of waves is correct?

options.A: It applies only when the two waves have exactly the same frequency
options.B: It applies only to transverse waves and fails for longitudinal waves
options.C: It follows from the linearity of the wave equation and applies to waves of every kind, including sound and light
options.D: It applies only when the two waves travel in the same direction

correct_answer: It follows from the linearity of the wave equation and applies to waves of every kind, including sound and light
explanation: If y1 and y2 each satisfy the linear wave equation, then any sum of them also satisfies it. Nothing in the argument refers to the type of wave, the direction of travel or the equality of frequencies.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: Two waves, each of amplitude A and of the same frequency, arrive at a point with a path difference of λ/3. The resultant amplitude at that point is:
explanation: The phase difference is (2 π/λ) × (λ/3) = 2 π/3. For two equal amplitudes, R = 2 A cos(φ/2) = 2 A cos(π/3) = 2 A x 0.5 = A.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: Two waves of the same frequency reinforce each other completely at a point when:

options.A: the path difference is an odd integral multiple of a quarter of the wavelength
options.B: the path difference between them is an integral multiple of the wavelength
options.C: the path difference is an odd integral multiple of half the wavelength
options.D: the two waves happen to have equal amplitudes

correct_answer: the path difference between them is an integral multiple of the wavelength
explanation: Phase difference and path difference are related by phase = (2 π/λ) x path. For the phase difference to be 0, 2 π, 4 π and so on, the path difference must be 0, λ, 2 λ and so on.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: Three waves, each of amplitude A and of the same frequency, superpose at a point with phases 0, 2 π/3 and 4 π/3. The resultant amplitude is:
explanation: The three phasors of equal length A are separated by 120°, so they form a closed equilateral triangle. Adding components, A cos 0 + A cos 120 + A cos 240 = A - 0.5 A - 0.5 A = 0, and A sin 0 + A sin 120 + A sin 240 = 0 as well. Hence the resultant amplitude is zero.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: For a progressive wave travelling through a medium, which statement is correct?

options.A: The wave velocity is constant for a given medium, while the particle velocity changes continuously during each oscillation
options.B: The particle velocity is always equal to the wave velocity
options.C: Both the wave velocity and the particle velocity are constant in magnitude and direction
options.D: The wave velocity is maximum at the crest and zero at the mean position

correct_answer: The wave velocity is constant for a given medium, while the particle velocity changes continuously during each oscillation
explanation: The wave velocity ω/k is fixed by the elastic and inertial properties of the medium and does not change with time. The particle velocity is the time derivative of the displacement and varies from zero at the extreme positions to A ω at the mean position.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: A progressive wave is given by y = 0.02 sin(300 t - 1.5 x) in SI units. The ratio of the maximum particle speed to the wave speed is:
explanation: Here A = 0.02 m, ω = 300 rad s⁻¹ and k = 1.5 rad m⁻¹. Maximum particle speed = 0.02 × 300 = 6 m s⁻¹ and wave speed = 300/1.5 = 200 m s⁻¹. The ratio is 6/200 = 0.03, which is also A k = 0.02 × 1.5.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
question: Two points on a progressive wave of frequency 500 Hz are 25 cm apart along the direction of propagation and differ in phase by π/2 rad. The speed of the wave is:
explanation: A phase difference of π/2 rad corresponds to a path difference of λ/4. So λ/4 = 0.25 m, giving λ = 1 m. Then v = f λ = 500 × 1 = 500 m s⁻¹.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves

subject: Physics
subtopic: Wave equation in the t and x form
question: A progressive wave is given by y = 2 sin 2 π (t/0.02 - x/40), where y and x are in centimetre and t is in second. The speed of the wave is:
explanation: Comparison gives T = 0.02 s and λ = 40 cm = 0.4 m. Hence v = λ/T = 0.4/0.02 = 20 m s⁻¹.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XI
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 10: Oscillations and Waves
