question: How many turns must be wound on a solenoid of length 1 m carrying a current of 5 A so that the field inside is 4 π x 10⁻³ T? Take μ₀ = 4 π x 10⁻⁷ T m A⁻¹.
explanation: n = B / (μ₀ I) = (4 π x 10⁻³) / (4 π x 10⁻⁷ x 5) = (10⁴) / 5 = 2000 turns per metre. Since the length is 1 m, the total number of turns required is 2000.

question: For an ideal toroid carrying a steady current, the magnetic field is:

options.A: uniform everywhere both inside and outside
options.B: zero in the empty space inside the inner radius and zero outside the toroid, and non zero only within the core enclosed by the windings
options.C: zero within the core and non zero outside
options.D: greatest at the centre of the toroid ring

correct_answer: zero in the empty space inside the inner radius and zero outside the toroid, and non zero only within the core enclosed by the windings
explanation: A circular loop drawn inside the inner radius encloses no current, so B = 0 there. A loop drawn outside the whole toroid is threaded by each turn twice, once inward and once outward, so the net enclosed current is zero and B = 0 there too. Only a loop lying within the core is threaded by N turns, giving B = μ₀ N I / (2 π r).
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII

question: Which statement correctly compares the magnetic field of a long solenoid with that of a toroid?

options.A: The field inside a long solenoid is uniform, whereas across the cross section of a toroid the field varies as 1 / r and so is not strictly uniform
options.B: Both fields depend on the radius of the winding
options.C: Both fields are exactly uniform throughout the interior
options.D: The toroid field is uniform while the solenoid field falls off along the axis

correct_answer: The field inside a long solenoid is uniform, whereas across the cross section of a toroid the field varies as 1 / r and so is not strictly uniform
explanation: In a long solenoid the interior field is μ₀ n I everywhere, independent of position and of radius. In a toroid, the same Amperian argument gives B = μ₀ N I / (2 π r), so points nearer the inner edge of the core have a stronger field than points nearer the outer edge. The field is nearly uniform only when the cross section is small compared with the mean radius.

question: The magnetic field inside a long air cored solenoid can be doubled by:

options.A: doubling the length while keeping the total number of turns and the current unchanged
options.B: doubling the radius of the solenoid
options.C: doubling the current while keeping the number of turns per unit length unchanged
options.D: doubling the length of the connecting leads

correct_answer: doubling the current while keeping the number of turns per unit length unchanged
explanation: Since B = μ₀ n I, the interior field is doubled by doubling either the current or the number of turns per unit length. Doubling the length at fixed total turns halves n and therefore halves B, while changing the radius or the leads has no effect.

question: Two long solenoids have the same number of turns per unit length and carry the same current, but the second has twice the radius of the first. The magnetic fields inside them are related as:

options.A: the field in the wider solenoid is one quarter of that in the narrower one
options.B: the field in the wider solenoid is twice that in the narrower one
options.C: the field in the wider solenoid is half that in the narrower one

explanation: The Amperian rectangle used in the derivation gives B L = μ₀ (n L) I, in which the radius never appears. So long as the solenoid is long compared with its diameter, the interior field depends only on n and I, and the two fields are equal.

question: In a moving coil galvanometer the pole pieces are made concave and a soft iron core is used so as to produce a radial magnetic field. The purpose of this arrangement is that:

options.A: the restoring torque of the suspension is eliminated
options.B: the torque becomes proportional to the square of the current
options.C: the plane of the coil always contains the field, so the deflecting torque is N B I A for every position and the scale becomes linear
options.D: the magnetic field inside the instrument is made zero

correct_answer: the plane of the coil always contains the field, so the deflecting torque is N B I A for every position and the scale becomes linear
explanation: In a radial field the field lines are always parallel to the plane of the coil, so sin θ = 1 whatever the deflection. The deflecting torque N B I A is then balanced by the restoring torque k φ, giving φ proportional to I. The scale is therefore uniform and the instrument can be read directly.

question: A coil of N turns, area A, carrying a current I is placed in a uniform magnetic field B, the normal to its plane making an angle θ with the field. The torque on the coil is:

options.A: N B I A sin θ, and it is maximum when the plane of the coil contains the field
options.B: N B I A² sin θ
options.C: N B I A cos θ, and it is maximum when the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the field
options.D: N B I A, independent of orientation

correct_answer: N B I A sin θ, and it is maximum when the plane of the coil contains the field
explanation: The magnetic moment of the coil is m = N I A directed along the normal, and the torque is m B sin θ, where θ is measured between the normal and the field. The torque is greatest when the normal is perpendicular to B, that is when the plane of the coil contains the field.

question: Which statement about the sensitivity of a moving coil galvanometer is correct?

options.A: Voltage sensitivity and current sensitivity are the same quantity expressed in different units
options.B: Increasing the number of turns raises the voltage sensitivity in the same proportion as the current sensitivity
options.C: Voltage sensitivity is obtained by multiplying the current sensitivity by the resistance of the coil
options.D: Increasing the number of turns raises the current sensitivity, but since the resistance of the coil also rises, the voltage sensitivity need not increase

correct_answer: Increasing the number of turns raises the current sensitivity, but since the resistance of the coil also rises, the voltage sensitivity need not increase
explanation: Voltage sensitivity is φ / V = φ / (I R) = N B A / (k R). Adding turns increases N but also lengthens the wire, so R increases in roughly the same proportion. The ratio N / R therefore changes little and the voltage sensitivity may not improve at all, even though the current sensitivity clearly does.

unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: In an AC generator the induced emf has its maximum value at the instant when:

options.B: the flux linked with the coil is maximum and is still increasing
options.C: the plane of the coil is parallel to the magnetic field, so that the flux linked with it is zero
options.D: the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the field, so that the flux linked with it is maximum

correct_answer: the plane of the coil is parallel to the magnetic field, so that the flux linked with it is zero
explanation: The emf depends on the rate of change of flux, not on the flux. When the plane of the coil lies along the field the flux linkage is momentarily zero, but it is changing at its fastest rate, and the sine term reaches unity so the emf takes its peak value N B A ω.

unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: The slip rings in an AC generator:

options.A: reverse the connections of the coil twice in every rotation
options.B: keep the rotating coil permanently connected to the same external terminals, so the output alternates
options.C: increase the emf generated by the rotating coil
options.D: convert the alternating emf of the coil into a steady direct emf

correct_answer: keep the rotating coil permanently connected to the same external terminals, so the output alternates
explanation: Each end of the coil is joined to its own slip ring, and each ring presses against a fixed brush. The connection to the external circuit never changes, so the reversal of the emf inside the rotating coil appears as an alternating emf across the load.

question: The average power consumed by an ideal capacitor connected to an AC source over one full cycle is:

options.A: zero, because the energy stored while charging is returned while discharging
options.B: V_rms² multiplied by the capacitive reactance
options.D: V_rms x I_rms, as in a resistor

correct_answer: zero, because the energy stored while charging is returned while discharging
explanation: Since cos(π/2) = 0, the average power is zero. The capacitor takes energy from the source while charging and gives exactly that energy back while discharging in each half cycle.

options.D: i = e0 ω C sin(ω t)

correct_answer: i = e0 ω C sin(ω t + π/2)
explanation: The peak current is e0 / X_C = e0 ω C, and the current leads the voltage by π/2. Hence i = e0 ω C sin(ω t + π/2).

unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: In a purely inductive AC circuit, the current:

options.A: leads the applied voltage by π/2 radian

options.C: lags behind the applied voltage by π/2 radian
options.D: is in phase with the applied voltage

correct_answer: lags behind the applied voltage by π/2 radian
explanation: The self induced emf opposes the change of current, so the current builds up a quarter cycle behind the applied voltage. Hence the current lags the voltage by π/2 radian.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: In a pure inductor carrying alternating current, at the instant when the current is maximum, the voltage across the inductor is:

options.A: half of its peak value, because the phase difference is 60°
options.B: equal to the peak current multiplied by the inductance
options.C: zero, because the rate of change of current is zero at that instant
options.D: also maximum, because voltage and current peak together

correct_answer: zero, because the rate of change of current is zero at that instant
explanation: At the peak of the current waveform the slope di/dt is zero, and since v = L di/dt, the voltage across the inductor is zero at that instant. This is exactly the quarter cycle phase difference expressed instant by instant.

question: The average power consumed by a pure inductor over one complete cycle of AC is:

options.C: V_rms x I_rms, the same as in a resistor

correct_answer: zero, since energy is stored and returned to the source in equal amounts
explanation: Since cos(π/2) = 0, the average power is zero. During one quarter cycle the inductor draws energy to build its magnetic field and during the next quarter cycle it returns exactly that energy to the source.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: In an induction furnace, a metal placed inside a coil carrying a high frequency alternating current melts because:

options.A: strong eddy currents induced in the metal dissipate heat within its own body
options.B: the alternating magnetic field breaks the chemical bonds of the metal
options.C: the coil conducts heat to the metal by direct contact
options.D: the metal loses its resistance and therefore becomes hot

correct_answer: strong eddy currents induced in the metal dissipate heat within its own body
explanation: The rapidly changing flux induces very large eddy currents throughout the metal. The i² R heating produced by these currents is generated inside the metal itself and is intense enough to raise the metal to its melting point.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: In the electromagnetic brakes of a train, the retarding force produced by eddy currents:

options.A: decreases as the train slows down, so this braking alone cannot bring the train fully to rest
options.B: acts only after the train has already stopped
options.C: increases as the train slows down, giving a sharp final stop
options.D: stays constant at all speeds, so the train stops with uniform deceleration

correct_answer: decreases as the train slows down, so this braking alone cannot bring the train fully to rest
explanation: The eddy currents are driven by an emf proportional to the speed, so the retarding force is also proportional to the speed. As the train slows, the braking force falls in proportion, giving a smooth jerk free retardation that becomes weaker and weaker, so mechanical brakes are needed for the final stop. The kinetic energy removed appears as heat in the rails and discs.

question: The coil of a dead beat galvanometer is wound on a metallic frame so that:

options.C: eddy currents induced in the frame oppose the motion and bring the coil quickly to rest
options.D: the frame carries part of the measured current and protects the coil

correct_answer: eddy currents induced in the frame oppose the motion and bring the coil quickly to rest
explanation: As the coil turns, the flux through the metal frame changes and eddy currents appear in it. By Lenz's law these currents oppose the rotation, dissipating the energy of the oscillation as heat so the pointer settles at its reading without swinging.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: Eddy currents are:

options.A: circulating currents induced in the body of a conductor placed in a changing magnetic flux
options.B: currents produced by the chemical action inside a conductor
options.C: currents that flow only in wires wound into closed loops
options.D: currents that flow along the surface of a conductor because of static charges

correct_answer: circulating currents induced in the body of a conductor placed in a changing magnetic flux
explanation: A changing magnetic flux induces emfs along every closed path inside a solid conductor. Because the conductor offers many such paths, whirling currents are set up in its body; these are called eddy or Foucault currents.

unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: A solid copper plate swinging between the poles of a strong magnet comes to rest very quickly. If deep slots are cut in the same plate, it will:

options.A: swing for a much longer time, because the slots interrupt the eddy current paths
options.B: swing for exactly the same time, because copper is not magnetic
options.C: swing for a longer time, because the slots reduce the magnetic field between the poles
options.D: come to rest even faster, because the slots make the plate lighter

correct_answer: swing for a much longer time, because the slots interrupt the eddy current paths
explanation: In the solid plate large eddy currents circulate and, by Lenz's law, oppose the swing, damping it rapidly. The slots break these wide circulating paths into narrow ones of much higher resistance, so the currents and the retarding force become small and the plate swings for far longer.

question: The core of a transformer is built from thin sheets insulated from one another in order to:

explanation: Laminations lie parallel to the flux, so they do not obstruct it, but the insulation between them confines each eddy current to a thin sheet. The narrow paths have a much higher resistance, so the induced currents and the heat they produce are greatly reduced.

question: A magnet is brought up to a closed coil, first quickly and then slowly, producing the same total flux change each time. Compared with the slow motion, the fast motion produces:

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: The negative sign in the relation e = -N d(φ)/dt indicates that:

options.A: the magnetic flux always decreases with time
options.B: the induced emf is always negative in value
options.C: energy is lost during the process of induction
options.D: the induced emf opposes the change in flux that produces it, which follows from conservation of energy

correct_answer: the induced emf opposes the change in flux that produces it, which follows from conservation of energy
explanation: The minus sign is the mathematical statement of Lenz's law. The induced emf drives a current whose effect opposes the change in flux, so that work must be done to maintain the change and energy is conserved.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: A closed metal ring is placed coaxially near a coil. At the instant the current in the coil is switched on and is rising, the ring:

options.A: is attracted to the coil, its induced current being in the same sense as the coil current
options.B: stays at rest, because the ring carries no source of emf
options.C: is repelled from the coil, its induced current being in the same sense as the coil current
options.D: is repelled from the coil, its induced current being opposite in sense to the coil current

correct_answer: is repelled from the coil, its induced current being opposite in sense to the coil current
explanation: While the coil current rises, the flux through the ring rises. The ring opposes this by driving a current in the opposite sense. Antiparallel currents repel, so the ring is pushed away from the coil.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: A small closed loop is held coaxially above a large loop in which the current is being increased steadily. Just after the increase begins, the small loop:

options.A: carries no current, because the two loops are not connected to each other
options.B: carries a current opposite in sense to that in the large loop and is pulled towards it
options.C: carries a current opposite in sense to that in the large loop and is pushed away from it
options.D: carries a current in the same sense as that in the large loop and is pulled towards it

correct_answer: carries a current opposite in sense to that in the large loop and is pushed away from it
explanation: The rising current in the large loop increases the flux through the small loop, so by Lenz's law the small loop drives a current in the opposite sense to oppose the increase. Coaxial loops carrying antiparallel currents repel, so the small loop is pushed away, and the work done in holding it in place accounts for the extra energy drawn from the source.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: For a coil in a changing magnetic field, the magnitude of the induced emf is given by Faraday's law while its direction is given by:
explanation: Faraday's laws fix how large the induced emf is, namely N times the rate of change of flux. Lenz's law fixes its sense, requiring the induced effect to oppose its cause; together they are written as e = -N d(φ)/dt.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: Lenz's law states that the direction of the induced current is such that it:

options.A: always flows in the clockwise sense when seen from the magnet
options.B: is always in the same direction as the applied magnetic field
options.C: opposes the change in magnetic flux that produces it
options.D: assists the change in magnetic flux that produces it

correct_answer: opposes the change in magnetic flux that produces it
explanation: The induced current always flows so that its own magnetic effect opposes the change in flux that caused it. This is expressed by the minus sign in e = -N d(φ)/dt.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: When a magnet is pushed towards a closed coil against the opposing magnetic force, the electrical energy that appears in the coil comes from:

options.A: the magnetic energy stored permanently in the bar magnet
options.B: the thermal energy of the surrounding air
options.C: the electric charges already resident in the coil
options.D: the mechanical work done by the agent pushing the magnet

correct_answer: the mechanical work done by the agent pushing the magnet
explanation: The coil opposes the approach, so the agent must do work against that opposition. This mechanical work is converted into electrical energy in the coil and finally into heat, keeping the total energy constant.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
subtopic: Loop moving inside a uniform field
question: A square conducting loop moves with constant velocity entirely within a large region of uniform magnetic field perpendicular to its plane. The induced current in the loop is:

options.A: constant and non zero, because the loop is moving in a magnetic field
options.B: zero, because the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the loop
options.C: zero, because the flux linked with the loop does not change
options.D: non zero only while the loop is accelerating

correct_answer: zero, because the flux linked with the loop does not change
explanation: Inside the uniform region the field and the enclosed area are the same at every instant, so the flux is constant and d(φ)/dt = 0. The motional emfs of the leading and trailing sides are equal and opposite around the loop, so no net current flows.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: A steady current flows in coil P placed close to a closed coil Q. When the switch in the circuit of P is opened, the current induced in Q, during the brief interval while the current in P falls to zero,:

options.A: is zero, because coil P no longer carries any current
options.B: flows in the same sense as the current that was flowing in P
options.C: reverses its direction twice before dying away
options.D: flows in the sense opposite to that of the current that was flowing in P

correct_answer: flows in the same sense as the current that was flowing in P
explanation: As the current in P collapses, the flux through Q falls. Coil Q opposes this fall by trying to maintain the flux, which requires a current in the same sense as the original current in P.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: A closed aluminium ring rests loosely around the top of a vertical solenoid with an iron core. When the solenoid is connected to a source, the ring flies upward because:

options.A: the iron core magnetises the aluminium ring and repels it
options.B: the induced current in the ring is opposite in sense to the solenoid current, so the two repel each other
options.C: the induced current in the ring is in the same sense as the solenoid current, so the two repel each other
options.D: the ring is heated by the current and rises with the hot air

correct_answer: the induced current in the ring is opposite in sense to the solenoid current, so the two repel each other
explanation: At switch on, the flux through the ring rises sharply. The ring opposes the rise by carrying a current in the opposite sense to that in the solenoid. Two antiparallel currents repel, and the repulsive force exceeds the weight of the light ring, so it jumps.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: A small bar magnet is dropped from rest along the axis of a fixed horizontal copper ring, passing through it. During the fall the acceleration of the magnet near the ring is:

options.A: exactly g, because the ring carries no battery
options.B: less than g, because the induced current in the ring opposes the relative motion
options.C: greater than g, because the induced current pulls the magnet towards the ring
options.D: exactly g, because copper is a non magnetic material

correct_answer: less than g, because the induced current in the ring opposes the relative motion
explanation: The moving magnet changes the flux through the ring, so an induced current appears. By Lenz's law this current opposes the relative motion, exerting an upward force on the descending magnet. The net downward force is less than the weight, so the acceleration is less than g.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: The north pole of a bar magnet is moved towards one face of a closed circular coil. As seen from the magnet, the induced current in that face flows:

options.A: anticlockwise, so that the near face behaves as a north pole
options.B: anticlockwise, so that the near face behaves as a south pole
options.C: in no direction, since the magnet does not touch the coil
options.D: clockwise, so that the near face behaves as a south pole

correct_answer: anticlockwise, so that the near face behaves as a north pole
explanation: The flux towards the coil increases, so the coil opposes the approach by presenting a north pole to the magnet. A face behaves as a north pole when the current in it runs anticlockwise as seen from the side facing the magnet.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: Suppose the induced current in a coil flowed in the sense opposite to that required by Lenz's law. The immediate consequence would be that:

options.A: the motion causing the flux change would be assisted and energy would be produced from nothing
options.B: the induced emf would become infinite in a finite time
options.C: the coil would gain charge continuously
options.D: no current would flow at all in the coil

correct_answer: the motion causing the flux change would be assisted and energy would be produced from nothing
explanation: If the induced current aided the change, the magnet would be pulled in faster, increasing the flux change and the current further. Both kinetic energy and electrical energy would grow with no external supply, which is impossible.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents

unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: Lenz's law is a direct consequence of the law of conservation of:
explanation: If the induced current aided the change, the change would grow on its own and energy would appear from nowhere. Opposition ensures that work must be done by an external agent, and that work appears as electrical and then thermal energy.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: The north pole of a bar magnet is pulled away from a closed coil. The coil then:

options.A: repels the magnet, its near face behaving as a north pole
options.B: neither attracts nor repels the magnet
options.C: attracts the magnet, its near face behaving as a north pole
options.D: attracts the magnet, its near face behaving as a south pole

correct_answer: attracts the magnet, its near face behaving as a south pole
explanation: As the magnet recedes the flux linked with the coil decreases, so the induced current acts to maintain it by attracting the magnet. The near face therefore behaves as a south pole for the receding north pole.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: The magnetic flux linked with a plane coil placed in a uniform magnetic field is maximum when:

options.A: the plane of the coil makes 45° with the field
options.B: the normal to the coil is perpendicular to the field
options.C: the plane of the coil is parallel to the field
options.D: the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the field

correct_answer: the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the field
explanation: Flux is maximum when the area vector, that is the normal to the coil, is parallel to B. The normal is parallel to B exactly when the plane of the coil is perpendicular to B, giving φ = B A.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: Magnetic flux is:

options.A: a vector quantity directed along the normal to the surface
options.B: a vector quantity directed along the induced current
options.C: a vector quantity directed along the magnetic field
options.D: a scalar quantity, because it is the dot product of the magnetic field and the area vector

correct_answer: a scalar quantity, because it is the dot product of the magnetic field and the area vector
explanation: Flux is defined as the scalar (dot) product of the magnetic field vector and the area vector. A dot product of two vectors is a scalar, so flux has magnitude and sign but no direction.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: A bar magnet is completely enclosed inside a closed surface. The net magnetic flux through that closed surface is:

options.A: positive and proportional to the pole strength of the magnet
options.B: equal to the flux through one face of the surface
options.C: zero, because magnetic field lines are continuous closed loops
options.D: zero only if the magnet is placed exactly at the centre of the surface

correct_answer: zero, because magnetic field lines are continuous closed loops
explanation: Magnetic field lines have no beginning or end; every line that enters the closed surface also leaves it. The inward and outward contributions cancel exactly, so the net flux is zero for any position of the magnet inside.

question: The dimensional formula of magnetic flux is:

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
subtopic: Flux and shape of the loop
question: A closed flexible wire loop of fixed length is held with its plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field. The loop is slowly reshaped from a circle into a square without changing the length of the wire. The flux through the loop:

options.A: becomes zero, because a square loop cannot enclose magnetic field lines
options.B: remains the same, because the length of the wire is unchanged
options.C: decreases, because for a given perimeter a circle encloses the largest area
options.D: increases, because a square has four sides and therefore a larger area

correct_answer: decreases, because for a given perimeter a circle encloses the largest area
explanation: For a fixed perimeter P the circle encloses P²/(4 π) which is about 0.0796 P², while the square encloses P²/16 which is 0.0625 P². The area falls, and since B and the orientation are unchanged the flux falls with it.

question: A coil of 200 turns and area 5 × 10⁻³ m² is placed in a uniform field of 0.4 T with its normal along the field. The coil is then rotated so that its normal makes 120° with the field. The magnitude of the change in flux linkage is:

unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
subtopic: Flux change on shrinking a loop
question: A flexible circular loop of radius 0.2 m is held with its plane perpendicular to a uniform field of 0.5 T. The loop is shrunk until its radius is 0.1 m, the plane staying perpendicular to the field. Take π = 3.14. The magnitude of the change in flux is:
explanation: Initial flux = 0.5 × 3.14 × (0.2)² = 0.5 × 3.14 × 0.04 = 6.28 × 10⁻² Wb. Final flux = 0.5 × 3.14 × (0.1)² = 1.57 × 10⁻² Wb. The change has magnitude 6.28 × 10⁻² minus 1.57 × 10⁻² = 4.71 × 10⁻² Wb, a fall to one quarter of the original value.

question: A rod of length 0.5 m moves at a constant 4 m s⁻¹ on frictionless rails in a field of 0.4 T, the circuit resistance being 0.2 Ω. The power supplied by the external agent is:
explanation: e = 0.4 × 0.5 × 4 = 0.8 V and i = 0.8/0.2 = 4 A. The retarding force is F = B i l = 0.4 × 4 × 0.5 = 0.8 N, so P = F v = 0.8 × 4 = 3.2 W, equal to e²/R = 0.64/0.2 = 3.2 W.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: The emf induced across the ends of a conductor moving in a magnetic field arises because:

options.A: the magnetic field exerts a force on the fixed positive ions of the lattice
options.B: the resistance of the conductor changes as it moves
options.C: the magnetic force q v x B pushes the free charges towards one end of the conductor
options.D: the moving conductor becomes electrically charged by friction with the air

correct_answer: the magnetic force q v x B pushes the free charges towards one end of the conductor
explanation: Free charges inside the moving rod share its velocity, so each experiences a magnetic force q v x B along the rod. Charges pile up at the ends until the electric field they set up balances this force, and the resulting potential difference is the motional emf B l v.

question: A vertical conducting rod PQ, with P at the top, moves to the right with velocity v in a uniform magnetic field directed into the plane of the page. The end at higher potential is:

options.A: Q, because the magnetic force on the free positive charges is directed downward

options.C: P, because the magnetic force on the free positive charges is directed upward
options.D: P, because electrons are heavier than protons and settle at the bottom

explanation: With v to the right and B into the page, the cross product v x B points upward along the rod. Positive carriers are therefore pushed to the top end P, which becomes positive, while the lower end Q is left negative.

question: A rod of mass 0.1 kg and length 0.4 m is given an initial speed of 10 m s⁻¹ along frictionless rails in a field of 0.5 T and is then left alone. The total charge that circulates in the circuit before the rod finally comes to rest is:
explanation: The retarding force is B i l, and its impulse over the whole motion is B l times the integral of i dt, that is B l q. This impulse must remove all the momentum, so B l q = m v and q = (0.1 × 10)/(0.5 × 0.4) = 1/0.2 = 5 C. Note that the resistance does not enter.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: The mutual inductance of two given coils will not change if:

options.A: one coil is turned so that its plane becomes perpendicular to the other
options.B: a soft iron rod is inserted through both coils
options.C: the current in the primary coil is doubled while everything else is fixed
options.D: the distance between the coils is increased

correct_answer: the current in the primary coil is doubled while everything else is fixed
explanation: Mutual inductance is the ratio of flux linkage to current. Since the shared flux is itself proportional to the current, the ratio is unchanged when the current is doubled. Separation, orientation and the core material all change the ratio.

question: A short coil of small radius is wound at the middle of a long solenoid of larger radius. In the expression for their mutual inductance, the area that appears is:

options.A: the cross sectional area of the outer solenoid
options.B: the difference of the two cross sectional areas
options.C: the sum of the two cross sectional areas
options.D: the cross sectional area of the inner coil, since only that area carries the shared field

correct_answer: the cross sectional area of the inner coil, since only that area carries the shared field
explanation: The uniform field of the long solenoid exists inside it, and the flux linked with the smaller coil is that field multiplied by the smaller of the two areas. By reciprocity the same value of M is obtained whichever coil is treated as primary, so the inner area is the one that enters.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: Two coils of self inductance 2 H and 8 H have a coefficient of coupling of 0.5. They are connected in series so that their fluxes aid each other. The equivalent inductance is:
explanation: M = 0.5 x √(2 × 8) = 0.5 × 4 = 2 H. For fluxes that aid each other, L = L1 + L2 + 2M = 2 + 8 + 4 = 14 H.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: The coefficient of coupling k between two coils:

options.A: can take any value greater than 1 for coils on an iron core
options.B: is measured in henry like the mutual inductance
options.C: is always exactly 1 for any two coils placed near each other
options.D: lies between 0 and 1, being 1 when all the flux of one coil links the other

correct_answer: lies between 0 and 1, being 1 when all the flux of one coil links the other
explanation: The coupling coefficient is the fraction of the flux of one coil that links the other, so it cannot be negative or exceed one. It is a dimensionless number, equal to one only for ideal coupling with no leakage.

unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: For any two coils placed in a fixed relative position, the mutual inductance of coil 1 with respect to coil 2 and that of coil 2 with respect to coil 1 are:

options.A: equal only if the two coils have the same number of turns
options.B: in the ratio of the numbers of turns of the two coils
options.D: equal only if the two coils have the same self inductance

explanation: The reciprocity theorem shows that the flux linkage in coil 2 per unit current in coil 1 is exactly equal to the flux linkage in coil 1 per unit current in coil 2, whatever the shapes, sizes or turn numbers of the coils.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: A steady direct current flows in the primary of a pair of closely coupled coils. The emf induced in the secondary is:

options.A: equal to M times the primary current
options.B: zero, because the current in the primary is not changing
options.C: equal to the primary emf multiplied by the turns ratio
options.D: large, because the coupling between the coils is strong

correct_answer: zero, because the current in the primary is not changing
explanation: The induced emf in the secondary depends on the rate of change of the primary current. For a steady direct current dI_1/dt = 0, so no emf is induced however strong the coupling.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: In an AC circuit, the product of the rms voltage and the rms current is called the apparent power. The true average power is:

options.A: equal to the apparent power multiplied by sin(φ)
options.B: always larger than the apparent power
options.C: always exactly equal to the apparent power
options.D: smaller than or equal to the apparent power, being the apparent power multiplied by cos(φ)

correct_answer: smaller than or equal to the apparent power, being the apparent power multiplied by cos(φ)
explanation: The power factor cos(φ) lies between 0 and 1, so the true power V I cos(φ) is at most equal to the apparent power V I, and equals it only when the phase angle is zero.

question: The power factor of a circuit containing only a pure inductor, and that of a circuit containing only a pure capacitor, are respectively:
explanation: In a pure inductor the current lags the voltage by π/2 and in a pure capacitor it leads by π/2. In both cases cos(φ) = cos(π/2) = 0, so neither element consumes average power.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: The wattless current in an AC circuit is:

options.A: the total current flowing when the circuit contains no resistance at all
options.B: the component I sin(φ) of the current that is perpendicular to the voltage phasor and consumes no average power
options.C: the component I cos(φ) of the current that is along the voltage phasor
options.D: the current that flows only during the first quarter of every cycle

correct_answer: the component I sin(φ) of the current that is perpendicular to the voltage phasor and consumes no average power
explanation: The perpendicular component I sin(φ) is a quarter cycle out of step with the voltage, so the power it carries is positive for half the time and negative for the other half, averaging to zero. It is therefore called the wattless current.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: To reduce the current in an AC circuit, a choke coil is preferred to a resistor because:

options.A: a resistor cannot reduce alternating current
options.B: the choke increases the power factor of the circuit towards unity
options.C: the choke limits the current only for direct current, which is safer
options.D: the choke limits the current with almost no dissipation, whereas a resistor wastes energy as heat

correct_answer: the choke limits the current with almost no dissipation, whereas a resistor wastes energy as heat
explanation: A resistor limiting the same current dissipates I² R as heat. A choke of large reactance and negligible resistance limits the current equally well, but since its power factor is almost zero the average power it consumes is nearly zero, so the energy is returned to the source rather than lost.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: A choke coil is used in a fluorescent tube circuit because:

options.A: it converts the alternating supply into direct current for the tube
options.B: it reduces the current using inductive reactance while consuming almost no power
options.C: it increases the current through the tube at the moment of starting
options.D: it reduces the current by converting the excess electrical energy into heat

correct_answer: it reduces the current using inductive reactance while consuming almost no power
explanation: The large inductive reactance limits the current, while the very small resistance makes the power factor nearly zero, so the average power V I cos(φ) dissipated in the choke is almost nil. A resistor doing the same job would waste large amounts of energy as heat.

unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: A series LCR circuit has R = 10 Ω, L = 0.2 H and C = 20 microF. The two half power angular frequencies are nearly:
explanation: LC = 0.2 × 20 × 10⁻⁶ = 4 × 10⁻⁶, so √(LC) = 2 × 10⁻³ and the resonant angular frequency is omega_r = 500 rad/s. The bandwidth is R / L = 10 / 0.2 = 50 rad/s. In the narrow-band approximation the two half power points sit symmetrically at omega_r +/- R/(2L), that is 475 rad/s and 525 rad/s. The keyed pair uses the standard symmetric narrow-band approximation about resonance.

question: In a series LCR circuit the resistance is increased while L and C are kept unchanged. Then:

options.A: the resonant frequency increases while the peak current decreases
options.B: the resonant frequency is unchanged and the peak current also stays the same
options.C: the resonant frequency is unchanged but the peak current and the sharpness both decrease
options.D: both the resonant frequency and the peak current decrease

correct_answer: the resonant frequency is unchanged but the peak current and the sharpness both decrease
explanation: Resonance occurs when X_L = X_C, a condition involving only L and C, so f_r is unaffected. However the peak current V / R falls and the quality factor omega_r L / R falls, so the resonance curve becomes lower and broader.

question: For a coil with a non magnetic core, which statement is correct?

options.A: The self inductance changes sign when the current is reversed
options.B: The self inductance falls as the current is increased, because I appears in the denominator
options.C: The self inductance is zero when no current flows, because the flux is then zero
options.D: The self inductance is a constant of the coil even though it is written as the ratio N φ/I

correct_answer: The self inductance is a constant of the coil even though it is written as the ratio N φ/I
explanation: For a non magnetic core the flux produced by the coil is directly proportional to the current, so the ratio N φ/I is fixed by the geometry and the core alone. It stays the same whether the current is large, small, zero in the limit, or reversed.

subject: Physics
unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: Self inductance is often called the inertia of electricity because:

options.A: it converts electrical energy into heat at a steady rate
options.B: it keeps the current constant at all times in every circuit
options.C: it stores charge in the coil in the way a capacitor does
options.D: it opposes any change in the current through the coil, just as mass opposes a change in velocity

correct_answer: it opposes any change in the current through the coil, just as mass opposes a change in velocity
explanation: The self induced emf always opposes the change in current, so a larger inductance makes the current harder to change. This is exactly the role mass plays in mechanics, where a larger mass makes the velocity harder to change.

question: A series LCR circuit is operating at a frequency at which the capacitive reactance exceeds the inductive reactance. If the supply frequency is now slowly increased, the impedance of the circuit:

options.B: remains unchanged, since the two reactances change by equal amounts

options.D: increases continuously, since inductive reactance always grows with frequency

correct_answer: first decreases, reaches a minimum equal to R, and then increases
explanation: Raising the frequency increases X_L and decreases X_C, so the magnitude of X_L - X_C first shrinks to zero at resonance, where Z = R, and then grows again as X_L overtakes X_C.

unit: Unit 14: Electromagnetic Induction and Alternating Currents
question: For a series LCR circuit driven by an alternating source, which statement is correct:

options.A: The instantaneous voltages across R, L and C always add to the instantaneous source voltage, but their rms values do not add arithmetically
options.B: Both the instantaneous and the rms voltages add arithmetically to the source voltage
options.C: The rms voltages add arithmetically but the instantaneous voltages do not
options.D: Neither the instantaneous nor the rms voltages satisfy any addition rule

correct_answer: The instantaneous voltages across R, L and C always add to the instantaneous source voltage, but their rms values do not add arithmetically
explanation: At any instant the sum v_R + v_L + v_C equals the source voltage, because Kirchhoff voltage law is an instantaneous statement. The rms values, however, describe waveforms that peak at different instants, so they combine as V = √(V_R² + (V_L - V_C)²).

chapter: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments; Wave Optics
question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a two slit interference pattern from a single slit diffraction pattern?

options.A: In interference the bands become narrower with order, while in diffraction all bands are of equal width
options.B: Interference occurs only with white light while diffraction occurs only with monochromatic light
options.C: Interference needs a single wavefront while diffraction needs two separate coherent sources
options.D: In interference the bright bands are of equal width and nearly equal brightness, while in diffraction the central band is much wider and much brighter than the rest

correct_answer: In interference the bright bands are of equal width and nearly equal brightness, while in diffraction the central band is much wider and much brighter than the rest
explanation: In two slit interference the maxima satisfy y = n x λ x D / d, so consecutive bands are equally spaced and of comparable intensity. In single slit diffraction the minima satisfy y = n x λ x D / a, so the central band spans twice the spacing of the others and carries most of the energy.

question: A single slit diffraction apparatus is taken from air into a liquid of refractive index mu. The angular width of the central maximum:

options.A: remains the same, because the slit width is unchanged
options.B: becomes 1 / mu times its value in air
options.C: becomes mu² times its value in air
options.D: becomes mu times its value in air

correct_answer: becomes 1 / mu times its value in air
explanation: Inside the liquid the wavelength becomes λ divided by mu, so the half angular width becomes λ divided by (mu x a). Every angle of the pattern therefore shrinks by the factor mu.

That wavelength, and the ratio of the widths of the central maximum for 6000 Å to that for the other wavelength, are:
explanation: Equating the two directions gives 1 × 6000 = 2 x λ dash, so λ dash = 3000 Å. Since the central maximum width 2 x λ x D / a is proportional to λ, the ratio of the widths is 6000 : 3000 = 2 : 1.

question: In the single slit diffraction pattern, the central maximum is:

options.A: half as wide as the secondary maxima
options.B: twice as wide as the secondary maxima but fainter than them
options.C: as bright and as wide as each of the secondary maxima
options.D: the brightest band and twice as wide as any of the secondary maxima

correct_answer: the brightest band and twice as wide as any of the secondary maxima
explanation: The first minima on the two sides are each at λ x D / a from the centre, so the central band spans 2 x λ x D / a. Successive minima are separated by λ x D / a, so each secondary maximum is only half as wide, and its peak intensity is a small fraction of the central one.

question: In a single slit diffraction experiment the width of the slit is made exactly equal to the wavelength of the light used. The first minimum then occurs at:

options.B: 0°, so the whole screen is dark
options.C: 45°, because the slit and the wavelength are equal
options.D: 90°, so no minimum is seen and the light spreads over the whole forward region

correct_answer: 90°, so no minimum is seen and the light spreads over the whole forward region
explanation: With a = λ, sin θ = λ / λ = 1, so θ = 90°. The first minimum is pushed to the edge of the forward hemisphere, which means the central maximum fills the entire region beyond the slit and no dark band is observed.

question: Diffraction effects of light become easily noticeable when:

options.A: the size of the obstacle or aperture is comparable with the wavelength of the light
options.B: the light is made to pass through a very thick glass slab
options.C: the obstacle is very much larger than the wavelength of the light
options.D: the light used is of very high intensity

question: For Fraunhofer diffraction at a single slit of width a, the directions of the dark bands are given by:

options.A: a x sin θ = (2n plus 1) x λ / 2
options.B: a x sin θ = n x λ, with n = 0, 1, 2 and so on
options.C: a x sin θ = n x λ, with n = 1, 2, 3 and so on
options.D: d x sin θ = n x λ, where d is the distance to the screen

correct_answer: a x sin θ = n x λ, with n = 1, 2, 3 and so on
explanation: The slit is imagined as split into pairs of strips whose contributions cancel in pairs when the extreme path difference a x sin θ equals a whole number of wavelengths. The value n = 0 must be excluded because there all the strips arrive in step, giving the central maximum.

question: Diffraction of light is the phenomenon of:

options.A: change in the direction of light when it passes from one medium to another
options.B: restriction of the vibrations of light to a single plane
options.C: bending of light around the edges of an obstacle or an aperture into the region of the geometrical shadow
options.D: splitting of white light into its constituent colours by a prism

correct_answer: bending of light around the edges of an obstacle or an aperture into the region of the geometrical shadow
explanation: When a wavefront is partly blocked, the secondary wavelets from the exposed part spread sideways, so light appears inside the region that geometrical optics would call a shadow.

question: In Huygens construction the secondary wavelets are taken only in the forward direction because:

options.A: the backward wavelets travel with a much smaller speed
options.B: the medium behind the wavefront becomes optically denser
options.C: the backward wavelets are absorbed by the source
options.D: the amplitude of a secondary wavelet is maximum in the forward direction and falls to zero in the backward direction

correct_answer: the amplitude of a secondary wavelet is maximum in the forward direction and falls to zero in the backward direction
explanation: The strength of a secondary wavelet depends on the angle θ measured from the forward normal. It is greatest at θ = 0° and becomes zero at θ = 180°, so no backward travelling wavefront is produced.

question: When light travels from air into glass, which set of changes is correct?

options.A: speed increases, wavelength increases, frequency remains the same
options.B: speed remains the same, wavelength decreases, frequency increases
options.C: speed decreases, wavelength remains the same, frequency decreases
options.D: speed decreases, wavelength decreases, frequency remains the same

correct_answer: speed decreases, wavelength decreases, frequency remains the same
explanation: The frequency is set by the source and is the same in every medium. Since v = c / mu is smaller in glass and v = f x λ, the wavelength in glass must be λ divided by mu, that is smaller than in air.

question: A plane wavefront of light of wavelength 6000 Å in air falls normally on an aperture. A glass slab of refractive index 1.5 and thickness 6 cm covers one half of the aperture. The extra optical path introduced by the slab and the number of wavelengths corresponding to it are:
explanation: Extra optical path = (1.5 minus 1) × 6 cm = 0.5 × 6 = 3 cm = 3 × 10⁻² m. With λ = 6000 Å = 6 × 10⁻⁷ m, the number of wavelengths = (3 × 10⁻²) / (6 × 10⁻⁷) = 5 × 10⁴.

question: A glass slab of thickness 3 cm has refractive index 1.5. Taking the speed of light in vacuum as 3 × 10⁸ m per second, the time taken by light to cross the slab normally is:
explanation: Speed in glass v = (3 × 10⁸) / 1.5 = 2 × 10⁸ m per second. Thickness = 3 cm = 3 × 10⁻² m. Time t = (3 × 10⁻²) / (2 × 10⁸) = 1.5 × 10⁻¹⁰ s.

question: Huygens construction applied to a plane wavefront striking a plane mirror shows that:

options.A: the angle of incidence is twice the angle of reflection
options.B: the wavelength of light doubles on reflection
options.C: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, both measured from the normal
options.D: the reflected wavefront travels with half the speed of the incident wavefront

correct_answer: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, both measured from the normal
explanation: In the construction the distance travelled by the wavelet from the first point and the distance travelled by the incident wavefront to reach the mirror are both v x t. The two right triangles formed share the same hypotenuse and have equal perpendiculars, so they are congruent and the two angles are equal.

question: In Huygens geometrical construction, the position of the wavefront after a time t is obtained by drawing:

options.A: a circle passing through the centre of the original wavefront
options.B: the largest single secondary wavelet only
options.C: the common tangent, that is the envelope, to all the secondary wavelets
options.D: a line joining the centres of all the secondary wavelets

correct_answer: the common tangent, that is the envelope, to all the secondary wavelets
explanation: Each point of the old wavefront emits a wavelet of radius v x t. The surface that touches all of these wavelets in the forward direction is the new wavefront at that instant.

question: Light passes from medium 1 of refractive index mu1 and speed v1 into medium 2 of refractive index mu2 and speed v2. Huygens construction gives sin i divided by sin r as:

options.A: v2 / v1, which equals mu1 / mu2
options.C: v1 / v2, which equals mu2 / mu1

correct_answer: v1 / v2, which equals mu2 / mu1
explanation: In the construction the incident wavefront covers v1 x t along the surface while the refracted wavelet covers v2 x t inside medium 2. Dividing the two sine expressions built on the common hypotenuse gives sin i / sin r = v1 / v2, and since mu = c / v this equals mu2 / mu1.

question: Two sources of light are said to be coherent if the waves emitted by them have:

options.A: the same frequency but a rapidly and randomly changing phase difference
options.B: different frequencies but a constant phase difference
options.C: the same amplitude but a continuously changing phase difference
options.D: the same frequency and a constant phase difference between them

correct_answer: the same frequency and a constant phase difference between them
explanation: The positions of the maxima depend on the phase difference between the arriving waves. Only if that phase difference is fixed do the maxima stay at the same places long enough for the eye to see a steady pattern.

question: Two coherent waves of equal amplitude arrive at a point with a path difference of 1.5 λ. At this point the waves interfere:

options.A: destructively, the phase difference being 3 π radian
options.B: destructively, the phase difference being 1.5 π radian
options.C: constructively, the phase difference being 6 π radian
options.D: constructively, the phase difference being 3 π radian

correct_answer: destructively, the phase difference being 3 π radian
explanation: Phase difference = (2 x π / λ) × 1.5 λ = 3 π radian. Since 3 π is an odd multiple of π, the two equal displacements are exactly opposite and the resultant amplitude is zero, so the point is dark.

question: For a steady and clearly visible interference pattern, which condition is essential?

options.A: The two sources must have exactly equal intensities
options.B: The two sources must be coherent and must emit light of the same wavelength
options.C: The two sources must emit light continuously in all possible wavelengths
options.D: The two sources must be at least one metre apart

correct_answer: The two sources must be coherent and must emit light of the same wavelength
explanation: If the sources are not coherent the positions of the maxima shift randomly, and if the wavelengths differ the two patterns of different fringe width overlap. Both conditions must hold for a steady visible pattern.

question: Two coherent sources have intensities in the ratio 1 : 4. For the interference pattern produced, the value of (Imax minus Imin) divided by (Imax plus Imin) is:
explanation: Amplitudes are in the ratio 1 : 2, so Imax is proportional to (1 plus 2)² = 9 and Imin is proportional to (2 minus 1)² = 1. Then (9 minus 1) divided by (9 plus 1) = 8 / 10 = 4 / 5.

question: Light from two identical electric lamps placed side by side does not produce an interference pattern because:

options.A: light from a lamp is longitudinal and cannot interfere
options.B: the two lamps emit light of different frequencies only
options.C: the two lamps emit light in independent bursts, so the phase difference between them changes randomly and very rapidly
options.D: the intensity of the lamps is too large for fringes to form

correct_answer: the two lamps emit light in independent bursts, so the phase difference between them changes randomly and very rapidly
explanation: Atoms in each lamp radiate independently in wave trains lasting about 10⁻⁸ s. The phase relation between the two lamps therefore changes millions of times per second, so the maxima shift about far too quickly to be seen and the screen looks uniformly lit.

question: In an interference pattern, bright and dark bands are formed. This shows that:

options.A: light energy is created at the bright bands
options.B: light energy is destroyed at the dark bands
options.C: light energy is only redistributed, the total energy remaining the same
options.D: the law of conservation of energy does not apply to light waves

correct_answer: light energy is only redistributed, the total energy remaining the same
explanation: At a bright band the intensity of two equal sources rises to 4 x I0 and at a dark band it falls to zero. The average over the pattern is 2 x I0, exactly the sum of the two separate intensities, so the total energy is unchanged and only its distribution alters.

question: Two coherent sources of unequal intensities I1 and I2 interfere. The intensity at a point of destructive interference is:

options.C: (square root of I1 minus square root of I2)², which is greater than zero

correct_answer: (square root of I1 minus square root of I2)², which is greater than zero
explanation: Amplitudes are proportional to the square roots of the intensities, so at destructive interference the resultant amplitude is the square root of I1 minus the square root of I2. Squaring gives the minimum intensity, which is zero only if I1 = I2.

question: Two coherent sources have intensities in the ratio 9 : 1. The ratio of the maximum to the minimum intensity in the interference pattern produced by them is:

question: The phenomenon that establishes the transverse nature of light waves is:
explanation: In a longitudinal wave the vibration is along the direction of propagation, so no direction across the ray is special and polarisation is impossible. Light can be polarised by a polaroid, hence its vibrations must be perpendicular to the direction of propagation.

question: A point source of light is placed in a homogeneous isotropic medium. At a short distance from the source the wavefront is:
explanation: In time t the disturbance from the point source covers the same distance v x t in every direction, so all points in the same phase lie on a sphere of radius v x t centred on the source. The wavefront is therefore spherical.

question: Which statement about a ray of light and the corresponding wavefront is correct?

options.A: The ray is the locus of points having the same phase
options.B: The ray always lies along the wavefront
options.C: The ray and the wavefront always make an angle of 45° with each other
options.D: The ray is always perpendicular to the wavefront at the point where it meets it

correct_answer: The ray is always perpendicular to the wavefront at the point where it meets it
explanation: Energy travels outward along the shortest path from one wavefront to the next, which is along the normal to the wavefront. Hence the ray is drawn perpendicular to the wavefront everywhere.

question: For a cylindrical wavefront produced by a long linear source, the amplitude of the wave at perpendicular distance r from the source varies as:
explanation: The energy crossing a cylindrical surface of radius r per second is fixed, and that area is proportional to r. Hence I varies as 1 / r. Using I proportional to A² gives A² proportional to 1 / r, so A varies as 1 divided by the square root of r.

chapter: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments; Wave Optics
question: Which of the following statements is NOT true according to the wave theory of light?

options.A: Light travels faster in water than in air
options.B: Light is propagated as a wave motion
options.C: Every point on a wavefront behaves as a secondary source of light
options.D: The frequency of light does not change when it passes from one medium to another

correct_answer: Light travels faster in water than in air
explanation: For water mu is about 1.33, so the wave theory speed is c divided by 1.33, which is less than c. Wave theory therefore predicts light to be slower in water than in air, and the experiment of Foucault confirmed this.

question: Light coming from a distant star is treated as a plane wavefront near the Earth because:

options.A: only a very small portion of the enormous spherical wavefront reaches the Earth and its curvature is negligible
options.B: the wavefront becomes plane because light loses energy on the way
options.C: a star emits plane wavefronts right from its surface
options.D: the atmosphere of the Earth converts spherical wavefronts into plane wavefronts

correct_answer: only a very small portion of the enormous spherical wavefront reaches the Earth and its curvature is negligible
explanation: The radius of the wavefront at the Earth is of the order of the star distance, which is enormous. A tiny patch of a sphere whose radius is huge has almost zero curvature, so it is treated as a plane wavefront.

question: According to Huygens principle, every point on a given wavefront:

options.A: acts as a sink that absorbs the incoming wave energy
options.B: sends out secondary wavelets only in the backward direction
options.C: acts as a secondary source and sends out secondary wavelets in the forward direction
options.D: remains at rest while the neighbouring points vibrate

correct_answer: acts as a secondary source and sends out secondary wavelets in the forward direction
explanation: The disturbance reaching a point sets it vibrating, and that vibrating point radiates fresh spherical wavelets into the medium ahead. Drawing the common tangent to these forward wavelets after time t gives the wavefront at that later instant.

question: A wavefront of light is best described as:

options.A: the boundary between two media at which light bends
options.B: the path along which the light energy travels
options.C: the surface on which the amplitude of the wave is always zero
options.D: the locus of all points of the medium that vibrate in the same phase

correct_answer: the locus of all points of the medium that vibrate in the same phase
explanation: Every point on a wavefront is reached by the disturbance at the same instant, so all such points oscillate in the same phase. Hence a wavefront is the locus of points having the same phase of vibration.

question: Newton's corpuscular theory and Huygens wave theory differ in their prediction of the speed of light in a denser medium. The experiment on the speed of light in water showed that:

options.A: the speed in water equals that in air, so both theories fail
options.B: the speed in water depends only on the intensity of the light used
options.C: the speed in water is less than that in air, supporting the wave theory
options.D: the speed in water is greater than that in air, supporting the corpuscular theory

correct_answer: the speed in water is less than that in air, supporting the wave theory
explanation: Wave theory requires the speed in water to be c divided by 1.33, that is about 2.25 × 10⁸ m per second, which is smaller than 3 × 10⁸ m per second. Measurement gave the smaller value, so the wave theory prediction was confirmed.

question: In a light wave travelling through a homogeneous medium, the energy is transported:

options.A: along the surface of the wavefront
options.B: in a direction making an angle of 45° with the wavefront
options.C: equally in all directions from every point of the wavefront
options.D: along the normals to the wavefront

correct_answer: along the normals to the wavefront
explanation: Successive wavefronts are separated by the shortest distance along their common normal, and the disturbance moves from one to the next along that normal. Hence the flow of energy is along the rays, which are the normals to the wavefront.

question: Unpolarised light of intensity I0 passes through three polaroids placed one behind the other. The axis of the second makes 30° with that of the first, and the axis of the third makes 30° with that of the second, in the same sense. The final emergent intensity is:
explanation: After the first polaroid the intensity is I0 / 2. After the second it is (I0 / 2) x cos² 30° = (I0 / 2) × 3 / 4 = 3 I0 / 8. After the third it is (3 I0 / 8) x cos² 30° = (3 I0 / 8) × 3 / 4 = 9 I0 / 32.

question: Unpolarised light falls from air on the flat surface of a transparent medium at the polarising angle, and the angle of refraction is found to be 30°. Taking c as 3 × 10⁸ m per second, the refractive index of the medium and the speed of light inside it are:

options.A: square root of 3 and about 5.2 × 10⁸ m per second
options.C: square root of 3, that is about 1.73, and about 1.73 × 10⁸ m per second

correct_answer: square root of 3, that is about 1.73, and about 1.73 × 10⁸ m per second
explanation: Since the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular at the polarising angle, θ B = 90° minus 30° = 60°. Then mu = tan 60° = square root of 3, about 1.73, and v = (3 × 10⁸) divided by 1.73 = about 1.73 × 10⁸ m per second.

question: According to Brewster law, the refractive index mu of a medium and the polarising angle θ B for light incident from air on it are related by:
explanation: At the polarising angle the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular, so the angle of refraction is 90° minus θ B. Putting this in Snell law, mu = sin θ B divided by sin (90° minus θ B) = sin θ B divided by cos θ B = tan θ B.

question: The polarising angle for a certain transparent medium in contact with air is 60°. The critical angle for total internal reflection at the same surface is:

options.A: 30°, since it is the complement of the polarising angle
options.B: 60°, the same as the polarising angle
options.C: the angle whose sine equals the refractive index of the medium
options.D: the angle whose sine is 1 divided by the square root of 3, that is about 35°

explanation: From Brewster law, mu = tan 60° = square root of 3, about 1.73. Then sin of the critical angle = 1 divided by 1.73 = 0.577, so the critical angle is about 35°.

question: Plane polarised light is light in which:

question: A man of height 180 cm has his eyes 10 cm below the top of his head. He wants to see his full image in a vertical plane mirror fixed on a wall. The lower edge of the shortest such mirror must be at a height above the floor of:
explanation: The eyes are at 180 - 10 = 170 cm above the floor. A ray from the feet reaches the eye after reflecting at a point midway in height between the feet and the eye, that is at 170 / 2 = 85 cm above the floor. So the lower edge of the mirror must be at 85 cm. The upper edge lies midway between the eye and the top of the head, at 175 cm, giving a mirror length of 175 - 85 = 90 cm as expected.

question: A boy walks straight towards a fixed vertical plane mirror at 2 m s⁻¹. The speed with which his image approaches him is:
explanation: The mirror is at rest, so v_image = -v_object with respect to the mirror. The boy moves towards the mirror at 2 m s⁻¹ and the image moves towards the mirror at 2 m s⁻¹ from the other side. Their approach speed is 2 + 2 = 4 m s⁻¹.

question: A small object placed between two inclined plane mirrors produces exactly 5 images. The angle between the mirrors is:
explanation: Five images require n - 1 = 5, so n = 6. Then θ = 360 / 6 = 60°. A check confirms 360 / 60 = 6 is even, so the rule n - 1 applies and gives 5 images.

chapter: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments; Wave Optics
question: Consider the two statements about the image formed by a plane mirror. Statement P: the image is always virtual and of the same size as the object. Statement Q: lateral inversion means the image appears upside down. Which of the following is true:

options.A: Both P and Q are wrong
options.B: P is correct and Q is wrong
options.C: P is wrong and Q is correct
options.D: Both P and Q are correct

correct_answer: P is correct and Q is wrong
explanation: A plane mirror always gives a virtual erect image of the same size as the object, so P is correct. Lateral inversion is a reversal of the front to back direction which appears as a left to right exchange; the image stays erect and is not turned upside down, so Q is wrong.

subject: Physics
chapter: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments; Wave Optics
question: Two plane mirrors are inclined at 70°. A ray of light in the plane perpendicular to both suffers one reflection at each mirror. The angle between the original incident ray and the finally emergent ray is:
explanation: The net deviation is 360 - 2 × 70 = 220°. Turning through 220° in one sense is the same as turning through 360 - 220 = 140° in the other, so the angle between the incident and emergent rays is 140°, which equals 2 × 70. A useful check is the right angle case, where 2 × 90 = 180° gives the antiparallel ray.

question: A ray of light falls on a plane mirror and is reflected. Keeping the incident ray fixed, the mirror is rotated through 10° about an axis lying in the mirror and perpendicular to the plane of incidence. The reflected ray turns through:
explanation: When the mirror turns by 10° the normal also turns by 10°, so the angle of incidence changes by 10°. The reflected ray is measured on the other side of the normal, so its direction changes by 10° from the change in angle plus 10° from the turning of the normal, a total of 20°.

subject: Physics

question: Two plane mirrors are fixed at right angles to each other. A ray of light in the plane perpendicular to both mirrors strikes one mirror, reflects, then strikes the second mirror and reflects again. The final emergent ray is:

options.A: antiparallel to the original incident ray
options.B: along the bisector of the angle between the mirrors
options.C: perpendicular to the original incident ray
options.D: parallel to the original incident ray and travelling in the same direction

correct_answer: antiparallel to the original incident ray
explanation: With θ = 90° the total deviation is 360 - 180 = 180°. A deviation of 180° means the emergent ray travels back exactly opposite to the incident ray, that is antiparallel to it. This is the principle of a corner reflector.

question: A person 1.8 m tall wishes to see his complete image in a fixed vertical plane mirror on a wall. The smallest vertical length of mirror that will do this is:
explanation: Rays from the top of the head and from the feet reach the eye after reflection at points midway in height between the eye and those extremes. The mirror therefore needs to span only half the height of the person, that is 1.8 / 2 = 0.9 m. The result does not depend on how far the person stands.

question: A ray of light is incident on a plane mirror at an angle of incidence of 25°. The angle through which the ray is deviated by the mirror is:

explanation: The image lies 40 cm behind the mirror. The object is 40 cm in front. The two are on opposite sides of the mirror, so the separation is 40 + 40 = 80 cm.

chapter: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments; Wave Optics
question: A ray of light travels from water of refractive index 4/3 into glass of refractive index 3/2. If the angle of incidence in water is 30°, the sine of the angle of refraction in the glass is:
explanation: Snell law gives (4/3) sin 30 = (3/2) sin r, so (4/3)(1/2) = (3/2) sin r, that is 2/3 = (3/2) sin r and sin r = (2/3)(2/3) = 4/9. Since 4/9 is less than 1/2, the ray bends towards the normal, as expected on entering the denser medium.

question: A vessel of depth 2d is filled to half its depth with a liquid of refractive index mu_1 and the upper half with an immiscible liquid of refractive index mu_2. Viewed from directly above, the apparent depth of the bottom of the vessel is:
explanation: Each layer of real thickness d contributes an apparent thickness d/mu. The total apparent depth is d/mu_1 + d/mu_2 = d(mu_2 + mu_1)/(mu_1 mu_2). As a check, putting mu_1 = mu_2 = mu gives 2d/mu, the standard single liquid result.

question: The absolute refractive indices of glass and water are 3/2 and 4/3 respectively. The refractive index of glass with respect to water is:
explanation: The refractive index of glass with respect to water is mu_glass / mu_water = (3/2) / (4/3) = (3/2) × (3/4) = 9/8 = 1.125. It exceeds one, confirming that glass is optically denser than water.

chapter: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments; Wave Optics
question: A microscope is focused on a mark at the bottom of an empty beaker. Water of refractive index 4/3 is poured in to a depth of 8 cm and the microscope has to be raised to refocus. The water is then poured out and replaced by the same depth of a liquid of refractive index 1.6. Compared with the water setting, the microscope must now be raised further by:
explanation: With water the shift is 8(1 - 3/4) = 8 × 0.25 = 2 cm. With the new liquid the shift is 8(1 - 1/1.6) = 8(1 - 0.625) = 8 × 0.375 = 3 cm. The microscope was already raised by 2 cm, so it must be raised a further 3 - 2 = 1 cm.

chapter: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments; Wave Optics
question: Light of wavelength 600 nm in air travels through a 6 cm thickness of a medium of refractive index 1.5. The number of complete waves contained in this path is:
explanation: Inside the medium the wavelength is 600/1.5 = 400 nm = 4 × 10⁻⁷ m. The path is 6 cm = 6 × 10⁻² m. The number of waves is (6 × 10⁻²)/(4 × 10⁻⁷) = 1.5 × 10⁵. Equivalently the optical path is mu x 6 cm = 9 cm and dividing that by the air wavelength gives the same count.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
source_chapter: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments; Wave Optics

subject: Physics
chapter: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments; Wave Optics
question: A ray of light travelling in air is incident obliquely on the flat surface of water of refractive index 4/3. Compared with the angle of incidence, the angle of refraction is:

options.A: smaller, the ray bending away from the normal
options.B: equal, the ray continuing without any bending
options.C: larger, the ray bending away from the normal
options.D: smaller, the ray bending towards the normal

correct_answer: smaller, the ray bending towards the normal
explanation: Snell law gives sin i / sin r = mu_water / mu_air = 4/3, which is greater than one. Hence sin r is less than sin i and r is less than i. A smaller angle with the normal means the ray has bent towards the normal on entering the denser medium.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
source_chapter: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments; Wave Optics
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 16: Optics

chapter: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments; Wave Optics
question: A mark on a sheet of paper is viewed from directly above through a glass slab 6 cm thick of refractive index 1.5. The mark appears to be raised by:
explanation: The shift is t(1 - 1/mu) = 6(1 - 1/1.5) = 6(1 - 2/3) = 6 × 1/3 = 2 cm. Equivalently the slab of real thickness 6 cm looks only 6/1.5 = 4 cm thick, so the mark rises by 6 - 4 = 2 cm.

chapter: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments; Wave Optics
question: A ray of light strikes a glass slab of thickness 6 cm at an angle of incidence of 60°. The refractive index of the glass is the square root of 3. The lateral shift of the emergent ray is:
explanation: Snell law gives sin r = sin 60 / √(3) = (0.866)/(1.732) = 0.5, so r = 30°. The lateral shift is t sin(i - r)/cos r = 6 x sin 30 / cos 30 = 6 × 0.5 / 0.866 = 3.46 cm, which is 2 times the square root of 3 centimetres.

chapter: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments; Wave Optics
question: A swimming pool is filled with water of refractive index 4/3 to a depth of 4 m. Seen from directly above, the bottom appears to be at a depth of:
explanation: Apparent depth = real depth / mu = 4 / (4/3) = 4 × 3/4 = 3 m. The bottom appears raised by 4 - 3 = 1 m, which is why pools always look shallower than they are.

question: Light of wavelength 600 nm in vacuum enters a medium of refractive index 1.5. Its wavelength in the medium is:
explanation: The frequency stays the same, so lambda_medium / lambda_vacuum = v / c = 1/mu. Hence lambda_medium = 600 / 1.5 = 400 nm. The light still appears the same colour to the eye because colour is set by frequency.
