syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: A sample of hydrogen atoms is excited so that the electrons occupy the level n = 4. The maximum number of different spectral lines that can be emitted as the atoms return to the ground state is:
explanation: Each distinct pair of levels among n = 1, 2, 3 and 4 gives one spectral line. The number of such pairs is 4 × 3/2 = 6. Listing them, the transitions are from 4 to 3, 4 to 2, 4 to 1, 3 to 2, 3 to 1 and 2 to 1. Three of these belong to the Lyman series, two to the Balmer series and one to the Paschen series.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The ratio of the shortest wavelength of the Lyman series to the shortest wavelength of the Balmer series of atomic hydrogen is:
explanation: Setting the upper level to infinity, the shortest wavelength of a series is λ = n_1²/R. For the Lyman series n₁ = 1, giving 1/R, and for the Balmer series n₁ = 2, giving 4/R. The ratio is therefore 1 : 4. Numerically this is 912 Å against 3647 Å, which indeed differ by a factor of four.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Among the following transitions in atomic hydrogen, the one that produces radiation of the shortest wavelength is:

options.A: from a very high level to n = 2
options.B: from a very high level to n = 1

correct_answer: from a very high level to n = 1
explanation: The photon energy is the difference between the two level energies. The greatest possible difference is obtained by falling from the top of the ladder, where the energy is essentially zero, to the deepest level, n = 1, at -13.6 eV. That gives 13.6 eV and a wavelength of 912 Å. Every other listed transition releases less energy and so gives a longer wavelength.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Taking the ground state energy of hydrogen as -13.6 eV and h c = 12400 eV angstrom, the shortest wavelength present in the Lyman series is nearest to:
explanation: The series limit photon carries the full ionisation energy of the ground state, 13.6 eV. Using λ = 12400/13.6 Å gives 911.8 Å, so about 912 Å. Every other Lyman line has a smaller photon energy and hence a longer wavelength.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The series limit of the Lyman series of atomic hydrogen corresponds to a transition from:
explanation: As the upper level rises, the term 1/n_2² tends to zero and the photon energy approaches its greatest value. For the Lyman series this limiting energy is 13.6 eV, produced when a free electron with negligible kinetic energy is captured into the ground state. The corresponding wavelength, 912 Å, is the shortest in the series.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: For hydrogen E_n = -13.6/n² eV and h c = 12400 eV angstrom. The wavelength of the second line of the Balmer series is nearest to:
explanation: The first Balmer line comes from n = 3 to n = 2, so the second comes from n = 4 to n = 2. Its photon energy is 13.6 (1/4 - 1/16) = 13.6 × 3/16 = 2.55 eV. The wavelength is 12400/2.55 = 4863 Å, which is blue green light.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The lines of the Balmer series of atomic hydrogen arise from transitions in which the electron finally arrives at the level:
explanation: In the Balmer series the electron drops from any level with n greater than 2 down to n = 2. The first line, from n = 3 to n = 2, has a photon energy of 1.89 eV and a wavelength of about 6563 Å, which is red light. Four Balmer lines fall in the visible region, which is why this series was discovered first.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: All the lines of the Lyman series of atomic hydrogen lie in the:
explanation: Every Lyman line corresponds to an electron falling to n = 1, so the smallest photon energy in the series is 13.6 - 3.4 = 10.2 eV and the largest is 13.6 eV. Using h c = 12400 eV angstrom, these correspond to wavelengths of 1216 Å and 912 Å, both well short of the violet limit of about 4000 Å. The whole series therefore lies in the ultraviolet.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: In terms of the Rydberg constant R, the wavelength of the first line of the Lyman series of atomic hydrogen is:
explanation: Substituting the quantum numbers, 1/λ = R (1/1 - 1/4) = 3R/4. Taking the reciprocal gives λ = 4/(3R). With R = 1.097 × 10⁷ m⁻¹ this evaluates to 1.216 × 10⁻⁷ m, in agreement with the value 1216 Å.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: For hydrogen E_n = -13.6/n² eV and h c = 12400 eV angstrom. The longest wavelength line of the Lyman series has a wavelength nearest to:
explanation: The smallest photon energy in the Lyman series comes from the closest pair of levels, n = 2 down to n = 1. That energy is 13.6 (1/1 - 1/4) = 13.6 × 0.75 = 10.2 eV. The wavelength is 12400/10.2 = 1215.7 Å, so about 1216 Å.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: A hydrogen atom emits a photon of energy 2.55 eV. Taking E_n = -13.6/n² eV, the transition responsible is:
explanation: The levels are E₁ = -13.6 eV, E₂ = -3.40 eV, E₃ = -1.51 eV and E₄ = -0.85 eV. The difference between the level at -0.85 eV and the level at -3.40 eV is 2.55 eV, which matches the emitted photon exactly. So the electron has fallen from n = 4 to n = 2, giving the second line of the Balmer series at 4863 Å.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: For a one electron ion of atomic number Z the level energies are E_n = -13.6 Z²/n² eV. In a singly ionised helium ion the transition that emits a photon of exactly the same energy as the transition from n = 2 to n = 1 in hydrogen is:
explanation: In hydrogen the transition from n = 2 to n = 1 releases 13.6 (1 - 1/4) = 10.2 eV. For the helium ion Z = 2, so the level energies are E_n = -54.4/n² eV, giving E₁ = -54.4, E₂ = -13.6, E₃ = -6.04 and E₄ = -3.4 eV. The difference between the level at -3.4 eV and the level at -13.6 eV is 10.2 eV, matching the hydrogen line exactly. In general, multiplying every quantum number by Z reproduces the hydrogen spectrum.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The Paschen series of atomic hydrogen consists of transitions ending at n = 3 and its lines lie in the:
explanation: The most energetic Paschen photon is the series limit, of energy 13.6/9 = 1.51 eV, and its wavelength is 12400/1.51 = 8200 Å. Since visible light stops at about 7500 Å, every Paschen line is longer in wavelength than visible red light and so lies in the infrared.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Transitions of a hydrogen atom that terminate at the n = 2 level form the:
explanation: The Balmer series consists of transitions from higher levels to n = 2 and lies mainly in the visible region.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: In a nuclear reaction the total rest mass decreases by 0.02 u. Taking 1 u as 931.5 MeV and 1 eV as 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, the energy released is nearest to:
explanation: First the energy in MeV is 0.02 × 931.5 = 18.63 MeV. Expressed in electron volt this is 1.863 × 10⁷ eV. Multiplying by 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J per eV gives 2.98 × 10⁻¹² J, so about 3.0 × 10⁻¹² J. For comparison, a chemical reaction between two atoms releases only a few times 10⁻¹⁹ J, which is why nuclear processes are millions of times more energetic.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: A nucleus of mass number 16 has a total binding energy of 128 MeV. Its binding energy per nucleon is:
explanation: Dividing, 128/16 = 8 MeV per nucleon. This value sits close to the flat top of the binding energy curve, so a nuclide of this kind is comparatively tightly bound.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The total binding energy of a helium nucleus, which contains two protons and two neutrons, is 28 MeV. Its binding energy per nucleon is:
explanation: The helium nucleus contains four nucleons, so the binding energy per nucleon is 28/4 = 7 MeV. This is unusually high for such a light nucleus, which is why the helium nucleus is emitted as a unit in alpha decay.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The mass of a proton is 1.00728 u, the mass of a neutron is 1.00867 u and the mass of a helium nucleus is 4.00151 u. Taking 1 u as 931.5 MeV, the binding energy of the helium nucleus is nearest to:
explanation: The constituent mass is 2 × 1.00728 + 2 × 1.00867 = 2.01456 + 2.01734 = 4.03190 u. Subtracting the actual nuclear mass, delta m = 4.03190 - 4.00151 = 0.03039 u. Multiplying by 931.5 gives 28.31 MeV. Dividing by four nucleons gives about 7.08 MeV per nucleon.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The property of the nuclear force that is directly responsible for the binding energy per nucleon being nearly the same over a wide range of mass numbers is that the force is:

options.A: attractive at every separation, however small
options.B: charge independent between any pair of nucleons
options.C: much stronger than the electrostatic force at all separations
options.D: short ranged, so that each nucleon interacts only with its nearest neighbours

correct_answer: short ranged, so that each nucleon interacts only with its nearest neighbours
explanation: If every nucleon attracted every other nucleon, the total binding energy would grow roughly as the square of the mass number and the binding energy per nucleon would rise steadily with A. In fact the nuclear force acts only over about one femtometre, so a nucleon deep inside a nucleus is bound to a fixed small number of neighbours no matter how large the nucleus is. The total binding energy therefore grows in proportion to A and the binding energy per nucleon stays nearly constant, which is the property called saturation.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Among several nuclides, the most stable is the one with the largest:
explanation: The total binding energy of a heavy nucleus is large simply because it contains many nucleons. To compare nuclei of different sizes one must ask how tightly each individual nucleon is held, which is the binding energy divided by the mass number. Iron group nuclei, with about 8.8 MeV per nucleon, are the most stable on this measure even though uranium has a far larger total binding energy.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The mass of a proton is 1.00728 u, the mass of a neutron is 1.00867 u and the mass of a deuteron nucleus is 1.00728 u plus 1.00867 u less 0.00240 u. Taking 1 u as 931.5 MeV, the binding energy of the deuteron is nearest to:
explanation: The mass defect is stated to be 0.00240 u. Multiplying, 0.00240 × 931.5 = 2.2356 MeV, so about 2.24 MeV. Dividing by the two nucleons gives a binding energy per nucleon of only about 1.1 MeV, which is why the deuteron is a very loosely bound nucleus.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The binding energy of a certain nucleus is 931.5 MeV. Its mass defect is:
explanation: Dividing, 931.5/931.5 = 1, so the mass defect is exactly 1 u, which is 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. A nucleus whose constituents lose a whole atomic mass unit on assembly is a moderately heavy one; for comparison, the helium nucleus loses only about 0.03 u.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Four nuclides P, Q, R and S have binding energies per nucleon of 7.6 MeV, 8.8 MeV, 7.1 MeV and 1.1 MeV respectively. The most stable of them is:
explanation: Comparing the four values, 8.8 MeV per nucleon is the largest, so the nuclide Q is held together most tightly per nucleon and is the most stable. The value 8.8 MeV corresponds to the peak of the binding energy curve near mass number 56, while 1.1 MeV per nucleon is characteristic of the very loosely bound deuteron.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: A nucleus of mass number 240 and binding energy per nucleon 7.6 MeV splits into two fragments each of mass number 120 and binding energy per nucleon 8.5 MeV. The energy released is:
explanation: The parent has a total binding energy of 240 × 7.6 = 1824 MeV. The two fragments together have 240 × 8.5 = 2040 MeV. The difference, 2040 - 1824 = 216 MeV, is released. Equivalently the gain of 0.9 MeV per nucleon is multiplied by the 240 nucleons involved.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: A nuclear reaction releases energy whenever the products, compared with the reactants, have:

options.C: a greater total number of nucleons

explanation: Binding energy is the energy that was given up when nucleons assembled. If the products are more tightly bound than the reactants, the extra binding energy appears as kinetic energy of the products and as radiation. Equivalently, the total rest mass falls and the lost mass appears as energy. Both fission of very heavy nuclei and fusion of very light ones move the system towards the peak of the binding energy curve, so both release energy.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The total binding energy of a nuclide of mass number 16 is 128 MeV, and the total binding energy of the nuclide of the same element with mass number 15 is 112 MeV. The energy needed to remove one neutron from the heavier nuclide is:
explanation: Removing a neutron leaves a nuclide of the same element with one fewer nucleon. Since a free neutron has zero binding energy, the energy that must be supplied equals the loss of binding energy, that is 128 - 112 = 16 MeV. Note that this is twice the average binding energy per nucleon of 8 MeV, which shows that the separation energy of a particular nucleon can differ considerably from the average value.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Two deuterons, each of mass number 2 and binding energy per nucleon 1.1 MeV, fuse to form a helium nucleus of mass number 4 and binding energy per nucleon 7.0 MeV. The energy released is:
explanation: The helium nucleus has a total binding energy of 4 × 7.0 = 28.0 MeV. Each deuteron has 2 × 1.1 = 2.2 MeV, so the two together have 4.4 MeV. The energy released is 28.0 - 4.4 = 23.6 MeV. The reaction releases energy because the product lies much higher on the binding energy curve than the reactants.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: One unified atomic mass unit is equivalent to an energy of:
explanation: Multiplying 1.66 × 10⁻²⁷ kg by the square of 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹ gives 1.49 × 10⁻¹⁰ J. Dividing by 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J per eV gives 9.315 × 10⁸ eV, that is 931.5 MeV. This conversion turns any mass defect expressed in atomic mass units straight into a binding energy in MeV.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The mass defect of a certain nucleus is 0.5 u. Taking 1 u as equivalent to 931.5 MeV, the binding energy of this nucleus is:
explanation: Multiplying, 0.5 × 931.5 = 465.75 MeV. This is the energy that would have to be supplied to pull the nucleus apart into its separate free nucleons, and equally the energy that was released when they came together.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The mass defect of a nucleus is defined as:

options.A: the difference between the mass number and the atomic number of the nuclide
options.B: the amount by which the mass of the nucleus exceeds the sum of the masses of its free nucleons
options.C: the amount by which the sum of the masses of its free nucleons exceeds the mass of the nucleus
options.D: the difference between the mass of the nucleus and the mass of an equal number of protons

correct_answer: the amount by which the sum of the masses of its free nucleons exceeds the mass of the nucleus
explanation: When free nucleons combine to form a nucleus, energy is released, and by the mass energy relation the assembled nucleus is lighter than its separated constituents. The missing mass is the mass defect. For a stable nucleus it is always positive, and multiplying it by c squared gives the binding energy.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Nuclides that have the same mass number but different atomic numbers are called:
explanation: Isobars contain the same total number of nucleons but distribute them differently between protons and neutrons, so they are different chemical elements. The nuclide with Z = 18 and A = 40 and the nuclide with Z = 20 and A = 40 form a familiar pair. Since the mass number is the same, isobars have very nearly equal masses and, by the relation R = R₀ A¹⁄³, equal nuclear radii.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The density of nuclear matter is about 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³ and the density of water is 1.0 × 10³ kg m⁻³. Nuclear matter is denser than water by a factor of about:
explanation: Dividing, 2.3 × 10¹⁷ divided by 1.0 × 10³ gives 2.3 × 10¹⁴. So a spoonful of nuclear matter would weigh as much as a mountain of ordinary matter. The huge factor reflects the fact that atoms are almost entirely empty, with the mass confined to a volume about 10⁻¹⁵ of the atomic volume.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The radius R of a nucleus of mass number A is well described by the relation:
explanation: Experiments show that the volume of a nucleus is proportional to the number of nucleons it contains. Since volume is proportional to the cube of the radius, R³ is proportional to A and hence R is proportional to A¹⁄³. Writing the constant of proportionality as R₀ gives R = R₀ A¹⁄³ with R₀ about 1.2 fm.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The radius of a certain nucleus is measured to be 4.8 × 10⁻¹⁵ m. Taking R₀ = 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m, the mass number of this nuclide is:
explanation: Dividing, R/R₀ = 4.8/1.2 = 4. Cubing this gives A = 4³ = 64. As a check, the cube root of 64 is 4 and 1.2 × 4 = 4.8 fm, which is the given radius.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: A nucleus of mass number 64 has radius R. Among the nuclides listed, the one whose nuclear radius is 1.25 R has mass number:
explanation: The mass number varies as the cube of the radius, so A₂ = 64 × (1.25)³. Now (1.25)³ = 1.953125, and 64 × 1.953125 = 125. So a nuclide of mass number 125 has a radius 1.25 times that of a nuclide of mass number 64, since the cube roots are 5 and 4 respectively.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Two nuclides are said to be isotopes of each other when they have:

options.A: the same atomic number but different mass numbers
options.B: the same mass number but different atomic numbers
options.C: the same number of neutrons and the same number of protons
options.D: the same number of neutrons but different atomic numbers

correct_answer: the same atomic number but different mass numbers
explanation: The atomic number Z fixes the chemical element, so isotopes are different forms of the same element. They contain the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, so their mass numbers differ. Hydrogen with mass numbers 1, 2 and 3 is the standard example. Isotopes have almost identical chemical behaviour because chemistry depends on the electron count, which equals Z.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: As the mass number of a nucleus increases, the density of nuclear matter:

options.A: stays practically the same for all nuclei
options.B: decreases in inverse proportion to the mass number
options.C: increases in direct proportion to the mass number
options.D: increases in proportion to the cube root of the mass number

correct_answer: stays practically the same for all nuclei
explanation: The mass of a nucleus is about A times the nucleon mass m, while its volume is (4/3) π R³ = (4/3) π R_0³ A. Dividing, the mass number cancels and the density becomes 3m/(4 π R_0³), a constant of about 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³. Nuclear matter therefore has the same density in a light nucleus as in a heavy one, which is why nuclear matter is often described as incompressible.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Two nuclei X and Y have mass numbers 8 and 216 respectively. The ratio of the radius of X to that of Y and the ratio of the density of X to that of Y are respectively:
explanation: The cube root of 8 is 2 and the cube root of 216 is 6, so the radii are in the ratio 2 : 6, that is 1 : 3. For the density, the mass is proportional to A and the volume is also proportional to A, so the two dependences cancel exactly and every nucleus has the same density. The density ratio is therefore 1 : 1. This constancy is the physical content behind the empirical radius relation.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Two nuclei have mass numbers 16 and 128. The ratio of their nuclear volumes is:
explanation: Since R = R₀ A¹⁄³, the volume (4/3) π R³ equals (4/3) π R_0³ A, which is directly proportional to the mass number. Hence the volumes are in the ratio 16 : 128, that is 1 : 8. The radii themselves are in the ratio 1 : 2, being the cube roots of 16 and 128.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Two nuclides are isotones when they contain:

options.A: the same total number of nucleons
options.B: the same ratio of neutrons to protons

explanation: The neutron number is N = A - Z. Isotones have equal N but different Z and different A. The nuclide with Z = 6 and A = 14 has eight neutrons, and so does the nuclide with Z = 8 and A = 16, so these two are isotones.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Consider the nuclide P with Z = 6 and A = 14 and the nuclide Q with Z = 8 and A = 16. These two nuclides are:
explanation: For the nuclide P the neutron number is 14 - 6 = 8. For the nuclide Q it is 16 - 8 = 8. The neutron numbers agree while both the atomic numbers and the mass numbers differ, so the pair are isotones.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Taking R₀ = 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m and the mass of a nucleon as 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, the density of nuclear matter is nearest to:
explanation: The mass number cancels, leaving ρ = m divided by (4/3) π R_0³. First R_0³ = (1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵)³ = 1.728 × 10⁻⁴⁵ m³. Multiplying by 4 π/3 = 4.19 gives a volume per nucleon of 7.24 × 10⁻⁴⁵ m³. Dividing the nucleon mass by this, ρ = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷/7.24 × 10⁻⁴⁵ = 2.3 × 10¹⁷ kg m⁻³.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Two nuclei have mass numbers 27 and 125. The ratio of their nuclear radii is:
explanation: Taking cube roots, the cube root of 27 is 3 and the cube root of 125 is 5. Hence the radii are in the ratio 3 : 5. The mass numbers differ by a factor of about 4.6 while the radii differ by less than a factor of 2, which shows how slowly nuclear size grows with mass.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: A nuclide has atomic number 92 and mass number 238. The number of neutrons in its nucleus is:
explanation: The mass number counts protons and neutrons together, so the neutron number is N = A - Z = 238 - 92 = 146. Heavy nuclei carry many more neutrons than protons because the extra neutrons help to offset the mutual electrostatic repulsion of the protons.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The nucleus of a nuclide X has twice the radius of the nucleus of a nuclide Y. The mass number of X is greater than that of Y by a factor of:
explanation: Inverting the radius relation gives A = (R/R₀)³, so the mass number varies as the cube of the radius. Doubling the radius therefore multiplies the mass number by 2 cubed, that is by 8. Equivalently the nuclear volume, and hence the number of nucleons, has increased eightfold.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Taking R₀ = 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m, the radius of a nucleus of mass number 27 is:
explanation: The cube root of 27 is 3, so R = 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ x 3 = 3.6 × 10⁻¹⁵ m, that is 3.6 fm. This is roughly one hundred thousand times smaller than the radius of the corresponding atom.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: Statement I: Fusion of light nuclei can release energy. Statement II: The products may have greater binding energy per nucleon than the reactants.

options.A: Both statements are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
options.B: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.C: Both statements are correct but Statement II does not explain Statement I
options.D: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

correct_answer: Both statements are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
explanation: A rise in binding energy per nucleon corresponds to a decrease in total mass, and the mass difference is released as energy.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: A nuclear reaction has a positive Q-value. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Energy is absorbed from the surroundings
options.B: The products have greater rest mass by Qc²
options.D: The total rest mass of products is smaller than that of reactants

correct_answer: The total rest mass of products is smaller than that of reactants
explanation: For released energy Q, the mass decrease is Δm = Q/c²; charge and nucleon number remain conserved.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: If the mass number of a nucleus becomes eight times, its radius becomes approximately:
explanation: Nuclear radius R = R₀A¹⁄³; multiplying A by 8 multiplies R by 2.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The binding energy per nucleon is greatest for nuclei near the middle of the mass-number range. This explains why energy can be released by:

options.B: Both fusion of light nuclei and fission of very heavy nuclei

correct_answer: Both fusion of light nuclei and fission of very heavy nuclei
explanation: Both processes move products toward higher binding energy per nucleon, reducing total mass and releasing energy.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The number of alpha particles scattered per unit time into a given small angular range about a scattering angle θ is proportional to 1/(sin(θ/2))⁴. The ratio of the number scattered at 60° to the number scattered at 120° is:
explanation: At θ = 60°, sin(θ/2) = sin 30° = 1/2, so (sin(θ/2))⁴ = 1/16 and N is proportional to 16. At θ = 120°, sin(θ/2) = sin 60° = 0.866, so (sin(θ/2))⁴ = (0.75)² = 0.5625 and N is proportional to 1/0.5625 = 1.78. The required ratio is 16 divided by 1.78, which is 9. So nine times as many alpha particles appear at 60° as at 120°.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The occurrence of a small number of alpha particles scattered through very large angles was taken by Rutherford as evidence that:

options.A: the atom contains an equal number of positive and negative charges
options.B: the positive charge and almost the whole mass of the atom are concentrated in a very small volume
options.C: the electrons inside the atom are arranged in fixed circular shells
options.D: the nuclear force between the alpha particle and the target is attractive

correct_answer: the positive charge and almost the whole mass of the atom are concentrated in a very small volume
explanation: To turn an energetic alpha particle through more than 90° the repulsive Coulomb force must be enormous, which is possible only if the alpha particle can approach very close to a large positive charge. In a uniformly spread positive charge the field inside falls towards zero at the centre and no such force arises. The rare violent deflections therefore require the positive charge to be compressed into a tiny volume, and since the alpha particle is scarcely able to move that centre, essentially all the atomic mass must sit there too.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: A proton of kinetic energy K is fired head on at a fixed nucleus and stops at a distance d from its centre. An alpha particle of kinetic energy 4K is then fired head on at the same nucleus. Its distance of closest approach is:
explanation: For the proton, d = (1/(4 π ε₀)) (1)(Z) e² / K. For the alpha particle the projectile charge is doubled and the kinetic energy is four times larger, so its closest approach is (1/(4 π ε₀)) (2)(Z) e² / (4K), which equals one half of the proton value. Hence the alpha particle stops at d/2.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: The principal failure of Rutherford's nuclear model of the atom is that, according to classical electromagnetism, the orbiting electron should:

options.A: move with a speed greater than the speed of light in the innermost orbit
options.B: be pulled out of the atom by the repulsion of the nuclear charge
options.C: radiate continuously, lose energy and spiral into the nucleus in a very short time
options.D: have an angular momentum that decreases in fixed steps of h/(2 π)

correct_answer: radiate continuously, lose energy and spiral into the nucleus in a very short time
explanation: In the Rutherford picture the electron moves in a circle, so it has a centripetal acceleration. Classical electrodynamics requires an accelerated charge to emit electromagnetic radiation, so the electron would steadily lose energy, its orbital radius would shrink and it would fall into the nucleus in a time of the order of 10⁻⁸ s. The model therefore predicts that no atom can be stable. It also predicts a continuously changing frequency of emitted radiation, that is a continuous spectrum, whereas atoms in fact emit sharp lines.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: In Rutherford scattering, the alpha particles that are scattered through the largest angles are those for which the impact parameter is:

options.A: equal to the nuclear radius, so that the alpha particle grazes the nuclear surface
options.B: largest, so that the alpha particle spends the longest time near the nucleus
options.C: smallest, tending to zero for a head on collision
options.D: equal to the atomic radius, so that the alpha particle enters the electron cloud

correct_answer: smallest, tending to zero for a head on collision
explanation: The impact parameter is the perpendicular distance between the initial line of motion and the parallel line through the nucleus. A small impact parameter brings the alpha particle deep into the strong Coulomb field near the nucleus, so the repulsive impulse is large and the deflection is large. In the limit b tending to zero the alpha particle travels straight at the nucleus, is brought to rest at the distance of closest approach and is thrown straight back, giving a scattering angle of 180°. Large impact parameters correspond to weak, distant encounters and small angles.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: An alpha particle fired head on at a heavy nucleus comes to rest momentarily at a distance r from the centre of the nucleus. If an identical alpha particle is fired head on at the same nucleus with twice the kinetic energy, the corresponding distance becomes:
explanation: Equating the initial kinetic energy to the electrostatic potential energy at the turning point gives K = (1/(4 π ε₀)) × (2e)(Ze)/r₀. Rearranging, r₀ = (1/(4 π ε₀)) × 2 Z e² / K, so r₀ varies inversely with the kinetic energy. Doubling K therefore halves the distance of closest approach, giving r/2.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: In the alpha particle scattering experiment gold was rolled into an extremely thin foil mainly because:

options.A: a thin foil increases the total number of nuclei that each alpha particle meets
options.B: a thin foil makes multiple successive scatterings of the same alpha particle very unlikely
options.C: gold nuclei are lighter than the alpha particles and so recoil strongly
options.D: gold is the only metal that does not absorb alpha particles at all

correct_answer: a thin foil makes multiple successive scatterings of the same alpha particle very unlikely
explanation: Rutherford's analysis assumes that a given deflection is produced by one encounter with one nucleus. If the foil were thick, an alpha particle would suffer many small deflections whose combined effect could not be traced to a single Coulomb encounter, and the angular distribution would be meaningless. Gold was chosen because it can be beaten into foils only a few hundred atoms thick and because its large atomic number gives strong Coulomb deflection.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: In the alpha particle scattering experiment the number of alpha particles that were turned back through angles greater than 90° was found to be roughly:
explanation: Geiger and Marsden found that only about one alpha particle in every eight thousand was scattered through an angle exceeding 90°. Rutherford described this as being as surprising as a shell bouncing back from tissue paper. The rarity of the event shows that the target responsible for it occupies only a minute fraction of the atomic cross section, of the order of 10⁻⁵ of the atomic radius in linear size.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: An alpha particle and a proton, each of kinetic energy 5 MeV, are fired head on at the same heavy nucleus. The ratio of the distance of closest approach of the alpha particle to that of the proton is:
explanation: For a projectile of charge z e the turning point satisfies K = (1/(4 π ε₀)) z Z e² / r₀, so at fixed kinetic energy and fixed target r₀ is proportional to z. The alpha particle has z = 2 and the proton has z = 1, hence the ratio of closest approaches is 2 : 1. The alpha particle, being more strongly repelled, is turned back sooner.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: According to the nuclear model of the atom, the ratio of the radius of the nucleus to the radius of the atom is of the order of:
explanation: A typical nuclear radius is a few times 10⁻¹⁵ m while a typical atomic radius is about 10⁻¹⁰ m. Dividing gives a ratio of order 10⁻⁵, so the nucleus is about one hundred thousand times smaller in linear size than the atom. In terms of volume the nucleus occupies only about 10⁻¹⁵ of the atomic volume, which is why the atom is described as almost entirely empty.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: An alpha particle of kinetic energy 7.2 MeV is fired head on towards a stationary nucleus of atomic number 50. Taking (1/(4 π ε₀)) e² = 1.44 MeV fm, the distance of closest approach is:
explanation: Substituting the data, r₀ = 2 × 50 × 1.44 MeV fm / 7.2 MeV. The numerator is 100 × 1.44 = 144 MeV fm. Dividing by 7.2 MeV gives r₀ = 20 fm, that is 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁴ m. Note that this is much larger than an actual nuclear radius, which is why the alpha particle never touches the nucleus and pure Coulomb scattering applies.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: In Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment almost all the alpha particles passed through the thin gold foil without any appreciable deviation. This observation leads directly to the conclusion that:

options.A: most of the space inside an atom is empty
options.B: the positive charge of the atom is spread uniformly over its whole volume
options.C: the electrons in the atom are at rest at fixed points
options.D: the alpha particles are much heavier than the gold atoms

correct_answer: most of the space inside an atom is empty
explanation: An alpha particle is deflected only when it comes close to a concentrated centre of positive charge. Since the overwhelming majority of alpha particles emerge along their original direction, they must have travelled through regions containing no such centre. Hence the volume of an atom is mostly empty space, with the positive charge and nearly all the mass packed into a very small nucleus.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 18: Atoms and Nuclei

subject: Physics
question: A semiconductor of conductivity 5 S m⁻¹ is subjected to a uniform electric field of 40 V m⁻¹. The current density in it is:
explanation: J = sigma E = 5 × 40 = 200 A m⁻². To obtain an actual current one would still have to multiply by the area of cross section of the sample.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: As the temperature of a semiconductor is raised, the mobility of its charge carriers:

options.A: falls, because stronger lattice vibrations scatter the carriers more frequently
options.B: rises, because more carriers become available to share the current between them
options.C: rises, because the carriers acquire larger thermal speeds at higher temperature
options.D: stays constant, because mobility depends only on the strength of the applied field

correct_answer: falls, because stronger lattice vibrations scatter the carriers more frequently
explanation: Mobility is proportional to the average time a carrier travels between collisions. Heating increases the amplitude of the lattice vibrations, so collisions occur more often and this time falls. The mobility therefore decreases with temperature, even though the conductivity of the semiconductor rises because far more carriers become available.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: In a semiconductor the electrons and the holes drift in opposite directions, and their mobilities are different. Which statement about the resulting current is correct?

options.A: only the carrier with the larger mobility contributes, the other being effectively at rest
options.B: the two carriers have opposite charges as well as opposite drift directions, so both contributions point the same way and simply add
options.C: the two contributions point in opposite directions, so the net current is the difference of the two
options.D: the two contributions add only in the special case where the two mobilities happen to be equal

correct_answer: the two carriers have opposite charges as well as opposite drift directions, so both contributions point the same way and simply add
explanation: A hole of charge +e drifts along E, giving a conventional current along E. An electron of charge -e drifts opposite to E, and a negative charge moving backwards is again a conventional current along E. Both contributions therefore point along the field and add, giving J = e (n_e mu_e + n_h mu_h) E. The mobilities fix only how large each share is.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: A doped semiconductor has n_e = 3 × 10²¹ m⁻³, n_h = 1 × 10²¹ m⁻³, mu_e = 0.3 m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ and mu_h = 0.1 m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹. Taking e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, its conductivity is:
explanation: n_e mu_e = 3 × 10²¹ x 0.3 = 9 × 10²⁰ and n_h mu_h = 1 × 10²¹ x 0.1 = 1 × 10²⁰. Their sum is 1.0 × 10²¹. Then sigma = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ x 1.0 × 10²¹ = 160 S m⁻¹.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: A potential difference of 2 V is applied across a semiconductor bar of length 1 cm. If the electron mobility is 0.35 m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, the electron drift speed is:
explanation: E = V / l = 2 / (1 × 10⁻²) = 200 V m⁻¹. Then v_d = mu E = 0.35 × 200 = 70 m s⁻¹. Note how much larger this is than the drift speed of order 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹ found in a metal wire, because the carrier concentration here is far smaller.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: The SI unit of the mobility of a charge carrier is:
explanation: The drift speed is measured in m s⁻¹ and the electric field in V m⁻¹. Dividing gives (m s⁻¹) × (m V⁻¹) = m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹. Typical values are a few tenths of this unit for electrons and holes in silicon and germanium.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: Three materials, glass, germanium and silver, are compared at room temperature. Arranged in order of increasing electrical conductivity they are:
explanation: Glass is an insulator with conductivity of order 10⁻¹² S m⁻¹ or less, germanium is a semiconductor with conductivity of the order of a few S m⁻¹, and silver is the best metallic conductor with conductivity of the order of 10⁷ S m⁻¹. So the increasing order is glass, germanium, silver.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: A solid sample has resistivity 2 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m at room temperature. Its conductivity and its likely classification are:
explanation: sigma = 1 / ρ = 1 / (2 × 10⁻⁸) = 0.5 × 10⁸ = 5 × 10⁷ S m⁻¹. A resistivity of 2 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m lies squarely in the metallic band of 10⁻⁸ to 10⁻⁶ Ω m, so the sample is a conductor.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: A semiconductor slab of conductivity 2 S m⁻¹ and cross sectional area 5 × 10⁻⁶ m² is placed in a uniform electric field of 100 V m⁻¹ directed along its length. The current through the slab is:
explanation: J = sigma E = 2 × 100 = 200 A m⁻². Then I = J A = 200 × (5 × 10⁻⁶) = 1.0 × 10⁻³ A, that is 1 mA.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: The resistivity of a pure semiconductor sample is 4 Ω m. On heating, its carrier number density becomes 8 times larger while the carrier mobility falls to one half of its earlier value. The new resistivity is:
explanation: Conductivity is proportional to n mu. The product changes by a factor 8 × (1/2) = 4, so the conductivity becomes 4 times larger. Since ρ = 1 / sigma, the resistivity becomes 4 / 4 = 1 Ω m.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: On heating a semiconductor the mobility of its carriers actually decreases, and yet its conductivity increases. The correct resolution is that:

options.A: the fall in mobility applies only to holes, while the electron mobility rises steeply with temperature
options.B: the sample shortens on heating so its resistance falls even though the conductivity is unchanged
options.C: the carrier number density grows exponentially with temperature and easily dominates the modest fall in mobility
options.D: the electronic charge grows with temperature and compensates for the loss of mobility

correct_answer: the carrier number density grows exponentially with temperature and easily dominates the modest fall in mobility
explanation: Write sigma = e n (mu_e + mu_h) for a pure sample. Raising the temperature from 300 K to 400 K may multiply n by a factor of many hundreds, while mu falls only by a factor of about two or three. The product therefore rises strongly and so does the conductivity.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: A uniform bar of a solid has length 4 m, cross sectional area 2 × 10⁻⁶ m² and resistance 20 Ω. Its resistivity and the class to which it belongs are:
explanation: ρ = R A / l = 20 × (2 × 10⁻⁶) / 4 = (4 × 10⁻⁵) / 4 = 1 × 10⁻⁵ Ω m. This lies in the semiconductor range of about 10⁻⁵ to 10⁶ Ω m, so the bar is a semiconductor.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: In the free electron model of a metal, the valence electrons are best described as:

options.A: bound to their parent atoms and merely oscillating in place when a field is applied
options.B: completely at rest until a field is applied and then moving together with a very large uniform speed
options.C: detached from individual atoms, moving at random through the whole crystal and drifting slowly when a field is applied
options.D: travelling in fixed circular orbits around the lattice ions even when a field is applied

correct_answer: detached from individual atoms, moving at random through the whole crystal and drifting slowly when a field is applied
explanation: The valence electrons of a metal leave their atoms and behave like a gas filling the crystal. Their random speeds are very large, but the random velocities cancel so no current flows. An applied field superposes a very small common drift velocity on this random motion, and that drift constitutes the current.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: Two identical silicon diodes are joined in series with a 100 Ω resistor across a 3.4 V supply, both diodes being forward biased. The current in the circuit is:
explanation: Each silicon diode drops about 0.7 V, so the two together drop 1.4 V. The resistor therefore receives 3.4 - 1.4 = 2.0 V, giving I = 2.0 / 100 = 0.02 A = 20 mA. Both diodes and the resistor carry this same current since they form a single loop.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: In a good silicon diode the reverse saturation current is typically of the order of:
explanation: In reverse bias the majority carrier flow is stopped, and only the few minority carriers that reach the depletion layer are swept across. Since their number is very small, the resulting current is of the order of microampere in silicon, small enough for the diode to be treated as an open circuit in most calculations.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: When the reverse voltage across a junction diode is raised past its breakdown value, the reverse current:

options.A: reverses its direction and becomes a forward current
options.C: rises in direct proportion to the voltage, as in a resistor
options.D: rises very sharply while the voltage across the diode stays nearly constant

correct_answer: rises very sharply while the voltage across the diode stays nearly constant
explanation: Beyond the breakdown voltage, either the intense junction field frees bound electrons directly or accelerated carriers create fresh pairs by collision. Either way carriers are produced in large numbers and the reverse current climbs steeply, while the voltage across the diode remains close to the breakdown value. This constant voltage property is what a Zener diode exploits.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: A 12 V supply is to drive a silicon diode in series with a resistance R, with the current limited to 10 mA. The value of R should be:
explanation: The diode holds about 0.7 V, so the resistor must drop 12 - 0.7 = 11.3 V while carrying 10 mA. Hence R = 11.3 / (10 × 10⁻³) = 1130 Ω. In practice the nearest standard value above this would be chosen so that the current never exceeds the limit.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: A silicon diode carries a forward current of 7 mA when the voltage across it is 0.7 V. Its static resistance at this point is:
explanation: Converting the current, I = 7 mA = 7 × 10⁻³ A. Then R = 0.7 / (7 × 10⁻³) = 100 Ω. This is the ratio of the coordinates of one point on the characteristic and it changes from point to point because the curve is not a straight line through the origin.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: A silicon diode and a germanium diode are joined in series in the forward direction. Once both are conducting, the total voltage drop across the pair is about:
explanation: Both diodes carry the same current and their drops appear one after the other along the loop, so the drops add to give 0.7 + 0.3 = 1.0 V. This is the reason a series chain of diodes is sometimes used to obtain a roughly fixed voltage reference.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: The forward voltage of a diode changes from 0.70 V to 0.75 V while its current changes from 10 mA to 15 mA. The dynamic resistance of the diode is:
explanation: The change in voltage is 0.75 - 0.70 = 0.05 V and the change in current is 15 - 10 = 5 mA = 5 × 10⁻³ A. Hence r = 0.05 / (5 × 10⁻³) = 10 Ω. Note how much smaller this is than the static resistance at the same point, which shows how steeply the forward curve rises.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: The knee voltage, also called the cut in voltage, of a silicon junction diode is nearly:
explanation: Below the knee voltage the applied forward voltage is not enough to overcome the barrier, so the current stays very small. Once the applied voltage reaches about 0.7 V in silicon the barrier is largely cancelled and the current rises very steeply with any further increase in voltage.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: Diamond of gap 5.4 eV and silicon of gap 1.1 eV have the same crystal structure. At room temperature the ratio of their conduction electron populations is enormous. The best physical reason is that:

options.A: diamond has no valence electrons available for excitation while silicon has four per atom
options.B: the number excited across a gap falls off in direct proportion to the gap, so the ratio is close to five
options.C: the number of electrons excited across a gap falls off exponentially as the gap grows, and 5.4 eV is far beyond the thermal energy available at 300 K
options.D: diamond has far fewer atoms per unit volume than silicon and therefore fewer electrons in total

correct_answer: the number of electrons excited across a gap falls off exponentially as the gap grows, and 5.4 eV is far beyond the thermal energy available at 300 K
explanation: The fraction of electrons able to cross a gap is governed by an exponential factor in which the gap is compared with the thermal energy k T, about 0.026 eV at 300 K. Increasing the gap from 1.1 eV to 5.4 eV increases the exponent by a factor of about five, and since the dependence is exponential the population drops by many tens of powers of ten. Diamond is therefore an excellent insulator.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: A semiconductor has a forbidden gap of 2.48 eV. Using hc = 1240 eV nm, the longest wavelength of light that can lift an electron from the valence band to the conduction band is:
explanation: lambda_max = 1240 / 2.48 = 500 nm. A photon of wavelength longer than 500 nm carries less than 2.48 eV and cannot lift an electron across the gap, however intense the beam.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: In a divalent metal the valence band is completely filled, and yet the metal conducts extremely well. The reason is that:

options.A: the empty conduction band overlaps the filled valence band, so unoccupied states lie immediately above the filled ones
options.B: a completely filled band by itself can carry a current once a field is applied
options.C: the metal contains pentavalent impurities that donate electrons to its conduction band
options.D: the forbidden gap of such a metal is about 1 eV and is crossed easily at room temperature

correct_answer: the empty conduction band overlaps the filled valence band, so unoccupied states lie immediately above the filled ones
explanation: Counting electrons alone would suggest that a divalent metal has a full valence band and should be an insulator. In the real crystal the next band dips down and overlaps the valence band in energy, so electrons spill into it and both bands end up partly filled. Vacant states then lie immediately above occupied ones and conduction is easy.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: Light of wavelength 620 nm falls on separate samples of silicon of gap 1.1 eV and germanium of gap 0.7 eV. Taking hc = 1240 eV nm, the light:

options.A: carries 2 eV per photon and can create electron hole pairs in both samples
options.B: carries 0.5 eV per photon and can create pairs in neither sample
options.C: carries 2 eV per photon and can create pairs in silicon only
options.D: carries 2 eV per photon and can create pairs in germanium only

correct_answer: carries 2 eV per photon and can create electron hole pairs in both samples
explanation: E = 1240 / 620 = 2 eV per photon. Since 2 eV is greater than 1.1 eV and also greater than 0.7 eV, the photon can lift an electron across the gap in either material, so pairs are created in both samples.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: A slab of pure silicon of forbidden gap 1.1 eV is first kept in the dark and its resistance measured. It is then illuminated with light whose photons each carry 2 eV. The resistance of the slab:

options.A: rises, because the absorbed photons heat the lattice and hinder the motion of the carriers
options.B: falls, because photons of 2 eV exceed the gap and create extra electron hole pairs
options.C: stays unchanged, because light cannot alter the number of charge carriers inside a solid
options.D: falls, because photons of 2 eV knock electrons right out of the surface of the slab

correct_answer: falls, because photons of 2 eV exceed the gap and create extra electron hole pairs
explanation: Each photon carries 2 eV, which is more than the 1.1 eV gap, so it can be absorbed by a valence electron and lift it into the conduction band. Every such event adds one free electron and one hole. The carrier concentration therefore rises above the thermal value, the conductivity rises and the measured resistance falls.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: The energy required to break a covalent bond in germanium, compared with that in silicon, is:

options.D: the same for both, roughly 1.1 eV in each case

explanation: Breaking a covalent bond means lifting a valence electron across the forbidden gap into the conduction band, so the bond energy equals Eg. For germanium this is about 0.7 eV and for silicon about 1.1 eV, which is why germanium devices are more sensitive to temperature.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: The valence band of a solid is:

options.A: the band in which the electrons have escaped from the crystal altogether
options.B: the band of energies that stays completely empty at every temperature
options.C: the band of energies occupied by the valence electrons of the atoms of the solid
options.D: the range of energies that no electron in the solid may possess

correct_answer: the band of energies occupied by the valence electrons of the atoms of the solid
explanation: The valence electrons of the atoms occupy the valence band. In a pure semiconductor or insulator this band is completely full at 0 K. The next allowed band above it, separated by the forbidden gap, is the conduction band, which is empty at 0 K.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: At room temperature a germanium sample carries a larger intrinsic current than an identical silicon sample mainly because:

options.A: germanium has a smaller forbidden energy gap, so many more electron hole pairs are generated thermally
options.B: germanium is pentavalent while silicon is tetravalent
options.C: germanium has a larger forbidden energy gap, which pushes electrons across more easily
options.D: germanium has no forbidden energy gap at room temperature

correct_answer: germanium has a smaller forbidden energy gap, so many more electron hole pairs are generated thermally
explanation: The gap of germanium is about 0.7 eV and that of silicon about 1.1 eV. At the same temperature the smaller gap of germanium lets a far greater number of electrons be lifted into the conduction band, and each such electron leaves a hole behind. With more carriers of both kinds, germanium shows the larger intrinsic conductivity.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: A semiconductor has a forbidden energy gap of 1.24 eV. The minimum frequency of radiation that can create an electron hole pair in it is nearly (h = 6.6 × 10⁻³⁴ J s, 1 eV = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J):
explanation: First convert the gap: Eg = 1.24 × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 1.984 × 10⁻¹⁹ J. Then nu = Eg / h = 1.984 × 10⁻¹⁹ / 6.6 × 10⁻³⁴ = 3.0 × 10¹⁴ Hz. Radiation of lower frequency carries less energy per photon than the gap and cannot create a pair.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: Which statement about the forbidden energy gap of a crystalline solid is correct?

options.A: No electron of the solid can possess an energy that lies inside the gap
options.B: The forbidden gap is widest in conductors
options.C: Electrons drift freely inside the gap while carrying current
options.D: The holes of the crystal are stored inside the forbidden gap

correct_answer: No electron of the solid can possess an energy that lies inside the gap
explanation: The gap is defined as the energy interval between the top of the valence band and the bottom of the conduction band in which the crystal provides no allowed state. An electron may be in the valence band or in the conduction band but never at an energy inside the gap. Holes are vacancies in the valence band and conductors show no gap at all.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: The continuous range of energies formed by the levels of the valence electrons of the atoms of a solid is called:
explanation: When atoms come close in a crystal, the sharp energy levels of their valence electrons spread out into a continuous band. This band, which is completely filled at 0 K in a semiconductor, is the valence band. The next higher allowed band, empty at 0 K, is the conduction band, and the energy range between the two contains no allowed states and is the forbidden band.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: The longest wavelength of a photon that can just lift an electron across a forbidden gap of 2.48 eV is (take hc = 1240 eV nm):
explanation: Using λ = hc / Eg with hc = 1240 eV nm gives λ = 1240 / 2.48 = 500 nm. A photon of longer wavelength carries less than 2.48 eV and cannot lift an electron across the gap, so 500 nm is the longest usable wavelength.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: In a good conductor such as copper, the valence band and the conduction band:

options.A: are both completely empty at room temperature
options.B: overlap each other, so that there is no forbidden gap between them
options.C: are separated by a gap of about 1 eV
options.D: are separated by a gap of more than 5 eV

correct_answer: overlap each other, so that there is no forbidden gap between them
explanation: A metal has either a partly filled valence band or overlapping valence and conduction bands. Because empty allowed levels lie immediately above the occupied ones, even a small applied field accelerates electrons into those levels and a large current flows. There is no forbidden gap to be crossed.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII
syllabus_reference: NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus, Unit 19: Electronic Devices

subject: Physics
question: The forbidden energy gap of pure silicon at room temperature is nearly:
explanation: Silicon is the most widely used semiconductor and its forbidden energy gap at room temperature is about 1.1 eV. Germanium, the other common elemental semiconductor, has a smaller gap of about 0.7 eV, while insulators such as diamond have gaps of several electron volt.
source_document: Official NMC/NTA NEET-UG 2026 Physics syllabus; NCERT Physics, Class XII

subject: Physics
question: Which set contains only trivalent dopants?
explanation: Boron, aluminium, gallium and indium each have three valence electrons, so when one replaces a silicon atom one of the four bonds is left short of an electron. That incomplete bond is an acceptor site, and the material becomes p type.
